For a bridge rectifier with a capacitor filter operating under normal loaded conditions, the DC output voltage is approximately \(U_L \approx 1.2U_2\), because the capacitor charges to near the peak value during diode conduction and maintains the voltage between peaks, giving an average output higher than the unfiltered value of \(0.9U_2\). Substituting \(U_2 = 10\text{V}\) gives \(U_L \approx 1.2 \times 10\text{V} = 12\text{V}\). Final answer: \(12\text{V}\)

The figure plots collector current \(I_C\) versus collector-emitter voltage \(U_{CE}\) for several fixed base currents; at \(U_{CE}=6\text{V}\) all curves are flat, so \(I_C\) is essentially constant for each base current. The curve passing through \(I_C=2\text{mA}\) is labeled \(I_B=20\,\mu\text{A}\) (the label uses \(\mu\text{F}\), but the variable is base current and the value must be in microamperes). The current amplification factor is \(\beta = I_C/I_B\), giving \(\beta = 2\text{mA}/20\,\mu\text{A} = 2000\,\mu\text{A}/20\,\mu\text{A} = 100\). Final answer: 100.

The image shows a 555 timer with pins 8 and 4 connected to +Vcc, pin 1 grounded, pin 5 bypassed to ground through a 0.01µF capacitor, pin 7 (discharge) connected through a single resistor R to +Vcc, pin 6 (threshold) connected to pin 7, and pin 2 (trigger) connected to the junction of capacitor C and the input u1, with capacitor C connected to ground. This arrangement, in which one resistor R charges capacitor C from Vcc and an external trigger signal u1 is applied to pin 2 while pins 6 and 7 terminate the timing cycle, is the defining structure of a monostable multivibrator (one-shot), whose output pulse width is approximately T = 1.1RC. Final answer: monostable multivibrator.

The figure shows three two-input XOR gates, with the first computing A⊕B, the second computing C⊕D, and the third combining them to give Y = (A⊕B)⊕(C⊕D) = A⊕B⊕C⊕D. For Y = 1, the XOR of all four inputs must be 1, which occurs when an odd number of A, B, C, D are 1; equivalently, (A⊕B) must differ from (C⊕D), meaning either A≠B with C=D or A=B with C≠D. The valid ABCD combinations are therefore 0001, 0010, 0100, 1000, 0111, 1011, 1101, and 1110. Final answer: Y = 1 when ABCD has an odd number of 1s, specifically 0001, 0010, 0100, 1000, 0111, 1011, 1101, 1110.

The figure shows a single series loop containing a battery \(E\), a variable resistor \(R\), and a capacitor \(C\). In DC steady state, the capacitor is fully charged and behaves as an open circuit, so the loop current is \(I=0\). With zero current, the voltage drop across the resistor is \(V_R=IR=0\), and Kirchhoff’s voltage law gives the capacitor voltage as \(V_C=E\). Changing \(R\) only changes the time constant \(\tau=RC\) and the charging rate; it does not affect the final steady-state voltage across the capacitor. Therefore, if the circuit is already stable and \(R\) is increased, the voltage across the capacitor remains unchanged. Final answer: It remains unchanged (equal to \(E\)).

The circuit contains a 15 V source in series with a 10 Ω resistor connected to the base of a BJT, a 10 kΩ resistor in series with a 10.7 V source connected to the emitter, and a 1 kΩ resistor connected between the collector terminal a and ground terminal b. To find the Thevenin resistance, all independent DC sources are turned off (short-circuited), and the BJT is replaced by its small-signal model. In active mode the BJT behaves as a voltage-controlled current source \(g_m v_{be}\) in parallel with the base-emitter resistance \(r_\pi\). With the base tied to ground through 10 Ω and the emitter tied to ground through 10 kΩ, the small-signal base-emitter voltage \(v_{be}\) is forced to zero by the circuit topology, so the controlled current source is inactive. Consequently the only resistance seen between terminals a and b is the 1 kΩ resistor. Final answer: 1000.00 Ω.

The figure shows a straight conductor 1 m long, parallel to the z-axis, located at a radial distance of 1 m from the z-axis, and the problem states that the magnetic field is B = 1 T directed radially outward. For a conductor moving perpendicular to a magnetic field, the induced motional emf is e = B l v, where l is the conductor length and v is the tangential speed. Setting e = 1 V, B = 1 T, and l = 1 m gives v = e/(B l) = 1 m/s. Since the radius is r = 1 m, the angular speed is ω = v/r = 1 rad/s. Converting to revolutions per minute, N = ω × 60/(2π) = 60/(2π) ≈ 9.55 r.p.m. Final answer: 9.55 r.p.m.

The graph shows a real, odd pulse: for \(-T/2<t<0\), \(f(t)=t/T+1/2\), and for \(0<t<T/2\), \(f(t)=t/T-1/2\), with \(f(-T/2)=f(T/2)=0\) and a jump from \(+1/2\) to \(-1/2\) at \(t=0\); thus \(f(-t)=-f(t)\). Using the Fourier transform \(F(\omega)=\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(t)e^{-i\omega t}\,dt=\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(t)\cos(\omega t)\,dt-i\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(t)\sin(\omega t)\,dt\), the first integrand is odd\(\times\)even = odd, so its integral over the symmetric interval is zero, while the second integrand is odd\(\times\)odd = even, giving a real coefficient; therefore \(F(\omega)=-i\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(t)\sin(\omega t)\,dt\) is purely imaginary. Moreover, \(F(-\omega)=-i\int f(t)\sin(-\omega t)\,dt=i\int f(t)\sin(\omega t)\,dt=-F(\omega)\), so \(F(\omega)\) is an odd function of \(\omega\). Final answer: imaginary and odd.

The graph gives the electron mobility (solid line) in silicon at 300 K; at a doping concentration of \(10^{16}\,\text{cm}^{-3}\) the electron mobility is about \(1.1\times10^{3}\,\text{cm}^2\text{V}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}\), which equals \(0.11\,\text{m}^2\text{V}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}\). Since phosphorus is a donor, the electron concentration is approximately the doping concentration, \(n \approx 10^{16}\,\text{cm}^{-3}=10^{22}\,\text{m}^{-3}\). Using \(\sigma = q n \mu\), we get \(\sigma = (1.6\times10^{-19}\,\text{C})(10^{22}\,\text{m}^{-3})(0.11\,\text{m}^2\text{V}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}) \approx 176\,\text{S}\,\text{m}^{-1}\). Final answer: \(176\,\text{S}\,\text{m}^{-1}\) (approximately).

The figure shows a 555 timer IC configured as a monostable multivibrator: pins 8 and 4 are tied to Vcc, pin 1 is grounded, pin 5 is bypassed by a 0.01 µF capacitor to ground, resistor R is connected between Vcc and the common timing node, and capacitor C is connected from that node to ground, with the trigger input v1 applied to pin 2. In monostable operation, after a trigger pulse the internal discharge transistor turns off and C charges from near 0 V toward Vcc through R, while the output remains high until the capacitor voltage reaches the upper comparator threshold of (2/3)Vcc. The capacitor voltage during charging is v_C(t)=Vcc(1-e^{-t/RC}); setting v_C(t_w)=(2/3)Vcc gives (2/3)=1-e^{-t_w/RC}, so e^{-t_w/RC}=1/3 and t_w=RC ln(3)≈1.1 RC. Final answer: t_w=1.1RC (or RC ln 3).

Figure (a) is the reference sine wave \(e = E_m\sin(\omega t)\), which starts at zero, rises to a positive maximum at \(\omega t=\pi/2\), and falls to a negative maximum at \(\omega t=3\pi/2\); figure (d) has the same amplitude, frequency, and shape but is reflected across the time axis, so it represents \(e = -E_m\sin(\omega t)\), meaning its value at every instant is the negative of the value in (a). Two AC waveforms are inverses when one is the negative of the other, which corresponds to a \(180^\circ\) phase shift and makes their sum zero at every instant. Figures (b) and (c) are only phase-shifted versions of the sine wave and therefore are not inverse to (a). Final answer: (a) and (d).

The lower 2-to-1 multiplexer has data inputs \(C\) and \(\bar C\) with select line \(B\), so its output is \(C\) when \(B=0\) and \(\bar C\) when \(B=1\), which equals \(C\oplus B\). The upper 2-to-1 multiplexer takes that lower output at its data input \(0\), takes \(A\) at data input \(1\), and has its select input tied to the \(0\) shown at the top, so it always passes data input \(0\). Therefore \(f\) equals the lower multiplexer output, giving \(f = C\oplus B = \bar B C + B\bar C\). Final answer: \(f = C\oplus B\) (equivalently \(f = \bar B C + B\bar C\)).

The plot shows an initial asymptote of -40 dB/dec passing through 54 dB at ω=0.1 rad/s, so the transfer function contains a 1/s² factor; the slope changes by -20 dB/dec at ω=2 rad/s, +20 dB/dec at ω=5 rad/s, and -20 dB/dec at ω=25 rad/s, indicating poles at 2 and 25 rad/s and a zero at 5 rad/s. Therefore G(s) = K(1+s/5)/[s²(1+s/2)(1+s/25)], and using the low-frequency asymptote 54 = 20 log₁₀(K/0.1²) gives K ≈ 5. Final answer: G(s)=5(1+s/5)/[s²(1+s/2)(1+s/25)].

The circuit shows a 19 V supply with both NPN transistors’ collectors and the base of the top transistor tied to the positive rail, the top transistor having β = 85, the bottom transistor β = 30, and a 150 Ω resistor from the bottom emitter to ground. With two 0.7 V base-emitter drops in series, the voltage across the 150 Ω resistor is 19 V − 0.7 V − 0.7 V = 17.6 V, so the bottom transistor’s emitter current is I4 = I_E2 = 17.6 / 150 = 0.11733 A = 117.33 mA. For the bottom transistor, I_E2 = I_C2 + I_B2 and β2 = I_C2 / I_B2 = 30, giving I_C2 = [β2/(β2+1)] I_E2 = (30/31)(117.33 mA) = 113.55 mA. Since I2 is the collector current of the bottom transistor, I2 = 113.55 mA. Final answer: 113.55 mA.

In the circuit all resistors are 1 kΩ and the op-amp is ideal, so the virtual-short condition \(V_+ = V_-\) applies and no current enters the op-amp inputs. With the switch in position A, the non-inverting input is connected through a 1 kΩ resistor to the 1 V source and through another 1 kΩ resistor to ground, giving \(V_+ = 1\text{ V}/2 = 0.5\text{ V}\); hence \(V_- = 0.5\text{ V}\). KCL at the inverting node, which is connected to 5 V and \(V_0\) through 1 kΩ resistors, gives \((5-0.5)/1\text{k} + (V_{0A}-0.5)/1\text{k} = 0\), so \(V_{0A} = -4\text{ V}\). With the switch in position B, the non-inverting input is connected through a 1 kΩ resistor to node \(X\), and node \(X\) is connected through a 1 kΩ resistor to the inverting input; because \(V_+ = V_-\), both ends of this branch are at the same voltage, so no current flows in it, forcing \(V_+ = V_- = 0\text{ V}\). KCL at the inverting node then gives \((5-0)/1\text{k} + (V_{0B}-0)/1\text{k} = 0\), so \(V_{0B} = -5\text{ V}\). Therefore \(V_{0B}/V_{0A} = (-5)/(-4) = 5/4\). Final answer: 5/4

The figure shows a 1∠0 V source in parallel with a series R-L branch carrying I_RL = √2 ∠ -π/4 A and a capacitor branch carrying I_C. Converting I_RL to rectangular form gives I_RL = √2[cos(-π/4) + j sin(-π/4)] = 1 - j1 A, so the R-L branch draws 1 A in phase with the voltage and 1 A of lagging reactive current. In the usual power-factor-correction interpretation of this parallel arrangement, the capacitor supplies only reactive current and is sized to cancel that lagging component, so I_C is a purely leading current of magnitude 1 A, i.e. I_C = j1 A = 1∠90° A. (The “94A” text in the figure is not consistent with the stated phasor values.) Final answer: 190° A.

The circuit in figure (b) is a 555 timer wired as a Schmitt trigger: pins 2 (TRIG) and 6 (THRESH) are tied together and driven by the input, pin 4 and 8 are at \(V_{CC}=5\text{V}\), and pin 5 is bypassed by capacitor \(C_1\). The input in figure (a) is a triangular wave of amplitude \(\pm5\text{V}\) with a period of \(10\text{ms}\), so its slope magnitude is \((5-(-5))/(5\text{ms})=2\text{V/ms}\). For a 555 Schmitt trigger the upper threshold is \(V_{T+}=\frac{2}{3}V_{CC}=\frac{10}{3}\text{V}\) and the lower threshold is \(V_{T-}=\frac{1}{3}V_{CC}=\frac{5}{3}\text{V}\); the output is high from the falling crossing of \(V_{T-}\) until the rising crossing of \(V_{T+}\). The high-level interval therefore covers the input moving from \(+\frac{5}{3}\text{V}\) down to \(-5\text{V}\) and back up to \(+\frac{10}{3}\text{V}\), a total voltage change of \(\frac{5}{3}+5+5+\frac{10}{3}=15\text{V}\). At \(2\text{V/ms}\) this gives \(t_{\text{high}}=15/2=7.5\text{ms}\). Final answer: 7.5 ms.

The circuit has \(E_1=4\text{V}\), \(R_1=2\text{k}\Omega\), \(R_2=2\text{k}\Omega\), \(R_3=4\text{k}\Omega\), and \(E_2=3\text{V}\), with the diode ideal and \(U_{AB}\) taken across terminals A and B. With the diode disconnected, the voltage at the diode anode is determined by the \(R_1,R_2\) divider: \(V_{\text{anode}}=E_1\frac{R_2}{R_1+R_2}=4\text{V}\times\frac{2}{2+2}=2\text{V}\). The diode cathode is at node A, which is connected through \(R_3\) to \(E_2\). If the diode is off, no current flows through \(R_3\), so \(V_A=E_2=3\text{V}\). Since \(V_{\text{anode}}=2\text{V}<V_A=3\text{V}\), the diode is reverse-biased and indeed remains off. Therefore \(U_{AB}=V_A=3\text{V}\). Final answer: 3.

The figure shows the base region of an npn BJT with width \(0.5\,\mu\text{m}\) and a linear excess electron concentration that is \(10^{14}\,\text{cm}^{-3}\) at the emitter edge and zero at the collector edge, so the collector current is the electron diffusion current across the base. Using the Einstein relation \(D_n=\mu_n V_T=(800)(0.026)=20.8\,\text{cm}^2/\text{s}\), the magnitude is \(I_C = q A D_n \left|\frac{dn}{dx}\right| = (1.6\times10^{-19})(0.001)(20.8)\left(\frac{10^{14}}{0.5\times10^{-4}}\right)\,\text{A} = 6.656\times10^{-3}\,\text{A}\). Final answer: 6.66 mA.

The image shows an ideal operational amplifier (denoted by the ∞ symbol) with the input voltage \(u_i\) applied to its non-inverting (+) terminal, a resistor connected from the inverting (−) terminal to ground, and the output \(u_o\) fed back directly to the inverting (−) terminal. For an ideal op-amp with negative feedback, the virtual short principle gives \(u_+ = u_-\), so the inverting terminal voltage equals \(u_i\). Because the output is connected directly to the inverting terminal, \(u_o = u_-\), hence \(u_o = u_i\). Therefore, the voltage amplification factor is \(A_u = \dfrac{u_o}{u_i} = 1\). Final answer: 1.

The figure shows a 15 V unregulated input feeding the pass transistor Q1, whose output is divided by a 12 kΩ/24 kΩ resistor string and compared by an op-amp to a 6 V zener reference; the feedback holds the divider node at 6 V, so \(V_{\text{out}}\frac{24\text{k}}{12\text{k}+24\text{k}}=6\text{ V}\), giving \(V_{\text{out}}=9\text{ V}\). With a 10 Ω load, the load current is \(I_{\text{load}}=9\text{ V}/10\,\Omega=0.9\text{ A}\), and because regulation keeps \(V_{\text{out}}\) fixed, this current stays the same when the input changes. The voltage across Q1 is \(V_{\text{UR}}-V_{\text{out}}\), so the initial dissipation is \(P_1=(15\text{ V}-9\text{ V})(0.9\text{ A})=5.4\text{ W}\). After a 20 % increase, \(V_{\text{UR}}=18\text{ V}\), so \(P_2=(18\text{ V}-9\text{ V})(0.9\text{ A})=8.1\text{ W}\). The percentage change is \(\frac{8.1-5.4}{5.4}\times100\% = 50\%\). Final answer: 50 % increase.

In the figure, the 2×1 MUX has its output Y fed back to input 0, while input 1 is driven by Y through an inverter; with S = 1, the MUX selects input 1, so the effective relation is Y = NOT Y delayed by the MUX propagation delay. Since the MUX propagation delay is 10 ns and the inverter delay is 0 ns, the loop behaves like a single inverter with a 10 ns delay, causing Y to toggle every 10 ns. The period of oscillation is therefore 2 × 10 ns = 20 ns, and the frequency is 1 / 20 ns = 50 MHz. Final answer: Y is a square wave that toggles every 10 ns, with a period of 20 ns and a frequency of 50 MHz.

The figure shows a first-stage autotransformer T1 with total winding ab and sliding tap P at its midpoint, and a second-stage ideal transformer T2 whose primary is connected across the P–b section while its secondary c–d supplies the load R. Since P is at the midpoint, the voltage across P–b is one-half the input voltage across a–b; for an ideal autotransformer, power conservation gives V_in I_in = V_Pb I_T2primary, so with V_Pb = V_in/2 the current entering the T2 primary is I_T2primary = 2 I_in. For the ideal second-stage transformer, the current ratio satisfies I_R / I_T2primary = N1/N2. Given that the load current is I_R = 10 I_in, substitution gives N1/N2 = (10 I_in)/(2 I_in) = 5. Final answer: 5:1 (primary turns : secondary turns).

The magnitude plot shows the gain is flat at 20 dB at low frequencies, drops to a flat −40 dB over a mid-frequency band, and then returns to 20 dB at high frequencies, indicating equal low- and high-frequency gain with attenuation in a middle band. This frequency response is characteristic of a notch or band-reject filter, whose transfer function has the form \(G(s)=K\frac{s^2+2\zeta_z\omega_0 s+\omega_0^2}{s^2+2\zeta_p\omega_0 s+\omega_0^2}\) with \(\zeta_z > \zeta_p\), producing a dip near \(\omega_0\). Final answer: notch compensator (or band-reject/notch filter).

The image shows an inverting operational amplifier configuration with the non-inverting input grounded, a 10 kΩ resistor connecting the input signal source to the inverting input, and a 30 kΩ feedback resistor connecting the output back to the inverting input. For an ideal op-amp in this configuration, the inverting input is at virtual ground (0 V) because negative feedback forces the inverting terminal voltage to equal the non-inverting terminal voltage. The input resistance \(R_i\) seen by the source is therefore determined by the current flowing through the input resistor: \(i_{in} = \frac{v_s - 0}{10\ \text{k}\Omega} = \frac{v_s}{10\ \text{k}\Omega}\), so \(R_i = \frac{v_s}{i_{in}} = 10\ \text{k}\Omega\). Final answer: 10 kΩ.

The C-core is 4 cm deep, and the 6 cm total height minus the 4 cm inner notch height gives a back/leg thickness of 2 cm; assuming a uniform cross-section, the flux-carrying area is \(A=(2\ \text{cm})(4\ \text{cm})=8\ \text{cm}^2=8\times10^{-4}\ \text{m}^2\). With the core permeability very high, the magnetic reluctance is dominated by the 1 mm nonmagnetic spacer, so \(L\approx N^2\mu_0 A/g\). Using \(N=100\), \(\mu_0=1/800{,}000\ \text{H/m}\), and \(g=1\times10^{-3}\ \text{m}\) gives \(L=(100)^2(1/800{,}000)(8\times10^{-4})/(1\times10^{-3})\ \text{H}=0.010\ \text{H}=10.0\ \text{mH}\). Final answer: 10.0

The circuit contains a 12 V source, \(R_1=R_2=R_4=R_5=1\,\Omega\), a 16 A current source directed upward into node \(b\), and the unknown resistor \(R_3\). Since \(I_5=0\), there is no voltage drop across \(R_5\), so \(V_a=V_b\). Applying KCL at node \(a\): \((12-V_a)/1=V_a/1\), which gives \(V_a=6\,\text{V}\) and therefore \(V_b=6\,\text{V}\). At node \(b\), the 16 A entering equals the sum of the currents leaving through \(R_3\) and \(R_4\): \(16=V_b/R_3+V_b/1=6/R_3+6\). Solving, \(6/R_3=10\), so \(R_3=0.6\,\Omega\). Final answer: \(0.6\,\Omega\).

The figure shows an ideal comparator with the sinusoidal input applied to the non-inverting (+) terminal and a 2 V reference, \(V_{\text{ref}}\), applied to the inverting (−) terminal, so the output is high whenever the input voltage is greater than 2 V. An 8 V peak-to-peak sinusoid with no DC component has amplitude \(A = 8/2 = 4\) V, so the input can be written as \(v(t) = 4\sin(\omega t)\). The output is high when \(4\sin(\omega t) > 2\), or \(\sin(\omega t) > 0.5\). Solving \(\sin\theta = 0.5\) gives \(\theta = \pi/6\) and \(\theta = 5\pi/6\), so the output is high over an angular interval of \(5\pi/6 - \pi/6 = 2\pi/3\) out of a full period \(2\pi\). Therefore the duty cycle is \((2\pi/3)/(2\pi) = 1/3\). Final answer: 1/3 (approximately 33.3%).

The circuit shows a 5 Ω resistor in series with a capacitor \(-jX_C\), with the voltage across this series branch labeled \(\dot U_1\), and a parallel combination of a 10 Ω resistor and a \(j10\ \Omega\) inductor whose voltage is \(\dot U_2\). Because the 10 Ω and \(j10\ \Omega\) elements are in parallel, the current through the series branch is \(\dot I=\dot U_2(1/10+1/(j10))=\dot U_2(0.1-j0.1)\). The voltage across the series branch is therefore \(\dot U_1=\dot I(5-jX_C)=\dot U_2(0.1-j0.1)(5-jX_C)=0.1\dot U_2[(5-X_C)-j(5+X_C)]\). For \(\dot U_1\) to lag \(\dot U_2\) by \(90^\circ\), the ratio \(\dot U_1/\dot U_2\) must be purely negative imaginary, so its real part must be zero: \(5-X_C=0\), giving \(X_C=5\ \Omega\); substituting \(X_C=5\ \Omega\) yields \(\dot U_1/\dot U_2=-j\), confirming the \(90^\circ\) lag. Final answer: \(5\ \Omega\).

The image shows a p-MOSFET with its source at 5 V and gate fixed at 3 V, so its source-gate voltage is \(V_{SG}=5\text{ V}-3\text{ V}=2\text{ V}\), and an n-MOSFET with its source grounded and gate at \(V_G\), so \(V_{GS}=V_G\); both drains are connected to the output \(V_0\). With a threshold magnitude of 1 V, the n-MOSFET overdrive at \(V_G=1.5\text{ V}\) is \(V_{GS}-V_{tn}=1.5-1=0.5\text{ V}\), giving a saturation current \(I_{Dn}=\frac{1}{2}(1\text{ mA/V}^2)(0.5\text{ V})^2=0.125\text{ mA}\). The p-MOSFET overdrive is \(V_{SG}-|V_{tp}|=2-1=1\text{ V}\), so it is stronger and pulls \(V_0\) high into the triode region while the n-MOSFET remains saturated; equating currents with the p-MOSFET triode current \(I_{Dp}=1[(1)(5-V_0)-\frac{1}{2}(5-V_0)^2]\) mA to \(0.125\) mA gives \((5-V_0)-\frac{1}{2}(5-V_0)^2=0.125\). Solving yields the triode solution \(5-V_0\approx0.134\text{ V}\), hence \(V_0\approx4.866\text{ V}\). Final answer: approximately 4.87 V.

The circuit has a top node (call it A) and a bottom reference node. From the figure, the branches connected to node A are: a 2 A current source directed upward in series with the 3 Ω and left-hand 4 Ω resistors; a 4 Ω resistor (with I1 defined downward) in series with a 12 V source Us whose positive terminal is at the top; a 12 Ω resistor in series with a 12 V source whose positive terminal is at the bottom; a 6 Ω resistor in series with a 24 V source whose positive terminal is at the top; and a 4 A current source directed downward. Because a current source fixes its branch current, the 3 Ω and left-hand 4 Ω resistors do not affect I1. Let V be the voltage of node A with respect to the bottom node. The currents leaving node A through the resistor branches are I1 = (V − 12)/4, I2 = (V + 12)/12, and I3 = (V − 24)/6, where the source polarities give the resistor-bottom voltages 12 V, −12 V, and 24 V respectively. Kirchhoff’s current law at node A gives −2 + 4 + I1 + I2 + I3 = 0, so (V − 12)/4 + (V + 12)/12 + (V − 24)/6 = −2. Multiplying by 12 yields 3(V − 12) + (V + 12) + 2(V − 24) = −24, which simplifies to 6V − 72 = −24 and V = 8 V. Therefore I1 = (8 − 12)/4 = −1 A, meaning the actual current is opposite to the drawn arrow. Final answer: −1 A

The figure shows a horizontal parallel-plate capacitor with the upper plate carrying charge \(-Q\) and the lower plate \(+Q\); the left half of the gap is filled with a dielectric and the right half with air, and the positive particle of mass \(m\) and charge \(+q\) is in the air region. Because the conducting plates are equipotential, the uniform electric field magnitude \(E\) is the same in both halves before the dielectric is removed. Let the dielectric have relative permittivity \(\kappa>1\) and the plate area be \(A\); then the free charge densities satisfy \(\sigma_{\text{air}}=\varepsilon_0 E\) and \(\sigma_{\text{dielectric}}=\kappa\varepsilon_0 E\), so the total charge is \(Q=(A/2)(\sigma_{\text{air}}+\sigma_{\text{dielectric}})=(A\varepsilon_0 E/2)(1+\kappa)\), giving \(E=2Q/[A\varepsilon_0(1+\kappa)]\). After removing the dielectric the same charge spreads uniformly over the whole plate, producing field \(E'=Q/(A\varepsilon_0)\). Since \(\kappa>1\), \(E'/E=(1+\kappa)/2>1\), so the field in the air region increases. The field points upward from the positive lower plate to the negative upper plate, so the electric force on \(+q\) is upward and initially balanced gravity; after removal \(qE'>mg\), giving a net upward force. Final answer: The particle moves upward (toward the negatively charged upper plate).

The image shows a symmetrical JFET with two p+ gate regions above and below an n-type channel, with source and drain at the two ends and both gates connected to the same gate voltage V_G = -2 V. For a JFET the saturation drain current can be written as I_D = I_DSS f(V_G/V_P), where the pinch-off voltage V_P depends only on the channel half-height and doping concentration and is independent of the channel width W, while I_DSS is proportional to W. The mutual transconductance is g_m = dI_D/dV_G = (I_DSS/|V_P|) times a function of V_G/V_P; because V_G and V_P are unchanged, g_m is proportional to I_DSS and therefore to W. Doubling W thus doubles g_m, so the transconductance ratio of the initial JFET to the modified JFET is W : 2W = 1 : 2. Final answer: 1:2

In a radial network, Kirchhoff’s current law fixes the branch power flows: the line segment from the source to node 1 must carry the total load S̃1 + S̃2, and the segment from node 1 to node 2 must carry S̃2, because there is only one path from the source to each load. The diagram shows R(s) entering a 1/s block, whose output is added to R(s) at the first summer; that sum then passes through a second 1/s block, and the output of that second integrator is added to R(s) at the second summer to produce C(s). Let the output of the first integrator be R(s)/s. The first summer output is R(s)/s + R(s), so the second integrator output is [R(s)/s + R(s)]/s = R(s)/s^2 + R(s)/s. The image shows the first two rows of a Routh table: the \(s^3\) row contains \(1\) and \((2K+3)\), and the \(s^2\) row contains \(2K\) and \(4\), so the corresponding characteristic equation is \(s^3 + 2K s^2 + (2K+3)s + 4 = 0\). For stability, every entry in the first column of the Routh table must be positive. The \(s^1\) row first entry is computed as \(\frac{2K(2K+3) - 1 \cdot 4}{2K} = \frac{2K^2 + 3K - 2}{K}\). The first-column conditions are \(2K > 0\) and \(\frac{2K^2 + 3K - 2}{K} > 0\). From \(2K > 0\) we get \(K > 0\), which means the numerator must also be positive: \(2K^2 + 3K - 2 = (2K-1)(K+2) > 0\), giving \(K > \frac{1}{2}\) (since \(K > 0\) rules out \(K < -2\)). Final answer: \(K > \frac{1}{2}\).

The image shows a filter whose magnitude-squared response \(|H(f)|^2\) is a triangle centered at \(f=0\), reaching a maximum value of \(1\) at \(f=0\) and falling linearly to zero at \(f = \pm 10\,\text{kHz}\). Since \(S_X(f)\) is constant, this becomes \(P_Y = S_X \times \text{area under }|H(f)|^2\). The area of the triangle is \(\frac{1}{2}\times \text{base}\times \text{height}=\frac{1}{2}\times 20\,000\,\text{Hz}\times 1 = 10\,000\,\text{Hz}\). Therefore, \(P_Y = (1\times 10^{-10}\,\text{W/Hz})(10\,000\,\text{Hz}) = 1\times 10^{-6}\,\text{W}\). Final answer: \(1\times 10^{-6}\,\text{W}\) (or \(1\,\mu\text{W}\)).

Because Jia is in the Southern Hemisphere, January is summer and July is winter; the graph shows that winter (July) rainfall alone accounts for the great majority of the annual total, while summer is very dry. Southern Anhui Province has a subtropical monsoon climate with rainfall concentrated in summer. Therefore, compared with southern Anhui, Jia’s precipitation is concentrated in winter rather than summer and is extremely unevenly distributed across the seasons. Final answer: Precipitation in Jia is concentrated in winter (July) and is very unevenly distributed seasonally, opposite to the summer concentration seen in southern Anhui.

The diagram depicts the China-Russia crude oil pipeline running from Russian oilfields near Skovorodino through Mohe to Daqing in China, providing a direct overland route for crude oil imports from Russia to China. The commissioning of this pipeline diversifies China's oil import sources and reduces reliance on seaborne crude shipments, especially those originating in the Middle East that must pass through strategic chokepoints; therefore, asserting that China's dependence on oil imports from the Middle East has increased is contrary to the pipeline's actual significance. Final answer: the Middle East

The two grayscale satellite images show the same deltaic region—likely Myanmar’s Irrawaddy Delta—before and during/after a flood or cyclone, with the right image displaying extensive white areas indicating inundation or heavy cloud cover; such imagery is captured by remote sensing, but calculating the affected area, assessing losses, and planning reconstruction require spatial data management and analysis. This is the function of a Geographic Information System (GIS), which can overlay disaster-extent layers with population, infrastructure, land-use, and administrative-boundary data, perform area calculations and spatial analyses, and support decision-making for resource allocation and reconstruction. Final answer: GIS (Geographic Information System).

The profile shows a north–south cross-section from the Yanshan Mountains, through Beijing, to the Yongding River; Beijing sits on a low, flat plain, with relatively flat terrain continuing southward. As urbanization advances, built-up areas expand outward from the city onto the flat suburban plains, where the land is easiest and most valuable to develop. Among agricultural land uses, cultivated land (arable land/farmland) is the type most commonly found on these flat suburban plains and is therefore the most likely to be converted into urban construction land, causing its proportion among agricultural land in Beijing’s suburbs to decrease. Final answer: cultivated land (arable land/farmland).

The image is a line graph showing the percentage change in area for six land-use categories—cultivated land, forest land, grassland, construction land, water area, and unused land—between two time points, separately for urban (solid line) and suburban (dashed line) areas, so the problem requires measuring how the extent of each land-use type has changed over roughly ten years. To estimate such temporal land-use change, repeated observations of the Earth’s surface are needed; remote sensing (RS) acquires multi-temporal satellite or aerial images that reveal how land-cover categories expand or shrink, and the resulting classifications can be analyzed with a geographic information system (GIS) to compute change rates. Among the core geographic information technologies, RS is the primary tool for detecting these land-use changes over time. Final answer: Remote sensing (RS).

In the left figure, AB is the terminator; because the local time at its intersection with the 40° latitude line is 7:00, AB is the morning line, giving a day length of 2×(12−7)=10 h at 40° and indicating the region is in its winter season. The contour lines form a V pointing upstream toward the east, so the river flows westward. The right figure is the Jia cross-section oriented with south on the left and north on the right; sediment is deposited on the south bank while the north bank is eroded. For westward flow, the north bank is the right bank when facing downstream, and the Coriolis force in the Northern Hemisphere deflects water toward the right bank, causing erosion there and deposition on the left bank, which matches the observed pattern. Final answer: Northern Hemisphere.

The schematic links local coal to thermal power, coal coking, and coal chemical production; it links seawater desalination to chlor-alkali chemicals; and it routes imported iron ore through steel smelting into slag processing and cement building materials, showing that one industry’s output or waste becomes another’s input. In industrial geography, such agglomeration creates a circular economy by letting firms share infrastructure, shorten transport distances, and reuse by-products and waste as raw materials. Because the diagram explicitly turns steel slag into cement and uses coal for multiple downstream products, the clustered industries can achieve comprehensive resource utilization and waste recycling, which also lowers production costs and reduces pollution. Final answer: comprehensive utilization of resources (waste recycling/material and energy reuse), reducing production costs and environmental pollution.

The map shows a shaded urban area, noise-level contours of 55–85 PNdB centered on M, and a transport-direction arrow indicating that M is a noise-generating transport facility (airport); the four black dots 甲, 乙, 丙, and 丁 are candidate suburban relocation sites. A suitable new site should be far enough from the city to keep high noise levels away from residents, should avoid being upwind of the city so that noise and pollutants are not carried toward the urban area, and should still have transport access. On the North China Plain the prevailing winter wind is from the northwest, so 甲, located northwest of the city, would send noise and pollutants toward the city; 乙 is too close to the western edge of the city and within its likely expansion zone; 丁 is southeast of the city and still too near the existing M and built-up area, so noise would still affect residents. 丙 is the farthest from the urban area on the south side, lies downwind of the prevailing northwest wind, and is connected to the transport network, making it the most reasonable relocation site. Final answer: 丙.

The bar chart shows that the eastern part of the country has the larger shares of freshwater and land area, while the western part has the larger shares of population and technological strength. This pattern corresponds to Russia, where natural resources and freshwater are concentrated in the eastern Siberian and Far East regions, but the population is concentrated in the western European part. The main human factor is the concentration of economic development, industry, cities, and infrastructure in the west, which has attracted and supported a much larger population despite the east’s greater natural resource endowment. Final answer: economic development (industrialization and urbanization) concentrated in the west.

The diagram shows four population-growth types, each with bars for birth rate, death rate, and natural growth rate; natural growth rate equals birth rate minus death rate. Type ④ has the shortest bars, meaning a low birth rate, a low death rate, and a very low natural growth rate. China’s current population growth is of the modern type—low birth rate, low death rate, and low natural increase—which matches the pattern shown in type ④. Final answer: ④.

The figure shows the upper Yellow River valley in Gansu and Ningxia, with industrial centers such as Lanzhou, Baiyin, Qingtongxia, and Yinchuan aligned along the river, and it marks abundant non-ferrous metal deposits including lead-zinc, copper, and nickel, plus several hydropower stations. Because the corridor’s development is based on these mineral resources and the cheap hydroelectric energy provided by the Yellow River, it has become a major center for non-ferrous metal smelting and related heavy industry. Final answer: a non-ferrous metal industrial base (non-ferrous metal industrial region).

At time 2 in the diagram the natural population growth rate reaches its highest point, indicating a stage of very rapid natural increase with high birth rates and falling death rates. This pattern is characteristic of the early-expanding phase of the demographic transition, which is currently seen in many developing countries, especially in Africa. Among typical examples, Nigeria presently exhibits such high natural growth. Final answer: Nigeria.

The map shows City B in southwestern China near 102°E, along a railway line, with a legend that includes coal, oil, bauxite, and iron-ore deposits. City B’s location corresponds to Panzhihua, a city that developed as an industrial center after large local iron-ore deposits were exploited, supported by the railway network. Final answer: iron ore.

The map shows Zhongshan Station near 76°E, while Beijing time is based on 120°E. Seeing the sun on the horizon on the west side of the Amery Ice Shelf and then again on the east side two hours later means the sun set in the west and rose in the east with a night lasting about two hours; the midpoint of this short night is local midnight (00:00 local solar time), so the second sighting occurs one hour after midnight, at about 01:00 local time. The longitude difference is 120°E − 76°E = 44°, giving a time difference of 44° × 4 min/° = 176 min ≈ 2 h 56 min. Adding this to 01:00 gives 03:56, which rounds to about 4:00 a.m. Final answer: about 4:00 a.m. Beijing time.

The map shows southern Africa, with the shaded areas concentrated in the Western Cape and adjacent interior/southern coastal regions of South Africa, where the climate is Mediterranean (winter rainfall). In South African agricultural geography, this zone is the country’s principal wheat-producing area, since the winter-rainfall Mediterranean climate and corresponding soils are suited to wheat cultivation. Therefore, the shaded region represents the wheat region. Final answer: wheat region (wheat-producing region)

The image depicts the Lewis turning point as the intersection where an economy shifts from an unlimited labor supply stage to a labor shortage stage, with aggregate demand shifting rightward during industrialization and wages beginning to rise along the AS curve. When this turning point arrives, the surplus rural labor that previously kept wages low becomes exhausted, causing labor shortages and upward pressure on wages. The question notes that “difficulty recruiting workers” has appeared in coastal areas and major labor-exporting provinces, which are regions heavily dependent on large workforces in factories. Therefore, the industrial sector most affected is the one that relies most heavily on abundant low-cost labor. Final answer: labor-intensive industries (especially manufacturing).

The figure is a polar projection of Earth with the pole at the center, the inner dashed circle as the polar circle, and the outer circle as the equator; the left radial line is labeled 180°, so the right radial line is 0° and, for a North Pole view, longitudes increase counterclockwise so east is counterclockwise. Because London (UTC) is still Saturday while Beijing (UTC+8) is already Sunday, the UTC time must be between 16:00 and 24:00 Saturday; the midnight meridian, which marks the center of the night hemisphere, is therefore between 0° and 120°E, placing the night hemisphere in the Eastern Hemisphere. Since the terminator is tangent to the polar circle at P and the poleward side of the terminator is the night side, the projection is centered on the North Pole in polar night. Moving from P toward A goes away from the pole, hence south, and moving from the 180° meridian at P to the top meridian at A is clockwise, which is west in a North Pole view; therefore A lies to the southwest of P. Final answer: southwest.

The bar chart shows, for corn, wheat, and soybean, that the photosynthetic production potential (white bar) is by far the highest level, reaching about 50,000 kg/100 m² for corn and roughly 40,000–45,000 kg/100 m² for wheat and soybean, while each subsequent potential—light-temperature, climate, climate-soil, and actual yield—is progressively lower, with actual yield only a small fraction of the photosynthetic potential; because the largest potential resource is at the photosynthetic level and the later stages mainly represent constraints that reduce yield, the most important advantageous condition is the abundant solar radiation or light resource. Final answer: Abundant light (strong solar radiation)/high photosynthetic production potential.

The profile runs from Lhasa to Xining and shows elevations mostly above 4000 m, with several peaks rising toward or above 5000–6000 m and deep valleys carved by the Nu, Lancang, Yangtze, and Yellow Rivers. Such a high, rolling terrain with alternating mountain ridges and river valleys is characteristic of the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau, where the land surface is elevated and strongly undulating rather than flat. Final answer: The area is generally high in elevation (mostly above 4000 m) and has a rugged, undulating surface with alternating mountains and deep river valleys.

The contour map shows a west-to-east descent from a hilltop at A, which lies above the 100 m contour, to low ground at B beside the perennial water body; along A–B the terrain can be divided into four elevation belts. In subtropical coastal China the appropriate vertical agricultural pattern places forest on the highest steep slopes, economic forest or orchard on the middle slopes, crop farming on the lower gentle land, and aquaculture on the lowest belt adjacent to water. Therefore the fourth section from A to B, being the lowest belt next to the perennial water, should be used for aquaculture. Final answer: 水产养殖业.

The map shows Dongting Lake connected to the Yangtze River (Changjiang) near Yueyang and Chenglingji, and the Yangtze ultimately flows to the East China Sea; because the Dongting Lake basin drains into the Yangtze and then to the ocean, its water takes part in land–sea exchange rather than a closed inland cycle. In water-cycle classification, a basin that discharges to the ocean participates in the ocean-land water cycle (large cycle). Final answer: 海陆间循环 (ocean-land water cycle / large cycle).
表中j位于“暖温带”行与“半湿润区”列的交叉处，因此j代表暖温带半湿润气候；在我国，这种气候主要分布在华北地区，尤其是华北平原。Final answer: 华北地区（华北平原）。

The image shows the Yichang–Wanzhou railway linking Yichang, Enshi, and Wanzhou, crossing the river valley and connecting existing river and road routes. Opening this railway fills a long-standing rail gap between Hubei and the Chongqing/Sichuan region, increases the density of the regional transport network, creates a faster east–west railway corridor, and strengthens intermodal links with the Yangtze River waterway and highways; as a result, it improves accessibility for the mountainous areas along the route, raises passenger and freight capacity, shortens travel time and cost, and promotes an integrated, multimodal transportation system. Final answer: It fills the rail gap between Hubei and the Chongqing/Sichuan region, increases network density, forms a fast east–west corridor, strengthens railway–waterway–highway intermodal connections, and improves accessibility and transport capacity for the mountainous areas along the line.

The profile is near 40°N and runs west–east from about 100°E to 120°E, with the ocean on the right (east) side; the arrows in the figure point horizontally from left to right, that is, from west toward east. In meteorology wind direction is named by the direction the air comes from, and at about 40°N the prevailing mid-latitude winds are the westerlies. Because the arrows show air moving toward the east, the wind must be coming from the west, so its direction is a west wind. Final answer: west wind (westerly).

Image 1 shows dust plume 甲 (A) originating over North Africa/Sahara and being carried westward across the tropical/subtropical North Atlantic toward the Caribbean and Central America, while plume 乙 (B) lies farther south near the equatorial Atlantic. Saharan dust is transported westward by the northeast trade winds and the Saharan Air Layer; this Caribbean-reaching path is strongest in the Northern Hemisphere summer, when intense heating over the Sahara, a strong African easterly jet, and a northward-shifted ITCZ favor westward transport. In winter the dust plume shifts southward, matching pattern 乙. Therefore pattern 甲 corresponds to summer. Final answer: summer (about July).

The map titled "中国物流企业的总部分布格局" uses graduated circles to show the number of logistics enterprise headquarters in each city, with larger circles representing higher concentrations. The largest circles, corresponding to 81–120 and 41–80 headquarters, are located in major cities along China’s eastern coast, particularly in the Beijing–Tianjin region, the Yangtze River Delta around Shanghai, and the Pearl River Delta around Guangzhou and Shenzhen, while inland and western cities generally have far fewer. This pattern indicates that headquarters are mainly concentrated in large coastal cities and major regional centers in eastern China. Final answer: The headquarters of Chinese logistics enterprises are mainly concentrated in large coastal cities in eastern China, especially in the Beijing–Tianjin area, the Yangtze River Delta, and the Pearl River Delta.

The profile runs near 40°N from about 100°E to 120°E, with region C (丙) located between 100°E and 110°E, east of region B and west of region D. At this latitude and longitude, region C corresponds to the Loess Plateau, a thick loess-covered highland. Because loess is loose, fine-grained, and highly erodible, surface runoff from rainfall carves numerous gullies and ravines into the plateau, producing a dissected, fragmented landscape. Therefore, the typical surface form of the landform in region C is deeply gullied and broken, described as “thousands of gullies and ravines” (千沟万壑). Final answer: deeply gullied and fragmented, with thousands of gullies and ravines (a dissected loess plateau).

The bar chart compares the relative values of moisture, heat, and light for four Chinese regions labeled 甲, 乙, 丙, and 丁. For 丁, the moisture and light bars are relatively high (about 3), while the heat bar is distinctly lower (about 2). In Chinese regional climate, the Northeast Plain has a temperate monsoon climate with moderate precipitation, abundant sunshine, and relatively low accumulated heat due to its high latitude; this profile matches 丁. In contrast, 甲 fits the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau (high light, low heat and moisture), 乙 fits the Sichuan Basin (high moisture and heat but low light), and 丙 fits the middle–lower Yangtze Plain (high moisture, heat, and light). Final answer: 东北平原.

The profile runs about 200 km from north (left) to south (right); elevation stays mostly below about 1500 m, and the January mean-temperature curve remains above 0 °C (about 5–25 °C), with cooler temperatures over the northern ridges and a pronounced warm area on the southern side; the arrow marks a January prevailing wind from the north/northwest toward the south. Since all January temperatures are above freezing, the range must be in southern China; the modest summit height (~1500 m) rules out the high Tibetan/Himalayan ranges, and the strong warming on the leeward southern slope matches an east–west barrier that blocks the cold winter monsoon. Among China’s major ranges, the Nanling Mountains fit these traits: they trend east–west, reach about 1500 m, and shelter southern Guangdong from the cold north winds, giving a warmer southern side. Final answer: the Nanling Mountains (南岭).

The diagram places “工业” (industry) at the center and connects it to eight location factors labeled a–h: a 原料 (raw materials), b 劳力 (labor), c 市场 (market), d 动力 (power), e 技术 (technology), f 交通 (transportation), g 资金 (capital), and h 政策 (policy). Fast-food chains such as McDonald’s and KFC are retail/service businesses whose success depends mainly on being close to a large customer base, so their dominant location factor is the market. Therefore, the letter corresponding to the market factor is c. Final answer: c.

The map marks “沿江承接产业转移示范区” in inland areas such as Chongqing/Yubei, Hubei Jingzhou, and Anhui Wanjiang, showing that industry is moving from coastal regions to the Yangtze River inland, which creates non-farm jobs near workers’ hometowns and encourages migrant workers to return for local employment. Therefore, the claim that migrant workers return home to carry out agriculture is inconsistent with the industrial-transfer context shown. Final answer: 务农

The two graphs plot production (solid line) and consumption (dashed line) across three product-life-cycle stages—new product, mature product, and standardized product—for Place A and Place B. In Place A, production exceeds consumption during the mature and standardized stages, indicating an export surplus; in Place B, consumption exceeds production during the new and mature stages, indicating imports, but production later overtakes consumption in the standardized stage, turning Place B into an exporter. This pattern matches the product-life-cycle model in which manufacturing initially occurs in a developed region and then relocates to a developing region once the product becomes standardized and cost, especially labor cost, becomes the main competitive factor. Therefore, the enterprise is best characterized as a labor-intensive manufacturing or processing enterprise. Final answer: labor-intensive manufacturing/processing enterprises (e.g., electronics assembly, apparel, or similar standardized-product industries).

The figure is a latitude–longitude plot in which point A (甲) lies near 40°N, 70°W (North America/United States), point B (乙) near 70°N, 0°–10°E (Europe), point C (丙) near 30°N, 120°E (East Asia/China’s coast), and point D (丁) near 30°N, 90°E (China/inland China), with the lines indicating automobile-industry relocation from A, B, and C toward D. Industrial transfer is driven mainly by the search for lower production costs and larger markets: automobile assembly is labor- and market-oriented, so firms move to locations with cheaper labor/land and strong consumer demand. D is in China, which offers abundant, low-cost labor, lower land costs, and a huge market compared with the higher-cost origin regions. Final answer: The main reason is that D (China) has abundant cheap labor, lower production costs, and a large market.

Figure A places point P in a continental coastal zone near 30°–36° latitude, and Figure B shows a summer-wet precipitation pattern with a July peak of about 120 mm and most rainfall concentrated from May to September, which identifies P as having a subtropical monsoon climate. A subtropical monsoon climate is characterized by hot summers around 25 °C and cool winters with monthly mean temperatures staying above 0 °C. In Figure C, curve ③ displays exactly this pattern—a summer peak near 25 °C and a winter minimum above 0 °C—whereas curve ① is too warm in winter, curve ② has winter temperatures below freezing, and curve ④ is too cool overall. Final answer: ③

The table gives Beijing sunrise and sunset times for four dates, so the day lengths are: March 1 = 11 h 20 min, June 1 = 14 h 49 min, September 1 = 13 h 03 min, and December 1 = 9 h 32 min. The perfume lily needs daylight longer than 14 h 30 min to flower. March 1 is below this threshold, while June 1 is above it (14 h 49 min > 14 h 30 min), so the threshold is crossed between those two dates, around late May or early June. Since the flowering period lasts about 3 months, the plant would flower from roughly early June into early September. Final answer: it would enter the flowering period around late May to early June.

In the diagram, circle a is connected to the natural mountain forest area, the water source area, and the biogas digester: it receives water from the water source area, receives biogas (沼气) from the biogas digester, and sends domestic sewage (生活污水) to the biochemical pool and biogas digester. In an ecological agriculture circulation system, the component that uses biogas as household energy and produces domestic sewage is the residential area, because biogas is consumed for cooking and lighting in daily life, and sewage is generated from household activities. Therefore, a represents the residential area. Final answer: 居住区（生活区）

The image shows that the 2008 international financial crisis hit the Pearl River Delta and Yangtze River Delta, leading to factory closures, bankruptcies, production shutdowns, and the early return of millions of migrant workers. Because this was a large external demand shock to an export-oriented region, the Chinese government responded with macroeconomic stimulus and industrial restructuring measures. Consequently, the Pearl River Delta could obtain national policy support to help it cope with the crisis. Final answer: national policy support.

The map shows three west-to-east resource-transfer routes in China; route ① is the dashed line that begins in the northwestern inland near 40°N, 95°E, corresponding to the West-to-East natural gas pipeline whose source is the Tarim Basin/Xinjiang region. This source area lies far from the sea, has a dry continental climate, sparse vegetation, and a fragile ecosystem, so wind erosion, water shortage, and human pressure mainly cause land desertification. Final answer: land desertification.

The map covers eastern China roughly 90°E–120°E and 23°26′N–40°N; route ③ starts in the southwestern Yunnan–Guizhou–Guangxi region near the Tropic of Cancer and represents the southern channel of China’s West–East Electricity Transmission, whose power-export area lies on the Yunnan–Guizhou Plateau. That plateau has extensive karst terrain, steep relief, heavy monsoon rainfall, and thin, fragile soils, so vegetation removal and construction for power projects cause severe soil erosion that exposes bedrock and produces rocky desertification. Final answer: soil erosion, especially rocky desertification.

The figure shows houses and villages placed on the higher ground, while the lower land along the river is used as farmland for corn, rice, and wheat. This pattern occurs because the lower riverbank is flat, fertile, and well-watered, making it suitable for crops, but it is also prone to flooding, so people choose the safer, higher ground for settlement. Therefore, the main cause of the different land-use patterns is the difference in elevation and the associated flood risk. Final answer: differences in topography (elevation) and flood risk along the riverbanks.

The image shows the Sun at the center with Earth on an outer orbit and celestial body M on an inner orbit, meaning M is closer to the Sun than Earth. In the solar system, the planets orbiting inside Earth’s orbit are Mercury and Venus, so one possibility for M is Mercury. Final answer: Mercury.

Figure 1 shows the Sun at the center with celestial body M orbiting on a path inside Earth’s orbit, so M must be one of the inferior planets whose orbits are smaller than Earth’s; the only such planets are Mercury and Venus, meaning the other possible planet is Mercury or Venus. Final answer: Mercury or Venus

The lake shown at about 40°N, 60°E next to a large desert is the Aral Sea, and Figure B’s April/July patterns show seasonal shrinkage and exposure of lakebed. This arid inland region commonly suffers desertification, soil salinization, and dust/salt storms, but red tide is a coastal algal-bloom phenomenon that requires a connection to the sea or large brackish coastal waters, so it cannot occur here. Final answer: red tide.

The diagram shows the shaded urban core at 乙, with 甲 to the northwest beside a lake and higher ground, and 丙 to the southwest on the outskirts near a major road and the ocean. Because the city is in southeast coastal China, the prevailing summer monsoon comes from the southeast and the winter monsoon from the northwest; a polluting chemical industry should therefore be placed on the outskirts, downwind of the city for both seasons, away from the urban water source, and with good transport access. Location 甲 is unsuitable because it lies next to the lake/river source and would pollute the city’s water supply, while also being upwind of the city during the northwest winter monsoon. Location 丙, however, is southwest of the city, so pollutants from it would be carried toward the northwest in summer and toward the southeast in winter, away from the urban area; it is also near the sea and a road for transport and is separated from the lake water source. Final answer: 丙.

Table 1 shows Beijing’s 2009 planned urban construction land by category: commercial services 200 ha (3.5%), residential commodity housing 700 ha (12.3%), affordable housing 600 ha (10.5%), science/education/culture/health/administration 400 ha (7%), industrial storage 800 ha (14%), other industries 200 ha (3.5%), and infrastructure 2800 ha (49.1%). The total planned supply is 200 + 700 + 600 + 400 + 800 + 200 + 2800 = 5700 ha, and infrastructure’s share is 2800 ÷ 5700 ≈ 49.1%, which is the largest share and nearly half of the total. Since the greatest proportion of land is allocated to infrastructure, this supply structure is most beneficial for improving Beijing’s urban infrastructure. Final answer: urban infrastructure.

The image shows a high-speed railway route in Northeast China connecting Harbin, Changchun, Shenyang, and Dalian, with a computer mouse graphic included. In transportation construction, the decisive factor for high-speed railway construction is socio-economic factors, particularly economic development level and passenger demand, because high-speed rail requires substantial investment and must serve large passenger flows to be viable, while natural conditions such as topography and climate mainly affect construction difficulty and cost rather than determine whether the railway is built. The image supports this by showing the railway linking major cities and economic centers in Northeast China, reflecting that high-speed rail development is driven by economic needs and passenger traffic demand. Final answer: socio-economic factors (economic development and passenger demand).

Figure 2 is a crop-distribution map of India showing four crops in the legend: jute (×), cotton (○), tea (leaf symbol), and sugarcane (stalk symbol). The tea symbol is placed in the low, flat Ganges Plain, whereas tea in India actually grows on the well-drained, cooler hill slopes of the Western Ghats and the northeastern hills (Assam, Darjeeling, Nilgiri), not in the hot alluvial plains. Therefore the crop whose marked distribution is obviously inconsistent with reality is tea. Final answer: 茶叶（茶）.

The map shows settlement P at a relatively low elevation in the southwest and mountain peak k at a much higher elevation toward the north-central part; the adjacent labeled contours 850 m and 800 m establish a 50 m contour interval, and k lies about 10–12 contour intervals above P, giving an approximate elevation difference of roughly 1000 m. Using the standard atmospheric temperature lapse rate of about 0.6 °C per 100 m (or about 6.5 °C per km), a 1000 m increase in elevation lowers the temperature by about 6 °C. Final answer: lower, by about 6 °C.

The figure shows settlements placed on higher, sloping ground with houses that appear raised or stilted above the hillside, alongside terraced fields growing rice, corn, and wheat. Building dwellings on elevated ground with ventilated, raised floors is a common adaptation to a hot, humid environment with heavy rainfall, because it reduces exposure to ground moisture, flooding, and insects, while rice cultivation also requires abundant warmth and water. These combined clues point to a monsoon climate, and the crop mix and architectural style are most typical of the subtropical monsoon climate zone. Final answer: subtropical monsoon climate.

The schematic shows a rain band over western China where cold air from the north meets warm, moist airflow from the south/southwest near the Sichuan Basin, with the subtropical high lying to the southeast; this rain area lies in the upper reaches of the Yangtze River. West China autumn rain mainly affects Sichuan, Guizhou, Chongqing, southern Shaanxi, and western Hubei, all within the Yangtze River basin, and persistent rainfall can raise river levels and cause flooding. Final answer: the Yangtze River basin.

The image places “工业” (industry) at the center and shows eight surrounding location factors labeled a–h: 原料 (raw materials), 劳力 (labor), 市场 (market), 动力 (power), 技术 (technology), 交通 (transport), 资金 (capital), and 政策 (policy). In industrial location theory, an entrepreneur evaluates all of these factors not for their own sake, but to determine which site yields the greatest net return; the core decision rule is to minimize total production and distribution costs while maximizing revenue and profit. Therefore, although raw materials, labor, market access, transport, and policy all matter, the overriding consideration is economic benefit. Final answer: economic benefit—minimizing total costs and maximizing profit.

The shaded urban area lies on a flat coastal plain beside a river and the sea, with roads linking the surrounding suburbs to the city, while hills rise to the northwest and south. In southeastern coastal China, suburban land this close to a city and well served by roads is typically used for market-oriented, perishable crops that can be supplied fresh to urban consumers. The warm, humid coastal climate also favors rapid vegetable growth. Therefore, the main crop planted in the suburbs is vegetables. Final answer: vegetables.

In the geological profile, location Jia lies above the upper brick-pattern aquiclude, while location Yi lies above the lower diagonal-pattern aquiclude, with the dotted aquifer sandwiched between them; according to the law of superposition, in a sedimentary sequence that has been folded but not overturned, a layer that underlies another is older, so the diagonal aquiclude exposed at Yi is older than the brick aquiclude at Jia. Final answer: Yi was deposited before Jia (the rock layer at Yi is older than the rock layer at Jia).

The map is a contour map with a 1600 m peak on the right and numbered locations 1–4 on the surrounding slopes. Rivers form in valleys, which on a contour map are shown where contour lines bend toward higher elevation, whereas ridges lines bend toward lower elevation. At place ② the contour lines bend toward the 1600 m high ground, indicating a valley that can collect runoff, while places ①, ③, and ④ lie on ridges or spur slopes where the contours bend away from higher ground and would not form a river. Final answer: ②.

The figure shows place B as an island off the southern coast of China, which is Hainan Island, with a solid arrow indicating its agricultural products are shipped northward to the mainland; because Hainan has a tropical climate, its main exported agricultural products are tropical fruits and vegetables, so the second category is vegetables. Final answer: vegetables

Figure b shows a basin or valley enclosed by mountains reaching about 5000 m, with wind crossing the ridge and sinking along the leeward slope, producing a rain-shadow/foehn effect that creates a dry, sunny, warm climate with low humidity. Such arid inland-basin conditions favor drought-tolerant crops that can exploit intense sunlight and large day–night temperature differences, so cotton is a suitable crop. Final answer: cotton.

In the map, F sits inside the highest closed 4400 m alpine forest-line contour in the southeastern Tibetan area, where the forest line rises above the surrounding 3800–4200 m values, indicating locally warmer and moister high-elevation conditions. Alpine forest lines are controlled mainly by temperature and moisture, so an unusually high forest line implies a warm, humid microclimate. F corresponds to the Yarlung Tsangpo (Brahmaputra) valley, which opens southward and channels warm, moist Indian Ocean monsoon air deep onto the plateau, raising the upper limit of tree growth. Final answer: warm, moist Indian Ocean monsoon air entering through the Yarlung Tsangpo (Brahmaputra) valley.

The map displays annual precipitation (with a legend of 2000, 1000, 500, and 200 mm) and annual average isotherms (20 °C and 25 °C) over part of a continent; the dashed line is interpreted as the Tropic of Cancer, and location 1 lies on the northern coastal strip where annual rainfall is roughly 500–1000 mm and the annual mean temperature is close to 20 °C, indicating a Mediterranean climate. In a Mediterranean climate, hot dry summers and mild wet winters favor drought-adapted vegetation, so the natural vegetation is sclerophyllous evergreen forest or scrub. Final answer: subtropical evergreen hard-leaved forest (Mediterranean vegetation).

The diagram shows about six months of 24-hour days from month 4 to month 9 and about six months of 24-hour nights from month 10 to month 3, with roughly 12-hour days and nights around months 3 and 10; this six-month polar day / six-month polar night pattern identifies the place as the North Pole. At the North Pole every horizontal compass direction is south, so on a GPS map the top, bottom, left, and right sides of the screen all point south. Final answer: top—south, bottom—south, left—south, right—south.

In the schematic, large rental points are represented by the larger circles, main roads by the double-line symbols, secondary roads by single lines, and the lake occupies the western side of the map. The large rental points are mainly located along the double-line main roads and at road intersections; they are concentrated in the central and eastern built-up parts of the area and are sparse or absent near the lake in the west. This arrangement follows the urban transport principle that large rental stations should be placed on high-traffic corridors and at major nodes to maximize accessibility, while small rental points fill in lower-order streets. Final answer: The large rental points are mainly distributed along main roads and at intersections, concentrated in the central/eastern built-up area, and relatively sparse near the western lake.

The map shows the Southeast Asian archipelago and mainland between about 90°E and 150°E, crossed by the equator and bordered by the Indian and Pacific Oceans, with labels such as Sumatra, Java, Borneo, Sulawesi, and New Guinea, indicating a hot, humid tropical monsoon region with extensive lowland river valleys and deltas. Monsoon paddy rice farming in Southeast Asia requires abundant rainfall or irrigation, warm year-round temperatures, fertile alluvial soils, and intensive labor, and it is typically carried out by smallholder families on river plains, deltas, and terraced hillsides rather than by large machines. Because the region’s agriculture remains labor-intensive and small-scale, the characteristic it does not have is large-scale mechanized farming. Final answer: large-scale mechanized farming.

The image shows 2010 urbanization levels and average annual urbanization speeds for the world, Asia, Africa, Europe and North America; Asia and Africa have lower urbanization levels but higher speeds (about 0.55% and 0.52% respectively) than Europe and North America, indicating that emerging regions are urbanizing rapidly. Rapid urbanization in emerging countries increases urban population density, accelerates aging and intensifies pressure on pension and social-security systems, so realistic retirement-policy responses generally include gradually raising the retirement age, expanding pension-insurance coverage and developing diversified elderly-care services. Therefore, the description most inconsistent with reality is that the retirement age is lowered or retirement benefits are substantially improved without a corresponding economic basis, because this would aggravate fiscal burdens and labor shortages rather than relieve urbanization pressures. Final answer: lowering the retirement age (or substantially lowering the retirement age) is the retirement-policy description most inconsistent with reality.

The map shows the main peak A enclosed by a 1600 m contour and a smaller hill to the southeast that contains point 5. On the equinox, sunrise at sea level is about 6:00 local time, and higher elevations see sunrise earlier. Place A sees sunrise at 5:00, one hour earlier than sea level, while place B sees it at 5:30, half an hour earlier. Since the 30-minute sunrise difference corresponds to the given 800 m relative height between A and B, a 60-minute difference corresponds to 1600 m, so A is 1600 m above sea level, matching the labeled 1600 m contour, and B is 800 m above sea level. This makes the contour interval 400 m. Point 5 lies inside the 800 m contour on the smaller hill and below the un-drawn 1200 m contour, so its elevation is between 800 m and 1200 m. Final answer: about 1000 m (between 800 m and 1200 m).

The graph plots time from 1980 to 2000 on the horizontal axis, with the dashed line showing groundwater level (left axis, depth in meters) and the solid line showing land subsidence (right axis, in millimeters). Over this period the dashed groundwater line falls from about 20 m to roughly 55 m, while the solid land-subsidence line rises from near 0 to about 250 mm, so the two trends move together: the deeper the groundwater level declines, the greater the land subsidence becomes. This relationship reflects the principle that excessive withdrawal of groundwater reduces pore-water pressure in aquifers, causing compaction of the overlying or underlying sediments and thus surface subsidence. Therefore, the decline in groundwater level in this place is related to increasing land subsidence. Final answer: land subsidence.

The map shows a strong high-pressure system over northwestern China/Mongolia, a low-pressure system to the northeast, and a cold front—indicated by the line with triangles—sweeping across northern China near Beijing. A cold front forces warm air upward, producing a rapid temperature drop, a rise in pressure, a wind shift from southerly to northerly, and short-lived showers or thunderstorms; it does not produce the long-lasting, steady precipitation that is characteristic of a warm front. Therefore, the phenomenon unrelated to this system passing through Beijing is continuous precipitation. Final answer: continuous precipitation (连续性降水).

The graph shows annual precipitation (line, right axis) varying mostly between about 1000 mm and 2000 mm from 1990 to 2000, while the seasonal bars show that summer activity/moisture is much greater than winter activity/moisture. This pattern—high annual rainfall with a strong summer concentration and a relatively dry winter—is characteristic of a monsoon climate. The totals are too high for a temperate monsoon climate, the summer-wet pattern rules out a Mediterranean climate, and the values are more typical of a subtropical monsoon climate than a tropical monsoon climate, which is usually wetter overall. Final answer: subtropical monsoon climate.

The map shows a Northern Hemisphere landscape with north at the top and the sea lying to the east; the highest terrain is the 940 m peak, and the surrounding ridges create different local horizons for points ①–④. In the Northern Hemisphere the winter sun rises in the southeast and the summer sun rises in the northeast, so a point that cannot see winter sunrise but can see summer sunrise must have higher land blocking its southeastern view while its northeastern view is open toward the sea. Point ① is on the western slope, where the main ridge blocks all eastern sunrise; points ③ and ④ are in positions with comparatively open southeastern horizons. Point ② is on the eastern slope, but higher ground lies to its southeast, blocking the winter southeast sunrise; its northeastern horizon is unobstructed, so the summer northeast sunrise is visible. Final answer: ②

The map shows the Yellow River Delta entering the Bohai Sea near Dongying city at about 38°N, 119°E, where the river deposits sediment that builds delta land. Excessive human diversion of Yellow River water reduces the downstream runoff, which in turn decreases the amount of sediment the river can transport and deposit, slowing delta growth. Final answer: runoff.

The image depicts Sri Lanka, an island country near 6°–9°N and 80°E, with a winter monsoon arrow blowing from the northeast toward the southwest. In the northern Indian Ocean, winter monsoon winds drive the North Equatorial Current westward; therefore, a commercial fleet sailing from Sri Lanka can travel faster toward the west, specifically toward the Arabian Sea, Red Sea, Persian Gulf, and adjacent western Indian Ocean regions. Final answer: westward, toward the Arabian Sea/Red Sea/Persian Gulf (western Indian Ocean).

The map shows a small Atlantic island with topographic contour lines, a river, a scale of 1:500 000, and four labeled locations—甲 (A), 乙 (B), 丙 (C), and 丁 (D). Because vegetation is uniform, soil and water loss is controlled mainly by slope steepness and runoff concentration, with steeper slopes producing greater erosion. On the map, the contour lines are closest together near 乙 (B) on the western side of the island, indicating a steep slope, and this point also lies near the river valley where runoff is concentrated. In contrast, 甲 (A) and 丁 (D) are near the coast with more widely spaced contours, and 丙 (C) lies in a more gently sloping interior area. Therefore, the steepest and most runoff-prone location is 乙 (B). Final answer: B (乙).

The map displays haze conditions across mainland China using two categories: dark shading for heavy haze and lighter gray shading for light haze. The heavy haze is concentrated in North China, particularly over the Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei region, Shandong, Henan, and neighboring areas, while light haze extends across parts of central and eastern China. Overall, the haze is mainly distributed in the eastern part of mainland China, with the densest concentrations in North China and the eastern coastal region. Final answer: The haze is mainly distributed in the eastern part of mainland China, especially concentrated in North China (the Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei region, Shandong, and Henan areas) and extending toward the eastern coastal region.

Place 1 lies on the northeastern side of the 1024 hPa high-pressure system, where the isobars run roughly northwest–southeast and pressure decreases toward the northeast, so the horizontal pressure-gradient force points northeast, perpendicular to the isobars. In the Southern Hemisphere (the map is centered near 30°S), the Coriolis force deflects the wind to the left of the pressure-gradient force, causing the surface air to flow toward the northwest; therefore the wind at place 1 comes from the southeast. Final answer: southeast wind (SE).

Place B lies inside a closed isopleth labeled 8, while the adjacent outer isopleths are labeled 10, giving a contour interval of 2°C on this maximum negative temperature anomaly map. Because the map shows negative anomalies, the 8 and 10 isopleths represent −8°C and −10°C; the closed −8°C line surrounds a local minimum in negative anomaly, so the next unlabeled inner isopleth would be −6°C. Thus the maximum negative anomaly at B is greater than −8°C and less than −6°C. Final answer: −8°C < B < −6°C.

The left map places City A on the southwest coast of Australia near 30°S–35°S and 115°E–120°E, a location that falls within the Mediterranean climate zone. Mediterranean climate generally occurs on the west coasts of continents between about 30° and 40° latitude, but in this part of Australia it is confined to a small area because the southwest corner of the continent is a narrow coastal plain bounded by the Indian Ocean to the west and south and by arid to semi-arid inland areas to the north and east, leaving little room for the climate type to expand. Final answer: The Mediterranean climate around City A has a small distribution mainly because the southwest corner of Australia is a narrow coastal area surrounded by ocean on the west and south sides and by arid/semi-arid inland regions on the north and east sides, restricting this climate to a narrow coastal strip.

The image is a map of an urban street network showing a public bicycle rental system with many small rental points and a few large rental points distributed along main roads, secondary roads, and branch roads, indicating that the system is designed to replace short motorized trips. Public bicycle systems reduce the need for cars, buses, and motorcycles, and since these vehicles burn fossil fuels, reducing their use lowers the release of pollutants produced by combustion. Therefore, the main emissions reduced are those from motor vehicles. Final answer: motor vehicle exhaust emissions.

The photo shows Mount Fuji’s summit covered with snow while cherry blossoms bloom at the mountain’s foot in May. Using the standard vertical temperature lapse rate of about 0.6 °C per 100 m, the summit temperature in the hottest month is approximately 24.5 °C − 0.6 °C/100 m × 37.76 ≈ 1.8 °C, which is above freezing, and the altitude of the 0 °C summer isotherm is about 24.5/0.6 × 100 m 4 083 m, higher than Mount Fuji’s 3 776 m peak. Therefore the snow is not permanent year-round snow; it belongs to seasonal snow cover. Final answer: seasonal snow cover.

The figure plots monthly TSS flux (positive inflow bars in summer, small or negative outflow bars in winter) and lake water level, which rises from May, peaks around August–September, and then falls. The large summer inflow of TSS coincides with the period of high water level, while low TSS flux corresponds to low water level, so the seasonal TSS flux variation is directly driven by changes in the basin’s water level. Final answer: water level.

The diagram plots monthly TSS flux as positive inflow and negative outflow bars, together with a line showing lake water level in meters. The inflow TSS peaks sharply in July–August, while the water-level line also rises to its highest point during the same period and then declines through the winter. Because the seasonal TSS flux pattern closely tracks the rise and fall of this line, the other direct cause of the lake’s TSS flux seasonal change is the change in lake water level. Final answer: water level.

The map shows mineral-spring points, general faults, and deep faults in the Jiangxi–Fujian border area; the water bodies marked by the mineral-spring symbols are natural discharges of water from underground along fracture zones, which means they belong to groundwater. Final answer: groundwater.

The image shows four schematic maps labeled 甲–丁, corresponding to A–D; the leftmost map (A) lies near 110°E around the Tropic of Cancer, matching Hainan Island / the Leizhou Peninsula in the tropical South China region, where the Leiqiong volcanic field occurs. Because this destination is in a tropical coastal area, the distinctive landscape that can also be enjoyed near the volcano is tropical coastal scenery. Final answer: tropical coastal scenery.

The four maps show, from left to right, Baja California (甲), Iceland (乙), New Zealand (丙), and Japan (丁); location B corresponds to the second map, which depicts Iceland at about 20°W and crossed by the Arctic Circle (66.5°N). Iceland is a volcanic island on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge and is also famous for its large ice caps and glaciers, such as Vatnajökull, giving it the nickname “land of ice and fire.” Therefore, besides volcanoes, visitors near location B can also enjoy glacier scenery. Final answer: glaciers.

The four maps are labeled 甲, 乙, 丙, and 丁, corresponding to destinations A, B, C, and D; map 丙 (C) shows two islands between about 40°S and 50°S near 170° longitude, matching New Zealand, with the marked volcano on the North Island. New Zealand lies on the Pacific–Australian plate boundary, so its North Island has active volcanoes and extensive geothermal activity; therefore, near the volcano at C tourists can also enjoy a geothermal landscape of geysers, hot springs, and boiling mud pools. Final answer: a geothermal landscape (geysers, hot springs, and mud pools).

The fourth map (丁), which corresponds to location D, shows an island arc at about 130°E between 32°N and 38°N, identifying it as Japan; the marked volcano lies in central Honshu near the Mount Fuji area. Besides the volcano, Japan is world-famous for its spring cherry-blossom (sakura) scenery, so near location D tourists can also enjoy cherry blossoms. Final answer: cherry blossoms (sakura).

The image shows two maps: the left map marks U.S. soybean producing areas mainly in the central United States around the 40°N parallel, while the right map marks Brazilian soybean producing areas in the southern part of Brazil, mostly south of the Tropic of Capricorn.
