The attached table records strong sandstorm counts and land desertification speed by decade, rising from 5 strong sandstorms and 1560 km²/year desertification in the 1950s to 23 strong sandstorms and 24600 km²/year in the 1990s, indicating frequent sandstorm weather in northern China. In the corresponding North Pacific situation, warmer sea-surface conditions cause the isotherms to deviate poleward, so the isotherms protrude toward higher latitudes, i.e., they bulge northward. Final answer: The isotherms bulge northward (toward higher latitudes) in the North Pacific.

The map shows Zhangye at about 40°N and 100°E, deep inside the Eurasian continent, surrounded by desert and near the Heihe River with high mountains to the south; this inland desert location means the area receives strong solar radiation, has many sunny days, and experiences a large day–night temperature difference. In arid continental climates, hot sunny days promote photosynthesis and sugar production, while cool nights reduce respiration losses, so sugars accumulate in melons and fruits, giving them high sweetness and excellent quality. Final answer: The large day–night temperature difference and abundant sunshine in this inland arid region.

Curve ⑤ is the day-length curve for place ④; reading from the right-hand axis, it reaches about 18 h on the summer solstice and falls to about 6 h on the winter solstice. Since night length equals 24 h minus day length, the night length on the summer solstice is 24 h − 18 h = 6 h, and the day length on the winter solstice is about 6 h. Final answer: night length on the summer solstice is about 6 hours and day length on the winter solstice is about 6 hours.

The image shows the Sun sitting on the horizon at sunset, aligned with a straight railway track so that the solar disk appears between the two rails. Because the rails are fixed, the same view occurs only when the Sun sets at the same azimuth, which requires the same solar declination. Solar declination is symmetric about the summer solstice, so a date before the solstice has a matching date after it. May 1 is about 50–52 days before the summer solstice around June 21–22, so the corresponding date is about the same interval after the solstice. Counting roughly 52 days after June 22 gives approximately August 13. Final answer: around August 13.

The map depicts the domestic route of the ancient Silk Road crossing northwestern China, with stops including Xi'an, Lanzhou, Dunhuang, Turpan, and Kashgar, and passing through extensive arid and semi-arid zones. This region is characterized by a continental arid climate, scarce water resources, desert landscapes, sparse population, and fragile ecosystems, all of which constrain tourism development by raising infrastructure costs, limiting visitor comfort, and reducing environmental carrying capacity. Final answer: harsh natural environment (arid climate, water scarcity, and desert conditions).

The figure shows a city with a river running through it and several lakes; functional zone ② is marked with horizontal-line shading and lies mainly along the river banks and around the lakes. In ecological city planning, waterfront and lakeside areas are ecologically sensitive and should be preserved as green buffers rather than intensively developed, because they protect water quality, reduce flood risk, maintain biodiversity, and provide recreational open space. Therefore, zone ② should be planned as an ecological green belt/waterfront green space. Final answer: ecological green belt (waterfront green space / ecological protection zone).

The schematic diagram shows a city with a central district, radiating main roads and a highway, rivers, and lakes, and four legend patterns labeled ①, ②, ③, and ④. For ecological city planning, riverside and lakeside areas should be protected as green buffers rather than built-up or industrial land. Functional zone ③ is located along these water bodies, so it should be planned as a green space/ecological green belt to protect water quality, reduce pollution, and improve the urban environment. Final answer: green space (ecological green belt/green space zone).

The legend in the schematic distinguishes four planned functional zones marked ①–④, and zone ④ appears as a separate, buffer-like strip between other land-use areas. In ecological city planning, such buffer strips are normally designated as green belts/green space, because they help separate incompatible uses, reduce pollution, protect water bodies and improve the urban ecological environment. Therefore, functional zone ④ should be planned as a green belt. Final answer: 绿化带（绿地）

The image shows marine organism fossils preserved in rock at Yehliu Coast Geopark, Taiwan Province, indicating that this area was once covered by the sea. The formation sequence began with sedimentation, as marine sediments accumulated on the seafloor and buried organisms; this was followed by fossilization, in which the organic remains were preserved in the sedimentary layers. Next, lithification transformed the loose sediments into solid sedimentary rock. Subsequent crustal uplift, caused by tectonic forces, raised the rock above sea level. Finally, weathering and erosion exposed the fossils and shaped the present coastal landscape. Final answer: sedimentation, fossilization, lithification, crustal uplift, and weathering/erosion.

On the map, area A is located in the Tarim Basin of southern Xinjiang, in the far western part of western China, near Korla and the Tianshan foothill belt. The Tarim Basin is one of China’s major oil- and gas-bearing sedimentary basins, so the industrial belt there is classified as an energy base. Therefore, the key industry of area A is most likely oil and natural gas extraction and petrochemicals. Final answer: oil and natural gas (petrochemical) industry.

The diagram shows a city with four patterned functional zones; zone ④ is located along the river and adjacent to lakes, occupying areas with the best natural scenery and environmental quality. In urban planning, land uses that seek clean air, water views, and green surroundings are said to follow the ecological/environment optimal principle. Therefore, the layout of functional zone ④ follows the ecological environment optimal principle. Final answer: ecological environment

The map shows that Yulin is surrounded by large coal deposits in the Shenmu–Fugu area to the north, natural-gas fields around Jingbian to the southwest, and a sizable rock-salt deposit near Suide to the southeast, with railways and a gas pipeline crossing the region. These patterns mean Yulin has abundant and diversified mineral resources—coal for power and coal-chemical feedstock, natural gas for gas-chemical industries, and rock salt for salt-chemical production—located relatively close together, which lowers transport and linkage costs; the existing rail and pipeline networks also support large-scale extraction, transport, and market supply. Final answer: Yulin’s resource advantages are its abundant and spatially concentrated coal, natural gas, and rock-salt reserves, supported by railway and gas-pipeline infrastructure, making it well suited to become a national energy and chemical industry base.

The bar chart shows the percentage of each land-use type in 1975, 1990, and 2005. By comparing the heights of the bars, the grassland share stays at roughly 12% in 1975, about 14% in 1990, and about 11% in 2005, while forest land decreases sharply, housing land and road/square land increase, and the “other” category changes more noticeably. Final answer: grassland (草地).

The map shows Yunan County located in western Guangdong Province, with its county town and several built-up towns linked by railways and highways, indicating transportation infrastructure that supports industrial development. Industrial agglomeration occurs when the county undertakes industries such as building materials and fine chemicals from the Pearl River Delta, forming an industrial cluster. This concentration of industries mainly promotes local industrialization and urbanization by shifting the economic structure toward secondary industry, attracting rural population to towns, expanding built-up areas, and driving infrastructure and economic development. Final answer: promoting industrialization and urbanization

The map shows the new Dunhuang–Golmud railway (T) running directly between Dunhuang and Golmud, while the existing route makes a long detour eastward past points 甲 and 乙 across the provincial boundary. Dunhuang lies in Gansu Province and Golmud in Qinghai Province, so the old detour currently passes through the capitals of these provinces; point 甲 is the easternmost city on that detour, corresponding to Lanzhou, the capital of Gansu Province. Therefore, the central city of the provincial-level administrative region at 甲 that will no longer be detoured through is Lanzhou. Final answer: Lanzhou.

The graph shows that from 2000 to 2005 the concentration of inhalable particulate matter in Beijing stayed well above the 0.10 mg/m³ standard, while sulfur dioxide and nitrogen dioxide remained below their respective standards; this indicates that the high inhalable particulate matter has sources distinct from the usual sulfur/nitrogen oxide emissions. A major additional reason is the influence of dust and sand from the arid and semi-arid regions to the northwest of Beijing, where desertified land and sparse vegetation are easily lifted by winds and transported into the city, especially during spring dust storms; construction dust and road dust in the urban area also add to this load. Final answer: dust and sand from nearby arid/semi-arid regions and desertified land to the northwest, plus urban dust from construction and traffic.

In Figure 6, the cost structure of the Jia industry shows that the largest locational cost share is product transport, while the shares for raw material, technology, and wages are all smaller; because an industry with high product transport costs must locate near its market to minimize transport expenses, Jia’s location requirement corresponds to a market-oriented industrial layout. Final answer: market-oriented industry (市场指向型工业).

The map shows successive urban land-use boundaries for 1950, 1960, and 1990, with the built-up area clearly expanding outward along the railway, the Yangtze River, and the canal, so the arrangement of transport routes is guiding the city’s growth. In urban geography, the spatial arrangement, or layout, of transportation lines is a major factor in shaping urban form because development tends to cluster along accessible transport corridors. Therefore, the blank should describe how transport routes are arranged. Final answer: layout.

The chart shows that from 1975 to 2005 forest land and grassland together declined, while building land and road/square land increased, and the PM10 monthly average concentration also rose; this indicates that reducing green space and expanding built-up/road areas is associated with worsening air quality. Therefore, the city should not adopt measures that further reduce forest/grassland or increase construction and road land. Final answer: the city is not suitable to take measures that further reduce green space and expand built-up/road land, such as large-scale urban construction and road expansion.

The diagram shows precipitation being divided into evaporation, interception (截流), river-channel precipitation, and subsequent runoff components such as surface runoff, underground runoff, groundwater flow, and total runoff. Dense vegetation directly affects the interception link because plant canopies catch rainfall before it reaches the ground, increasing the amount of precipitation intercepted and later evaporated. Therefore, when total precipitation is the same, dense vegetation increases interception. Final answer: It increases interception (截流).

The sketch shows a river flowing past the gridded urban area, with a westward-flowing arrow near ②, and point ① lies on the forested hillside beside the river upstream of the town and upstream of the steel plant at A. Because a waterworks must draw clean water from an upstream location and forested slopes help protect water quality, while a downstream steel plant would pollute the lower reaches, place ① should be planned as a water source protection area/waterworks. Final answer: a waterworks (water source protection area).

The sketch map shows a river flowing westward past a gridded urban area, with point ② located on the downstream side of the city; the steel plant mentioned at A and the town itself would discharge wastewater that flows downriver. In urban planning, a sewage-treatment facility should be placed at the lower reach of a river so it can collect and treat effluent before release, while upstream sites are reserved for cleaner uses such as water supply. Therefore, place ② should be planned as a sewage treatment plant. Final answer: a sewage treatment plant.

The sketch map shows a riverside town at about 121°E, 29°N, with a grid-patterned urban area next to a river and a forested, hilly area to the west/northwest. A steel plant has been built at place A, and point ③ lies inside the urban area between the steel-plant site and the main residential zone. In urban planning, a polluting heavy-industry facility such as a steel plant needs a vegetated buffer between it and living areas, because a green belt can trap dust, absorb pollutants, reduce noise, and block winds that carry contaminated air. Since point ③ occupies this transitional zone, it should not be used for dense housing, commerce, or clean industry. Final answer: a green belt (protective green buffer zone).

The map shows a large garbage pool located between Hawaii and North America and labels an eastward-flowing current as “北太平洋暖流,” which carries water from the western Pacific toward the coasts of Canada and the United States; because ocean currents transport floating materials, this current moves plastic garbage from the garbage patch toward the U.S. coast, creating the reported danger. Final answer: 北太平洋暖流 (North Pacific Warm Current / North Pacific Drift).

The map covers roughly 34°N–35°N and 117°W–119°W, the Pacific coast of southern California, with point d near 35°N. Because the terminator passes through c and d and d’s local time is 6:20, d is on the morning terminator; a sunrise at 6:20 is after the 6:00 equinox sunrise, giving a day length of about 11 hours 20 minutes, which is shorter than 12 hours, so the Northern Hemisphere is in winter and the Southern Hemisphere is in summer. Therefore the seashores entering their peak tourist season are those in the Southern Hemisphere, especially the southeastern/southern coast of Australia. Final answer: the southern/eastern coast of Australia (Southern Hemisphere seashores).

The left map shows latitudes increasing downward (33°33′ at the top to 33°50′ at the bottom), so with north at the top the estuary is in the Southern Hemisphere. In the Southern Hemisphere the Coriolis effect deflects a flowing river current to the left, which erodes the left bank and causes sediment to accumulate on the right bank; because the small island grows by sediment accumulation, it will eventually connect with the right bank. Final answer: the right bank (the south bank in the figure).

The map shows the sea on the left and point ② on the coast at about 0 m elevation; inland the land rises in 100 m contours toward a central high peak that contains point ⑤, while points ③, ④, ⑥ and ① lie on the surrounding slopes. Visibility between two points on a contour map is determined by drawing a straight line of sight and checking whether any intervening ground rises above that line, because a higher ridge or slope will block the view. From ② to ③ the sight line stays on the slope facing the coast and the contours between them are lower than the line, so no terrain blocks the view. The sight lines from ② to ④, ⑤ and ⑥ pass behind the central ridge and peak, whose elevations are higher than those lines, and the line to ① is also blocked by the same high ground, so those places cannot be seen. Final answer: ③

The figure shows two latitudinal land-sea sections along about 20° latitude: the upper segment from roughly 75°E to 85°E between points 1 and 2 represents the Indian subcontinent, while the lower segment from roughly 70°W to 40°W between points 3 and 4 represents South America. Upwelling, which lifts nutrient-rich deep water to the surface and supports major fisheries, occurs along the western coasts of continents where surface waters are driven offshore. The sea area labeled 乙 is the Pacific Ocean off the western coast of South America, where the Peru (Humboldt) Cold Current causes strong coastal upwelling and forms the well-known Peru fishing ground; area 甲, the Arabian Sea/Bay of Bengal side of India, does not have such a major upwelling fishery at this location. Final answer: 乙海域.

The image gives temperature values at five labeled points: ① 5 °C, ② 4 °C, ③ 3 °C, ④ 1 °C, and ⑤ 2 °C, with additional 3 °C and 4 °C lines to the right. A front marks the boundary between different air masses and is located where the horizontal temperature gradient is strongest. Computing the changes between adjacent points gives decreases of 1 °C from ① to ② and from ② to ③, a sharp 2 °C drop from ③ to ④, and then a 1 °C rise from ④ to ⑤, so the largest temperature change occurs between ③ and ④. Therefore the front should be located at ④. Final answer: ④

The chart gives each city’s share of industrial output by sector, and city 4 is shown by the diagonally striped bars; in the aircraft sector the diagonally striped bar is clearly the highest, reaching about 35–40%, while its shares in automobile, electronics, and textiles are relatively low. Since the four cities are Detroit, Xi’an, Kolkata, and Munich, and Xi’an is distinguished by its dominant aircraft/aviation industry, the city whose industrial structure features the largest aircraft share must be Xi’an. Final answer: Xi’an.

The map’s north arrow points up, the Huangpu River runs from the Lupu Bridge in the southwest to the Nanpu Bridge in the northeast, and the World Expo Center sits on the northwest (left) bank with its long, narrow exterior wall following the riverbank, so that wall faces southeast. Sunrise always occurs in the eastern half of the sky; in the Northern Hemisphere the sun rises due east at the equinoxes, northeast of east in summer, and southeast of east in winter. Because the wall faces southeast, the rising sun can shine directly onto it when the sun rises in the southeast, which happens from the autumnal equinox to the vernal equinox. Final answer: from the Autumn Equinox to the following Spring Equinox (the winter half of the year).

The photograph shows a single tree in an open field; its canopy appears fuller on the left side, and a long shadow is cast toward the right side of the image. In the Northern Hemisphere, including northwest China, the south-facing side of a plant receives the most sunlight over the year and therefore grows better, so the denser left side of the crown indicates that left is south and right is north. Because a shadow points away from the sun, a shadow falling to the right/north means the sun was to the left/south. In the Northern Hemisphere the sun is due south at local noon, so the shooting time was most likely about local noon. Final answer: around 12:00 (local noon).

The graph uses Beijing time on the horizontal axis and solar altitude on the vertical axis; curve A (甲) is above the horizon from 0 to about 9 and sets at 9, while curve B (乙) rises at 9 and stays above the horizon until 24, so at 9 Beijing time A is on the sunset terminator and B is on the sunrise terminator. The terminator is a great circle on the Earth, and at any given instant the sunrise point and the sunset point on that circle are diametrically opposite; this is also consistent with A’s day length of about 9 h matching B’s night length of 24 h − 15 h = 9 h. Therefore A and B are on opposite sides of the Earth. Final answer: A and B are antipodal points (diametrically opposite) on the Earth.

The chart shows the downstream Yellow River channel sedimentation rate (solid line, left axis) and the middle-reaches climate humidity index (dashed line, right axis) from 0 to 1900 AD. Before the 19th century, the sedimentation rate remains low until about 900 AD, then rises, and reaches its highest pre-1800 level around 1700–1800 AD, while the humidity index during that interval is also relatively high (about 1.0–1.2), indicating a moist climate. Because high sedimentation under humid conditions points to reduced vegetation cover and accelerated erosion rather than climatic aridity, the period around 1700–1800 AD best reflects severe vegetation degradation. Final answer: the Qing dynasty, around 1700–1800 AD.

In the schematic, both “自然条件优越” and box a feed into “单产高” (high yield per unit area). For commercial grain agriculture, high yields depend not only on favorable natural conditions but also on advanced agricultural technology such as improved seeds and scientific management, so a represents that technological condition. Final answer: 农业科技先进.

The mountain peak is labeled 573 m, the contour interval is 100 m, and the waterfall drops 60 m; the waterfall appears to lie on the 300 m contour, so the pool below the waterfall is at 300 m − 60 m = 240 m and the viewing platform is at 240 m + 5 m = 245 m. Therefore the elevation difference between the peak and the viewing platform is 573 m − 245 m = 328 m, which is most likely about 330 m. Final answer: about 330 m.

Figure I places place D in the East Asian land sector between the 30°N and 40°N latitudinal circles, so a flight from D to an Arab country would head roughly westward. At a speed of about 20° of longitude per hour, in 1 hour 30 minutes the plane covers 20° × 1.5 = 30° of longitude. If D is near eastern China (about 115–120°E), a 30° westward displacement brings the aircraft to roughly 85–90°E, which is in northwestern China near Urumqi. Final answer: Urumqi Diwopu International Airport.

The left map shows the Iberian Peninsula at about 40°N, with Jia (甲) located on the western Atlantic coast and Bing (丙) situated farther inland to the east, separated from the coast by a mountainous zone shown by the dense topographic pattern. The right graph confirms that the three locations receive very different amounts of precipitation, with one station much wetter and another much drier. In this region, prevailing westerlies carry moist Atlantic air inland; when this air rises over the coastal mountains, it drops heavy rain on the windward side, while the inland leeward side lies in a rain shadow and receives far less precipitation. Because Jia and Bing are at similar latitudes and both lie west of the interior plateau, the marked difference in their rainfall is best explained by the blocking and rain-shadow effect of the terrain rather than by latitude or distance from the sea alone. Final answer: 地形（山脉阻挡/雨影效应）.

The image shows a volcano labeled M with a gray-white ash plume extending toward the southeast, indicating that the ash was carried by winds blowing toward the southeast, i.e., from the northwest. In the Southern Hemisphere mid-latitudes the prevailing surface westerlies blow from the northwest toward the southeast, and an eruption lasting about 8 months with persistent southeastward drift fits a volcano in that wind belt. The Andes along the west coast of South America, especially Chile, is a major subduction-related volcanic arc at these latitudes and hosted the 2011 Puyehue–Cordón Caulle eruption, which lasted roughly 8 months and produced southeastward ash plumes. Final answer: on the west coast of South America (the Andes/Chile).

The map shows two isotherms, 2 °C and 4 °C, with temperatures increasing toward the south, indicating the region is in the Northern Hemisphere; January is winter there, and point P lies in the sea close to the coast. In winter, land cools more strongly than the sea, so coastal-sea temperatures are milder than inland temperatures at the same latitude, and a January sea-surface temperature of about 4 °C places P in a relatively northern, temperate coastal sea. Among the adjacent seas of eastern China, only the Bohai Sea and the Yellow Sea have January temperatures near 4 °C; the East China Sea and South China Sea are significantly warmer. Therefore, the southernmost sea consistent with P’s January temperature of about 4 °C is the Yellow Sea. Final answer: the Yellow Sea.

The southwest coast of the map is shown along the sea and is covered by the “salt field” symbol (盐田), indicating that this coastal area has abundant salt resources; regional development planning should therefore exploit this local resource by building a salt-related industrial base there. Final answer: a sea-salt chemical industry base (海盐化工基地).

The map shows Place Yi located inland in the Murray–Darling basin of southeastern Australia, far from the coast and therefore in a drier, semi-arid environment; the climate graph for coastal Place Jia shows a hot summer (about 28°C), mild winter (about 12°C), and annual precipitation around 1000 mm with relatively low winter rainfall, indicating a warm summer-rain climate. Australian mixed wheat-and-sheep farming in this basin is extensive, highly mechanized, and commercial, giving a high commodity rate, but because rainfall is low and unreliable, crop yields per hectare are not high. Therefore the incorrect statement is that Place Yi has high yield per unit area. Final answer: yield per unit area.

The map shows the Expo Park (世博中心馆) situated along the Huangpu River between Nanpu Bridge and Lupu Bridge, indicating a central urban waterfront location with good transportation access and high land value. In urban land-use planning, centrally located, highly accessible, riverside land should be allocated to uses that generate high economic rent and strong public benefit, such as commerce, culture, exhibitions, tourism, and leisure, rather than low-value industrial uses. Therefore, after the Expo closed, this area was most suitably developed into a commercial, cultural, exhibition, tourism, and leisure functional area. Final answer: a commercial, cultural, exhibition, tourism and leisure functional area (commercial/cultural/tourism district).

On the isobar map, the isobars near Viedma (64°W, 40°30′S) run roughly northeast–southwest, with pressure decreasing toward the south/southwest, so the horizontal pressure-gradient force points from higher pressure toward lower pressure, i.e., toward the southwest. In the Southern Hemisphere the Coriolis force deflects moving air to the left of the pressure-gradient force, causing the wind to flow nearly parallel to the isobars with low pressure on the right, which gives a wind blowing toward the southeast; near-surface friction adds a small component toward the low pressure, but the dominant surface wind still comes from the northwest. Final answer: northwest wind.

The table lists Beijing’s daily air-pollution index for sulfur dioxide, carbon monoxide, ozone, nitrogen dioxide, and inhalable particulate matter from February 16 to May 2. During this period the highest values are for inhalable particulate matter, especially the sharp peaks of 500 on March 16 and 324 on April 15, while the gaseous pollutants remain much lower, indicating that inhalable particulates are the primary pollutant. In Beijing’s spring, such sudden large increases in coarse particles are mainly caused by dust (sandstorm) weather, when strong northwest winds associated with cold air outbreaks or Mongolian cyclones lift and transport dust from arid northwestern regions into the city. Final answer: frequent dust/sandstorm weather caused by strong northwest winds/cold air outbreaks.

In Figure A, line E–O–F runs horizontally and line M–O–N runs vertically through the central point O. The E–F profile in Figure B shows the land surface descending from both E and F toward O, with O at the lower elevation of 350 m, which is the cross-section of a valley. The M–N profile in Figure C shows the land surface rising from both M and N toward O, with O at the higher elevation of 350 m, which is the cross-section of a ridge. A location that appears as a valley in one perpendicular profile and as a ridge in the other is a saddle, or col. Final answer: saddle (鞍部).

The left map shows Iceland with volcanic symbols located beneath glaciers or ice caps, and the right photograph shows the 2010 Eyjafjallajökull eruption occurring under an ice cap. When a volcano erupts beneath a glacier, the intense heat melts large volumes of ice and snow, producing meltwater that can accumulate and then be suddenly released; this process generates a catastrophic glacial outburst flood known as a jökulhlaup. Final answer: glacial outburst flood (jökulhlaup).

The graph plots total solar radiation (vertical axis, in W/m²) against month (horizontal axis, 1–12) for three locations. Curve a stays high all year and shows two peaks, which is characteristic of the equatorial region where the sun is nearly overhead around both equinoxes and annual variation is small. Curve b falls to near zero from roughly April to October and peaks around December–January, matching the long polar night and short polar summer of the Antarctic/South Pole. Curve c is the opposite: near zero around the Northern Hemisphere winter and peaks around June–July, matching the Arctic/North Pole. Therefore, a is near the equator, b is near the South Pole/Antarctica, and c is near the North Pole/Arctic. Final answer: a near the equator, b near the South Pole (Antarctica), and c near the North Pole (Arctic).

The map shows latitude lines marked at 17°30′ S, 18° S, and 18°30′ S, so the vertical grid spacing is 0.5° of latitude and the whole map spans 1° of latitude from north to south; the island occupies nearly this full north-south extent. Because one degree of latitude equals about 111 km on Earth’s surface, the island’s north-south length is roughly 1 × 111 km 110 km. Final answer: about 110 km.

The map shows the west coast of southern Africa between about 10°S and 30°S, with the ocean to the west and land to the east, so location 1 lies in the coastal sea off Namibia/Angola. This coastal sea is influenced by the cold Benguela Current, whose cool sea surface cools the overlying moist air to its dew point, producing frequent condensation and fog. Therefore, the weather characteristic of the sea area at location 1 is foggy. Final answer: foggy.

The graph shows seven points along 31°N; the square-marked line gives longitude from 0°E at point ① to 180°E at point ⑦, and the diamond-marked line gives sea-level pressure in hPa. Point ⑥ corresponds to about 150°E, where the pressure is about 1010 hPa; pressure rises eastward to about 1020 hPa at 180° and falls westward toward the low near 90°E, so the pressure-gradient force at ⑥ points toward the west. In the Northern Hemisphere, moving air is deflected to the right of its motion, so a westward pressure-gradient-driven flow is turned toward the northwest, meaning the wind comes from the southeast. Final answer: southeast wind.

The figure is a bid-rent curve diagram with land rent level on the vertical axis and distance from the city center on the horizontal axis, showing three downward-sloping curves (a, b, c) that represent the rent-paying ability of different land uses across three zones (甲, 乙, 丙). In this model, each land use occupies the zone where its bid rent exceeds that of competing uses; curve c has the flattest slope and extends farthest from the city center, which corresponds to industrial land use because industry requires large land areas and can tolerate greater distance from the center. In area 丙 (C), the outermost zone, curve c lies above curves a and b, meaning the industrial sector has the highest rent-paying capacity in this area and therefore outbids commercial and residential uses. Final answer: Area C is leased by the industrial sector because the industrial bid-rent curve (c) is the highest in this outer zone farthest from the city center, so industry can pay the most rent; industry needs large land parcels and can afford to locate farther from the center, allowing it to outcompete other land uses in area C.

The figure is a North-pole-centered polar projection with meridians marked at 0° to the right, 90°E at the top, and 180° to the left; the dusk terminator a lies along the meridian midway between 180° and 90°W, i.e. 135°W. Because Earth rotates counterclockwise when viewed from the North Pole and the dusk line marks 18:00 local solar time, the midnight (0:00) meridian is 90° of longitude east of the dusk meridian, so 135°W + 90°E = 45°W. With the International Date Line at 180°, the new day extends eastward from 45°W to 180°, covering 225° of longitude, while the old day covers the remaining 135° from 180° eastward to 45°W. Final answer: The new day occupies 5/8 of the globe from 45°W eastward to 180°, and the old day occupies the remaining 3/8 from 180° eastward to 45°W.

The image shows Ningxia with annual precipitation isohyets of 200 mm and 400 mm, indicating that most of the region receives only 200–400 mm of rainfall and lies in the semi-arid to arid zone, while the Helan Mountains lie to the west and the Yellow River runs through the area. In agricultural regional geography, areas with low and unreliable rainfall cannot support rain-fed farming, so crop production depends on water supplied by rivers or groundwater; Ningxia’s plains are irrigated mainly by the Yellow River, forming a typical irrigated farming system. Therefore, among the world’s agricultural regional types, Ningxia agriculture mainly belongs to irrigated agriculture, also described as oasis agriculture in arid regions. Final answer: irrigated agriculture (oasis agriculture).

The contour map shows that point ① is located at the innermost closed contour of the island’s highest hill, while points ②, ③, and ④ lie on lower or outer slopes. In topography, a higher observation point has a more distant visible horizon and is obstructed less by surrounding terrain, so it can observe a larger area. Therefore, the highest location, ①, has the largest observed area. Final answer: ①.

The graph shows noon solar altitude on the vertical axis and day length on the horizontal axis. March 21 is the spring equinox, when every location on Earth has a day length of 12 hours, so only points on the 12-hour vertical line can represent March 21 locations. On the equinox the noon solar altitude is given by H = 90° − |φ|, where φ is latitude; a point north of the Tropic of Cancer has φ > 23.5°N, so its noon solar altitude must be less than 90° − 23.5° = 66.5°. Point ① has H = 90° (equator), point ② has H > 66.5° (between the equator and the Tropic of Cancer), point ③ has H ≈ 45° (< 66.5°), and point ④ has H = 0° (< 66.5°); point ⑤ has a day length of about 18 hours, which is impossible on the equinox. Therefore only points ③ and ④ may be located north of the Tropic of Cancer. Final answer: ③④.

The figure plots three variables from 1960 to about 2002: annual precipitation (open circles, left axis in mm), annual average temperature (solid line, right axis in °C), and water-level change (dashed line with triangles, left axis in mm). The water-level change curve rises and falls in a pattern that closely matches the precipitation curve, with peaks around 1967, 1989, and the mid-1990s and troughs around 1970 and 2000, whereas the temperature curve shows a smoother overall increase and does not track the water-level fluctuations as closely. Therefore, among the two climatic factors shown, precipitation has the strongest relationship with Qinghai Lake’s water-level changes. Final answer: precipitation.

The figure’s horizontal axis shows the percentage of total employees working in manufacturing, and its vertical axis shows per capita GDP in U.S. dollars; the three left‑most points (1, 2, 3) cluster near the origin with low manufacturing shares and low per capita GDP, while point 4 lies far to the upper right with a much larger manufacturing share and a much higher per capita GDP, and the arrow points from the low‑low cluster toward point 4. This arrangement indicates a positive relationship: a larger share of employment in manufacturing is associated with higher per capita GDP. Therefore, the arrow most likely represents the trend or process of industrialization/economic development, showing that as a country’s manufacturing employment share increases, its per capita GDP tends to rise. Final answer: the arrow most likely represents the process of industrialization/economic development, indicating that a rising share of manufacturing employment is associated with higher per capita GDP.

The pie chart shows the 2007 shares of global biocapacity for the top ten countries: Brazil 14.1%, the United States 11.3%, China 9.5%, Russia 7.6%, Canada 4.7%, India 3.6%, Australia 3.0%, Indonesia 2.5%, Argentina 2.3%, and Bolivia 1.5%, with “Other” at 40.0%. Because biocapacity is the total productive land area that can supply renewable resources and absorb carbon dioxide, a country’s share of global biocapacity is strongly related to its total land area. Among the listed top ten, India’s 3.6% share is one of the smallest, and India has a much smaller land area than Brazil, the United States, China, Russia, Canada, and Australia. Therefore, the country that has a small share because its land area is small is India. Final answer: India

The chart shows the industrial output structures of Detroit, Xi’an, Kolkata, and Munich; City 2 is the city whose industrial structure is dominated by textiles, which corresponds to Kolkata. Kolkata’s textile industry is based on jute processing, and because jute is bulky and perishable the mills are located close to the jute-growing areas of the Ganges-Brahmaputra delta, making the supply of raw materials the leading location factor. Final answer: raw materials (jute/raw material supply).

The map shows coral reefs (dotted pattern) surrounding lagoon-type islands in the Nansha Islands, and the reefs are thicker and more continuous on the northeastern sides of the islands/atolls than on the southwestern sides. Because the windward side receives more wave-driven mixing that supplies food and oxygen, coral grows faster and denser there, so the side with the denser reefs faces the prevailing wind. Therefore, the prevailing wind in the area most likely comes from the northeast. Final answer: Northeast wind (from the northeast).

The section shows horizontal sandstone and conglomerate at the top, underlain by an erosional surface that truncates tilted limestone beds, a granite body, and a fault. The limestone beds are folded and tilted, and the granite cuts across them, so the granite intruded after the limestone was deposited and folded. The fault displaces both the limestone and the granite, so faulting occurred after granite intrusion, and because the fault and underlying folded rocks are truncated by the unconformity beneath the undeformed sandstone and conglomerate, erosion and later deposition of those upper layers happened last. Therefore the sequence is: deposition of limestone, folding/tilting of the limestone, intrusion of granite, faulting, erosion and formation of an unconformity, and finally deposition of the overlying conglomerate and sandstone. Final answer: deposition of limestone → folding/tilting → granite intrusion → faulting → erosion/unconformity → deposition of overlying conglomerate and sandstone.

The profile is oriented east–west, with longitudes increasing from 100°E on the left to 120°E on the right and the ocean labeled on the far right; the leftward arrows show air moving from the ocean toward the land, and the cloud and rain symbols over the eastern highlands show that this moist air is being lifted and precipitating. Wind direction is defined as the direction from which the wind comes, so air moving toward the west originates from the east. At about 40°N in East Asia, the moist onshore flow from the Pacific is the summer monsoon, which blows from the southeast. Final answer: a southeast wind (from the southeast).

The figure contains four pie charts comparing relocation motivations for the enterprise overall, enterprise headquarters, production departments, and R&D departments, with a legend showing dark gray for policy factors, cross-hatch for strategic factors, white for economic factors, and diagonal pattern for emotional factors. In the “企业总部” (enterprise headquarters) chart, the largest segment is the white one, which corresponds to economic factors according to the legend. Since Shanghai’s strong economic development is also highlighted, this visual dominance indicates that economic factors are the primary motivation for headquarters locating there. Final answer: economic factors.

The left figure shows a west coast at 120°W between 30°N and 40°N, placing Jia on the western coast of North America in a Mediterranean climate zone, while the right figure shows an east coast at 150°E between about 23.5°S and 35°S, placing Yi on the eastern coast of Australia in a humid subtropical/east-coast climate zone. In the Mediterranean climate of Jia, the subtropical high shifts southward in local winter, allowing mid-latitude westerlies to bring moisture, so the rainy season is winter. In the humid subtropical climate of Yi, summer land-sea thermal contrast and moist onshore flow bring the heaviest rainfall, so the rainy season is summer. Because Jia’s rain falls in local winter and Yi’s rain falls in local summer, their rainy periods occur in opposite seasons. Final answer: different. Jia has winter rain, while Yi has summer rain.

The left image shows Q land located on the southeastern outskirts of the city, adjacent to the “大学城” (university town) and “科研所” (research institute), separated from the industrial zones and in a relatively clean-air area according to the SO₂ concentration map on the right. Urban land-use planning principles hold that high-tech industries benefit from proximity to universities and research institutions for talent, technology, and information exchange, and they require a clean environment away from heavy-polluting industrial districts. Because Q land is directly next to an educational and scientific-research cluster and lies in a low-SO₂-concentration zone, it is best suited for a functional zone that can leverage these advantages. Final answer: 高新技术产业园区 (high-tech industrial park / high-tech industrial zone).

The figure plots noon solar altitude against day length, with point P located at a day length clearly longer than 12 hours and a noon solar altitude of about 70°. For Beijing at roughly 40°N, the summer-solstice noon solar altitude is about 90° − |40° − 23.5°| ≈ 73.5° and the day length is about 15 hours, so P’s position matches the summer season in the Northern Hemisphere. In summer, Beijing is under the influence of the monsoon and often experiences hot, humid, and rainy conditions with frequent thunderstorms. Final answer: hot and rainy weather, often with thunderstorms.

The dashed curves are phreatic-water-level contours marked 23, 24, and 25; the river channel lies next to the 23 contour, so the groundwater level beside the river is lower than the surrounding 24 and 25 levels. Groundwater flows from higher head to lower head, perpendicular to the contours, so it moves from the 25 and 24 zones toward the 23 river, meaning groundwater discharges into the river and the stream is a gaining stream. A river continuously fed by groundwater in this way is typical of a humid region such as the middle Yangtze valley, and among major Chinese cities Wuhan lies on the Yangtze in such an area, so the river is most likely near Wuhan. Final answer: 武汉

The shaded region is night, the straight line separating day and night is the terminator, and point A lies on the polar circle, so the figure shows a solstice. The polar circle is at 66.5° latitude, which equals 90° minus the 23.5° obliquity of the ecliptic. Because the terminator is perpendicular to the incoming solar rays, the angle it makes with the equator (the 0° line) equals the polar-circle latitude. Therefore α = 90° − 23.5° = 66.5°, i.e. 66°34′. Final answer: 66.5° (66°34′).

The map shows four production centers in successive eras: a in the 1960s–70s near 0°E and 40°N, representing Western Europe; b in the 1970s–80s near 130°–140°E and 30°–40°N, representing Japan; c in the 1980s–90s near 110°–120°E and 20°–30°N, representing coastal China; and d after 2003 near 100°–110°E and 10°–20°N, representing Southeast Asia. The solid arrows show the industry moving stepwise from west to east and then southward over time, while the dashed arrows show products being shipped back toward earlier centers and markets. This sequential relocation from developed to developing regions is driven by the search for cheaper labor and lower land costs, which is characteristic of labor-intensive light industry. Among common industrial sectors, the textile/garment industry best fits this pattern, because it repeatedly shifts to lower-cost locations and exports products to earlier markets, whereas capital-intensive heavy industry or high-tech electronics would not match the same spatial-temporal path. Final answer: the textile industry (labor-intensive textile/garment industry).

In the diagram, place A lies due south of place B and is in sunlight, while the northern slope and valley behind the ridge are in shadow, so the noon Sun must be coming from the south. On December 22 the Sun’s declination is about 23.5°S, and in the Northern Hemisphere the noon Sun is in the south with altitude H = 90° − (latitude + 23.5°). The extensive shaded region shows the ridge casts a long shadow across the valley onto the opposite slope, which requires a fairly low noon Sun angle; this corresponds to a mid-latitude Northern Hemisphere location rather than the tropics. Solving for a low Sun angle gives a latitude around 40°N. Final answer: near 40°N.

The schematic shows the Western Pacific subtropical high ridge line located near 15°N, between the 10°N and 20°N parallels, which corresponds to the spring position of the ridge; in spring, eastern China experiences the Qingming rainy period and spring rains that fall while plum blossoms are blooming. Among the four verses, ① (Qingming rain) and ④ (fine rain wetting plum blossoms) describe spring precipitation, while ② refers to the early-summer plum-rain season and ③ refers to autumn rain. Arranging the two spring verses by their stem numbers gives ① first and ④ second. Final answer: ④ Clear breeze and fine rain wet the plum blossoms.

The image shows the sun low on the horizon at 05:50, which is sunrise time, and the photographer is facing the rising sun. Because the sun rises in the east, and a 05:50 sunrise at Huangshan occurs around late spring or early summer when the sunrise point is slightly north of due east, the sun is located to the east, roughly northeast, of the photographer. Final answer: east (approximately northeast).

The diagram shows an ecological agriculture circulation model containing a natural forest area, a biogas pond, a biochemical pond, a water source area, and three interconnected nodes (a, b, c), with arrows indicating that domestic sewage and production wastewater are channeled into the biochemical/biogas ponds for treatment rather than flowing directly into the water source area. Because the model intercepts and treats these wastes before they reach the water source, its main ecological effect on water sources is to protect the water source and reduce water pollution. Final answer: protect water sources and reduce water pollution.

The image shows four temperature-and-precipitation charts labeled 甲 (A), 乙 (B), 丙 (C), and 丁 (D). Rice needs a long warm growing season with monthly temperatures above about 20 °C and abundant rainfall, especially in summer. Chart A has hot summers but dry summers/winter rain, so it lacks summer moisture. Chart B stays mild and has only moderate, evenly distributed rain, so it is too cool and not wet enough. Chart C has a hot summer and a summer rainfall peak, but its winters are very cold and its total rainfall is lower. Chart D has hot summers, a long warm season, and the heaviest summer rainfall, giving the hot, wet conditions rice needs most. Final answer: D (丁).

The graph shows that from 1990 to 2008 both China’s imported iron ore volume (bars) and the share of pig iron production relying on imported ore (line) rose sharply, with the share climbing from about 10% to roughly 50%, indicating growing external dependence on steel raw materials. To cope with this rising dependence, reasonable responses include boosting domestic supply, improving resource utilization, and diversifying import sources; expanding steel production scale would increase iron ore demand and further raise reliance on imports, making it an unreasonable measure. Final answer: steel production scale.

The map shows the Guangxi Xijiang shipping trunk line running from the upper reaches near Baise and Tianyang in the west to the lower reaches near Guiping in the east, passing through cities such as Nanning, Guigang, and Hengxian; the lower Xijiang River area corresponds to the downstream, eastern portion of the trunk line, where the river enters a relatively flat plain and flood risk is elevated. In lower river reaches, flood control relies mainly on containing floodwaters within the channel and increasing conveyance capacity, so an standard effective measure is to strengthen or build river embankments (levees) and dredge the channel. Final answer: Strengthen river embankments (or build levees/dikes; or dredge the river channel).

The map shows the Xijiang shipping trunk line running eastward through Guangxi, with the lower Xijiang River area lying in the relatively flat eastern/downstream section near Guigang and Guiping, where slow river flow and concentrated rainfall make flooding a recurring risk. In a river’s lower reaches, where the gradient is gentle and discharge capacity is limited, an effective flood-control strategy is to increase the river’s ability to convey floodwater and to contain it within its banks; this is commonly done by constructing or reinforcing flood-control embankments (levees) and by dredging/widening the river channel. These measures directly reduce overflow onto surrounding lowlands in the lower Xijiang River area. Final answer: Construct/reinforce flood-control embankments (levees) and dredge/widen the river channel.

The graph shows two time series from 1900 to 1990: cloud cover, read on the left axis in percent, and annual temperature range, read on the right axis in degrees Celsius. The solid line, which matches the left axis, rises from about 47% around 1900 to roughly 60% by 1980, so cloud cover increases over the period. The dashed line, which matches the right axis, falls from about 14.2°C around 1900 to about 13.7°C by 1980, so the annual temperature range becomes smaller. Greater cloud cover implies more moisture and overcast conditions, while a smaller annual temperature range indicates reduced seasonal extremes, that is, a milder or warmer climate. Therefore, the country’s climate is trending toward warm and humid conditions. Final answer: warm and humid

The image shows a simplified map of southern Africa and Madagascar with six numbered locations: ① on the East African plateau just north of the equator, ② in the equatorial Congo Basin, ③ in the southern African interior, ④ on the southwest coast, ⑤ on the Mozambique side, and ⑥ on the east coast of Madagascar. Natural zones normally follow latitudinal zonal patterns controlled by heat and moisture belts, yet local factors such as elevation, ocean currents, wind direction, and topography can produce non-zonal disturbances. Location ① is near the equator where lowland areas would normally support tropical rainforest, but the high elevation of the East African Plateau lowers temperature and reduces convectional rainfall, producing savanna instead. Location ⑥ lies at about 20°–25°S, outside the equatorial rainforest belt, yet moist southeastern trade winds rise against Madagascar’s eastern mountain slopes and create a localized tropical rainforest zone. Because these two sites show the clearest deviations from the expected latitudinal pattern, the two places most strongly disturbed by non-zonal factors are ① and ⑥. Final answer: ①⑥

The image shows place B (乙) with the sun directly overhead at noon, while place D (丁) has its noon sun to the south and sunrise/sunset Beijing times of 4:40 (northeast) and 1:20 (northwest). Because B’s sun is overhead, B is at the subsolar point; D’s noon sun is south, so D lies north of the subsolar point, meaning B is south of D. For east-west position, D’s local noon in Beijing time is the midpoint of its sunrise and sunset: treating the 1:20 sunset as the next day’s 25:20 gives (4:40 + 25:20)/2 = 15:00. B’s sunrise and sunset are due east and due west, indicating a 12-hour day, so its local noon is about 12:00 Beijing time. Since B reaches noon earlier than D, B is east of D. Therefore, B is located to the southeast of D. Final answer: to the southeast of D.

The map shows January temperature-anomaly contours across Eurasia; point A appears to lie on or near the 0 °C anomaly contour in western Europe, while point B lies within the –8 °C anomaly region in eastern Asia, and the two points are at the same latitude. Since temperature anomaly = local temperature – average temperature at that latitude, the average temperature for this latitude is 5 °C – 0 °C = 5 °C. Therefore, B’s January average temperature is 5 °C + (–8 °C) = –3 °C. Final answer: –3 °C.

The right-hand map shows sea-surface isotherms of 22 °C, 20 °C and 18 °C from top to bottom; because temperature decreases toward the bottom of the map, the bottom is the poleward (south) side, placing the scene in the Southern Hemisphere. At point ② the isotherms bend toward the equator (northward), which indicates a cold current flowing from higher latitudes toward lower latitudes. In the Southern Hemisphere Atlantic Ocean, the major cold current is the Benguela Current. Final answer: Benguela Current.

The figure plots seismic-wave velocity versus depth, with the left curve being the S-wave (横波) and the right curve the P-wave (纵波); both speeds increase with depth, and at a depth near the 15 km focus the P-wave speed is roughly 8 km/s while the S-wave speed is roughly 4 km/s (exact values are uncertain from the small graph, but they lie between the labeled endpoint values). The early-warning time equals the extra time the slower S-wave needs to reach the surface after the faster P-wave has already arrived at the seismic network, so Δt = t_S − t_P = h/v_S − h/v_P. Using h = 15 km and representative speeds v_P ≈ 8 km/s and v_S ≈ 4 km/s gives t_P ≈ 15/8 ≈ 1.9 s and t_S ≈ 15/4 ≈ 3.8 s, so Δt ≈ 1.9 s; using the endpoint values 7.6 km/s and 4.2 km/s gives Δt ≈ 15/4.2 − 15/7.6 ≈ 1.6 s. Thus the system gained about 2 s. Final answer: about 2 seconds.

The graph shows monthly inflow as a solid line and outflow as a dashed line, with the inflow curve rising above the outflow curve in spring, remaining above it through the summer peaks, and then dropping below the outflow curve after about September. A reservoir’s stored water increases whenever inflow exceeds outflow and decreases whenever outflow exceeds inflow, so the maximum storage occurs at the last month when inflow is still at least equal to outflow before a sustained deficit. Because the inflow line stays above the outflow line from roughly March–April until September and falls below it afterward, water accumulates throughout that period and the stored volume reaches its highest level in September. Final answer: September.

The cross-section shows folded sedimentary strata with labels 甲, 乙, and 丙; at 丙 the rock layers are cut by a near-vertical discontinuity, and the same layers on the two sides do not match because the right-hand block has dropped downward relative to the left-hand block. In geology, a fracture in the crust along which rock bodies have moved relative to each other is called a fault, so the structure at 丙 is best interpreted as a fault. Final answer: a fault.

The bar chart shows the percentage shares of six input costs—wages, fuel, raw materials, freight, technology, and other—for three factory types labeled Jia, Yi, and Bing; for Jia, the tallest bar is in the raw-materials category, accounting for about 40% of total inputs, which is larger than its shares in wages, fuel, freight, technology, and other costs. In industrial classification by dominant location/input factor, a factory whose costs are dominated by raw materials is classified as a raw-material-oriented industry. Final answer: raw-material-oriented industry.

In the profile, the horizontal axis is centered on the mountain crest, with the left side representing the south slope and the right side the north slope; the wind arrow points from left (south) to right (north), so the south slope is windward and the north slope is leeward. The precipitation curve is clearly higher on the left/south slope and lower on the right/north slope, and the altitude curve shows the south slope is long and gentle while the north slope is short and steep. This combination—a gentle, rainier south slope and a steep, drier north slope—matches the well-known geomorphology and climate pattern of the Qinling Mountains, where the south-facing slope receives moisture from the summer monsoon and the north-facing slope lies in a rain shadow. Final answer: the Qinling Mountains.

The left map shows region J located in the subtropical arid zone of the Arabian Peninsula, an area dominated by persistent subtropical high pressure and dry trade winds that produce very low rainfall and high evaporation; these climatic controls lead to sparse vegetation and a widespread desert environment, so the large-area natural landscape is tropical desert. Final answer: tropical desert (tropical desert landscape).

The diagram illustrates the atmospheric greenhouse effect with numbered arrows representing different energy transfers. The arrow originating from the sun and directed toward Earth's atmosphere is labeled ①, which corresponds to solar radiation entering the Earth-atmosphere system. In standard atmospheric energy-balance diagrams, solar radiation is the incoming shortwave radiation from the sun, and it is conventionally assigned the first code in the sequence. Final answer: ①

In the schematic of the atmospheric heat-preservation effect, the arrow that goes from the atmosphere back toward the ground is the atmospheric counter-radiation (大气逆辐射), and this arrow is labeled with the numerical code ③. Final answer: ③

The left graph shows the sun’s altitude reaching 90° at 60°W, and the right graph shows it reaching 90° at 15°S, so the subsolar point is at (15°S, 60°W). Because Buenos Aires lies on the 60°W meridian (33°S, 60°W), it is experiencing local solar noon at this time; its noon solar altitude is H = 90° − |33° − 15°| = 72°. Final answer: solar noon (local noon, with the sun near its daily maximum altitude of about 72°).

The map shows a U.S. “preference index” distribution with four shaded classes, and Region A (labeled 甲) in the northern Great Plains is shaded for the lowest class (<50), indicating a low preference index. This area lies within the Great Plains wheat belt, where the economy is dominated by large-scale wheat farming and related agriculture, supporting a sparse population and therefore low settlement preference. Final answer: agriculture (wheat farming).

The diagram shows a mountain cross-section at noon on December 22, with a topographic shadow zone labeled “遮蔽区” where the ridge blocks sunlight; the slopes are marked 甲, 乙, 丙, and 丁. Vegetation on a hillside protects the soil by binding it with roots, intercepting rainfall, slowing runoff, and reducing the impact of raindrops on the surface. If the hillside vegetation is excessively cut down, these protective functions are lost, so rainfall and gravity can more easily detach and transport the soil. Therefore the most likely change in this place is intensified soil erosion, along with an increased risk of landslides or debris flows. Final answer: soil erosion will intensify (and the risk of landslides/debris flows will increase).

In the left figure, place A lies in the ocean immediately beside the shaded land, where the isotherms show 21°C closer to A and 25°C farther offshore, and the 21°C isotherm bulges outward into the warmer 25°C water. The rule for interpreting ocean currents from isotherms is that a cold current carries colder water into warmer water, making the lower-temperature isotherm bulge toward the higher-temperature region, while a warm current does the opposite. Because the 21°C isotherm extends toward the warmer 25°C offshore water, the current at A is transporting cold water into warm water. This is also consistent with the location of A on the right-hand world map along the west coast of North America, where the California Current is a cold current. Final answer: cold current

In the figure, AB is a latitude line and BC is a meridian, so they meet at a right angle at B, and C is on the equator at (0°, 30°W). Since ∠BAC = 70°, the remaining angle ∠BCA is 20°. At the equator, the angle between the terminator and a meridian equals the sun’s declination, so the sun is about 20° south of the equator. Because A is in the Northern Hemisphere and the sun is exactly on the horizon at local noon, A lies on the polar-night boundary; using the noon solar-altitude relation 0° = 90° − φ + δ gives A’s latitude as φ = 90° + δ ≈ 90° − 20° = 70°N. Final answer: A is experiencing polar night, with 0 hours of daylight and 24 hours of night.

The figure plots time on the horizontal axis and railway network length on the vertical axis, with the upper curve DL representing the length of railway network needed for economic development and the lower curve SL representing the length already built; the shaded vertical distance between DL and SL is the supply-demand gap, calculated as DL − SL. From the origin to about T3, DL rises faster than SL, so the gap widens; around T3, DL reaches its peak and then begins to decline, while SL continues to increase, causing the gap between DL and SL to shrink in the interval from T3 to T4. Because a smaller gap means less shortage of railway capacity relative to demand, the contradiction between railway transport supply and demand is somewhat eased during this period. Final answer: the T3–T4 stage.

On the contour topographic map of the Zhuzhou area, the Xiang River flows northward through the region, which in this local map appears as a flow from the lower-right toward the upper-left; because rivers carry pollutants downstream, any contamination detected at point R must originate from an upstream river section. Section ④ lies upstream of R along the main river, whereas sections ① and ② are downstream and would not supply pollutants to R, and section ③ is not the upstream source for R. Therefore, the pollution source most likely comes from section ④. Final answer: ④

The diagram shows the same mountain with a south-facing slope and a north-facing slope, and at comparable elevations the two slopes carry different natural belts—for example, the south slope displays alpine meadow and scrub belts while the north slope shows mountain grassland and semi-ar saline desert steppe belts. These differences arise because the two slopes receive different amounts of solar radiation, which creates contrasting temperature and moisture conditions, so the vegetation pattern is controlled by slope aspect rather than by latitude, longitude, or altitude alone. In geographic regional differentiation, such small-scale differences caused by local terrain orientation belong to local, non-zonal differentiation. Final answer: local/non-zonal differentiation (地方性分异规律).

The map shows a small island in the Atlantic Ocean with the 45°N parallel running through it and a meridian labeled M at the top. Because the island is in the Atlantic at about 45°N, it lies in the Western Hemisphere, and the mid-latitude western Atlantic near this parallel is centered near 60°W (the longitude of the Newfoundland/Nova Scotia region). Therefore the meridian M is most likely about 60°W. Final answer: 60°W.

The map shows a closed high-pressure system (anticyclone) over the North Pacific, with isobars increasing toward center A to 1027 hPa; the center lies near about 50°N, 145°W. In an anticyclone, air subsides (descends), and the eastern part of the system is the region east of the pressure center. Among the labeled points, point ③ is located on the eastern flank of the high, east of 150°W and within the high-pressure field, whereas ① and ② lie on the northern/western sides and ④ lies on the southern side. Therefore, the region affected by descending airflow in the eastern part of this system is point ③. Final answer: ③

The image shows the subtropical high located over the western Pacific southeast of China, with warm moist airflow on its northwestern side meeting cold air from the north and producing a frontal rain belt over central-eastern China around the middle-lower Yangtze River region. Because the main frontal rain belt is usually 5–8 degrees of latitude north of the subtropical-high ridge line, the rain belt’s position over the Yangtze valley places the ridge near 20–25°N, which is the typical latitude of the subtropical high during the Meiyu season. The subtropical high advances to about this latitude in June–July, so the configuration in the figure corresponds to that period. Final answer: June–July (6–7月).

The left image shows the east-facing rock-cut façade of Abu Simbel, and the upper right figure shows the inner sanctuary where a narrow beam of sunlight strikes the stone statue of Ramesses II. During the Sun Festival the rising sun aligns with the temple’s eastward axis; because the sun rises in the east and then moves southward across the sky, the projected sunbeam inside the sanctuary sweeps horizontally across the statues from left to right. Therefore, the sunlight shining on the Ramesses II statue moves from left to right. Final answer: from left to right.

The table shows Shanghai with a birth rate of 7.05‰ and a natural growth rate of 1.98‰, while Beijing has a birth rate of 7.48‰ and a natural growth rate of 3.07‰. Using the formula natural growth rate = birth rate − death rate, Shanghai’s death rate is 7.05‰ − 1.98‰ = 5.07‰ and Beijing’s death rate is 7.48‰ − 3.07‰ = 4.41‰. Shanghai’s natural growth is 1.09‰ lower than Beijing’s, caused by a birth rate that is 0.43‰ lower and a death rate that is 0.66‰ higher, so the larger influence is Shanghai’s higher death rate, which mainly reflects an older population structure. Final answer: Shanghai’s higher death rate (population aging).

In the graph, the dashed groundwater-level line rises to a peak around late spring/early summer and then declines throughout period M, which spans roughly the summer into early autumn; during this same interval the solid temperature line is high and the precipitation bars show the main rainy season, so natural recharge from rainfall should tend to raise the water table. Because groundwater level change depends on the balance between recharge (infiltration from precipitation) and discharge (evaporation, runoff, and human withdrawal), a falling water table during the wet season means discharge exceeds recharge. In this temperate monsoon region of China, summer is the crop-growing season when agricultural irrigation withdraws large amounts of groundwater, so the decline in period M is mainly driven by human activity rather than by natural climate factors. Final answer: human activities, mainly agricultural irrigation.

The cross-section shows a low-relief landscape whose terrain rises only to about 500 m, with a broad central lake and low hills on either side; the 8 o’clock isotherms give a surface temperature near 18 °C and slope upward toward the east, indicating warmer air aloft over the eastern side, while the upper-air flow is a weak westerly of 20 km/h. A morning temperature of about 18 °C in mid-latitude summer together with such weak westerlies is characteristic of the subtropical monsoon zone in eastern China, and the low elevation rules out the Tibetan Plateau, Sichuan Basin, and Loess Plateau. The combination of a large lake set in a low plain below 500 m therefore matches the middle–lower Yangtze River plain, where large freshwater lakes such as Taihu or Poyang occur. Final answer: the middle and lower reaches of the Yangtze River plain (长江中下游平原).

AB is tangent to the 80°N parallel, so the sun’s declination is about 10°N (because 90° – δ = 80°). CND is an equal-solar-altitude line passing through the North Pole N and is symmetric about the central meridian NM; at the pole the solar altitude equals the declination, so CND is the 10° solar-altitude line, centered on the subsolar point with an angular radius of 90° – 10° = 80°. Its intersections C and D with the equator are therefore about 80° west and east of the subsolar meridian, with D on the east (right) side. At 9:00 Beijing time (120°E), the 12:00 subsolar meridian lies 45° farther east, at 165°E, so D is roughly 165°E + 80° ≈ 245°E and its local solar time is about 12:00 + 80°/15° ≈ 17:20. Final answer: 17:20 (about 5:20 PM).

The pie chart shows an energy consumption structure composed of coal, firewood, crop stalks, oil, and electricity, in which crop stalks and firewood together account for a large share. Crop stalks and firewood are biomass resources that would normally decompose and return organic matter to the soil; when they are burned as fuel instead, the soil receives less organic matter. This reduction in organic matter lowers soil fertility, decreases soil aggregate stability, and can lead to soil erosion. Final answer: decreased soil fertility (or soil organic matter reduction/soil erosion).

The table lists 2009 data for countries 甲, 乙, and 丙, including population growth rate, elderly population share, infant mortality rate, urban population share, and per capita energy consumption. The left figure explains the wind-direction symbols, and the right-hand map shows closed isobars with M at the center of a low-pressure cell while P lies in a separate small high-pressure cell; the wind vane on the eastern side of the map is consistent with air flowing into the low at M. Air moves from high pressure toward low pressure, and in a low-pressure center the rising air expands and cools, condensing water vapor and producing clouds and rain, whereas N and ① are in outer or high-pressure areas where sinking or diverging air suppresses precipitation. Therefore, the place most likely to have rainy weather is M. Final answer: M.

In graph B (the upper-right panel labeled 乙), the precipitation curve stays very low all year, with a small summer peak of only about 20–25 mm per month, while the evaporation curve is consistently higher than precipitation and also peaks in summer; the total annual precipitation is far less than the annual potential evaporation. This pattern of extremely low, summer-concentrated rainfall and a large moisture deficit indicates an arid/semi-arid climate, and the strong seasonal evaporation cycle with low winter values places it in the mid-latitude dry zone rather than the tropics. Final answer: temperate continental climate (temperate desert/steppe climate).

The map shows contour lines labeled 300 m, 500 m, 700 m, and 900 m, with a dashed highway passing through the four labeled points 甲, 乙, 丙, and 丁. On a contour map, higher contour values mean higher ground, so a point located on or closer to a higher-numbered contour has a higher altitude. 甲 and 乙 are in the western part of the route near the 300 m contour, giving them altitudes of about 300 m. 丙 is near a small closed contour next to the 500 m line, but the road at 丙 lies on the outer, lower side of that closure, so its elevation is below 500 m. 丁 is on the eastern section of the highway right beside the 500 m contour, so its altitude is about 500 m, higher than the other three points. Table 2 shows that Hubei begins its grain harvest on May 18, while Jilin begins on July 13, indicating that Hubei has an earlier and longer growing season. Based on regional agricultural knowledge, Hubei lies in the warmer middle-lower Yangtze plain, where conditions support multiple cropping and higher annual grain output per mu; Jilin, in the cooler Northeast, has a shorter frost-free period and mainly single cropping, resulting in a lower average yield per mu. The diagram shows that box 乙 is produced by “冬季风强盛” (strong winter monsoon) and then feeds into box 丙, which is linked to “接近沙源地” and “人口城市密集.” In China, a strong winter monsoon outbreak is the classic cause of a cold wave (寒潮), and such strong cold winds can also help trigger dust/sandstorms in arid and semi-arid regions. Therefore, the meteorological disaster represented by 乙 is a cold wave. Final answer: 寒潮 (cold wave).

The figure is a side-view circle representing Earth, with center O, the vertical line as the Earth’s axis (north upward), the horizontal line as the equator, and the straight line L passing through O as the terminator. A point on the terminator is either at sunrise (~6:00) or sunset (~18:00) local solar time. In Jakarta (6°S) the noon shadow points north, so the Sun at noon lies north of that latitude, indicating the subsolar point is in the Northern Hemisphere and the North Pole side of the diagram is in daylight. Since the North Pole lies above line L, the region above L is day and the region below L is night; Earth rotates eastward, so a point at O moving eastward leaves the day side and enters the night side, placing O on the evening terminator. Therefore the local solar time at O is 18:00. Final answer: 18:00.

The figure shows the North Pole P, the 30°N latitude arc, and the terminator cutting that parallel at M (morning) and N (evening); PY is the 0° meridian and the marked angles ∠MPX and ∠NPY are each 7.5°. Taking X and Y as the terminator’s intersections with the equator, the daylight longitude span along 30°N is 180° − 7.5° − 7.5° = 165°. Since Earth rotates 15° of longitude per hour, the day length at 30°N is 165° ÷ 15° = 11 h, which is shorter than the 12 h equinox day, so the Sun is south of the equator and the Northern Hemisphere is in winter. In winter, Zhejiang is mainly affected by the Siberian cold high-pressure system. Final answer: Zhejiang is likely under the influence of the Siberian cold high (cold anticyclone), i.e., the cold, dry winter monsoon.

The map spans approximately 105°E–120°E and 25°N–40°N and is divided by dashed boundaries into six numbered regions; the roughly east-west dashed line near 34°N represents the Qinling–Huaihe boundary between the temperate zone to the north and the subtropical zone to the south, and its western part is the rugged Qinling–Daba mountain area.
