The map shows the western part of Australia between about 120°E–130°E and 20°S–30°S, where location ④ lies on the southwest coast; the wind arrows in the north blow from the northwest toward the southeast, indicating the summer northwest monsoon over northern Australia, so the season is summer. Location ④ has a Mediterranean climate, which in summer is controlled by the subtropical high-pressure belt (subtropical anticyclone) rather than by the winter westerlies, producing hot, dry conditions. Final answer: the subtropical high-pressure belt (subtropical anticyclone).

The bar chart gives day-arc degrees of about 220° for Beijing, 162.5° for ①, and 140° for ②. For a given solar declination δ, day arc A and latitude φ are related by cos(A/2) = –tan φ tan δ; an arc above 180° means the place is in the summer hemisphere, an arc below 180° means it is in the winter hemisphere, and the farther the arc is from 180°, the higher the absolute latitude. Beijing’s arc is 220° = 180° + 40°, ②’s arc is 140° = 180° – 40°, and ①’s arc is 162.5° = 180° – 17.5°. Because Beijing and ② deviate equally from the 180° equatorial arc (40°) but in opposite hemispheres, they have the same absolute latitude, while ① deviates less and therefore has the lowest latitude. Final answer: Beijing = ② > ①.

The diagram shows five tourism route patterns labeled M1–M5 radiating from a central “客源地” (tourist source). In a single-destination pattern, tourists leave the source, visit only one destination, and then return. M1 is the only pattern that connects the source to a single destination by a bidirectional (two-way) path, with no additional destinations or loops. M2–M5 all involve multiple destinations arranged as loops or chains. Therefore, the route that matches the single-destination pattern is M1. Final answer: M1

The diagram displays five tourism route patterns (M1–M5) around a central source market; M2 is a closed, directed loop of four destination nodes with one arrow connecting the source to a node on that loop. A complete circuit tour pattern is defined as an itinerary that leaves the source, visits multiple destinations along a closed loop, and returns to the source without retracing. M1 is a hub-and-spoke pattern, M3 is a linear chain, M5 is a single-destination round trip, and M4 is a smaller loop; among these, M2 best fits the complete circuit because it forms a single closed circuit linking several destinations. Final answer: M2.

In the diagram, arrows show that waste from food processing, manure from poultry such as贵妃鸡、山鸡、孔雀 and 野兔, and straw from grasses such as 黑麦草 and 玉米草 are all directed into a 沼气池 (biogas digester); the biogas digester then produces 沼气 (biogas/methane), which is used for lighting, cooking, and keeping chicks warm, while the remaining 沼液 and 沼渣 are applied as fertilizer to fruit trees including 百香果、核桃 and 红心蜜柚. Therefore, these organic wastes are used as raw materials for anaerobic digestion in the biogas digester to produce biogas energy and nutrient-rich residue for fertilizing crops. Final answer: They are put into a biogas digester to produce biogas for lighting, cooking, and keeping chicks warm, and the resulting biogas slurry/residue is used as fertilizer for fruit trees and grass.

In the left schematic, point A (甲) lies inside the shaded zone between roughly 10°N–15°N and 75°W–80°W, on the western side of a slanted boundary that represents a mountain range, while the unshaded zone lies to the east. Moist air is carried by the prevailing northeast trade winds from the Caribbean Sea, so the eastern windward slopes receive abundant rainfall, whereas the western leeward side—where A is located—is in a rain shadow and much drier. Therefore, the climate zone near A is controlled mainly by topography, specifically the rain-shadow effect of the mountains, together with the direction of the northeast trade winds. Final answer: topography (mountain rain shadow) and the northeast trade winds.

The image shows several soil mounds in an open area with patches of accumulated snow remaining on one side of each mound, and the snow has not been disturbed by human activity. Handan City lies in the Northern Hemisphere, so during the first lunar month (winter/early spring) the sun is in the southern part of the sky; consequently, north-facing slopes receive less direct solar radiation and remain cooler, causing snow to melt more slowly there than on south-facing slopes. Therefore, the remaining snow in the photo is on the north-facing sides of the mounds. Because the photographer is viewing these north-facing, snow-covered slopes, the camera must be located on the south side of the mounds and pointing toward the north. Final answer: from south to north (northward).

In Figure A the river runs from the higher ground near P, which is located on a contour line, toward the lower-lying lake to the south, so the water moves from P toward the lake. The geological cross-section in Figure B shows the valley at P is asymmetric, with a steep, eroded west bank and a gentler east bank. Because the Coriolis force deflects flowing water to the right in the Northern Hemisphere, the eroded bank is the right bank when looking downstream; for the west bank to be the right bank, the river must be flowing toward the south. Final answer: from north to south.

The diagram shows a closed circulation with the near-ground branch running from a to b, the upward branch from b to c, the upper branch from c to d, and the downward branch from d to a, forming a clockwise cell. In the mid-latitude (Ferrel) cell of the three-cell circulation, the near-ground flow moves from the subtropical high-pressure belt toward the subpolar low-pressure belt, so a lies near 30° latitude under the subtropical high and b near 60° latitude. The descending air at a (d→a) produces dry, high-pressure conditions, while the surface flow a→b corresponds to the mid-latitude westerlies; on the west coast of continents in the 30°–40° latitude belt this alternating control creates a Mediterranean climate. Final answer: Mediterranean climate.

Place 2 has a January data point (square) at about 0 °C and roughly 100 mm of precipitation, and a July data point (triangle) at about 10 °C and roughly 150 mm of precipitation, so it shows a small annual temperature range and year-round moisture with no dry season, indicating a temperate maritime/oceanic climate; the typical natural vegetation for this climate type is temperate deciduous forest. Final answer: temperate deciduous forest

The left graph plots 商品房均价 (average commercial housing price) from the Han River, across the Yangtze River, toward the southeast. The figure shows a straight tunnel with sunlight entering along its axis and reaching the statue at the far end, so the sun must align with the tunnel on only two days of the year. The graph shows monthly solar radiation; place N receives essentially zero radiation from roughly October through February, rises steeply in spring, peaks near June–July at about 1100 cal/(cm²·day), and falls back to zero by October. This pattern of a long winter polar night and a summer peak around the June solstice is characteristic of high northern latitudes. Final answer: the North Pole (Arctic region).

According to the map, Shanghai is densely marked with symbols for investment companies and R&D centers, indicating a concentration of capital and technological innovation functions in the city. Multinational petrochemical enterprises are attracted to Shanghai because it serves as the economic, financial, and technological center of the Yangtze River Delta, providing superior access to capital, advanced technology, market information, and high-level talent. In the figure, climate type Jia has the highest annual precipitation, about 1450 mm, and the highest monthly mean temperatures, with the temperature range spanning roughly 13 °C to 25 °C; this makes Jia the warmest and wettest of the four types, characteristic of a southern subtropical monsoon city. Because the figure itself does not label cities, the exact match depends on the provided city list, but in the standard set of options for this type of question Jia corresponds to the warmest, wettest city, Guangzhou. The figure shows four curves plotted against years from 1950 to 2010, with the vertical axis labeled for both urban population (hundred millions) and urbanization level (%). The map shows a large central and northwestern area marked as the arid/semi-arid vegetation belt, while humid vegetation belts occur along the eastern and southern margins closer to the ocean. This central belt lies deep within the continent, far from maritime moisture sources, so oceanic air masses lose most of their moisture before reaching the interior, producing dry conditions. A linear mountain that is crossed east of M on the east–west line and north of M on the south–north line must connect those two intercepts, so its strike runs from northwest to southeast. The profile runs along 38°N from about 110°E to 115°E, showing 乙 as a higher western inland area and 甲 as a lower eastern plain near the Bohai Sea; this east–west moisture gradient makes the eastern side wetter and the western side drier. The diagram uses the horizontal axis for noon solar altitude and the vertical axis for two months A and B within April–August, with A earlier than B; at month A the altitudes read from the x-axis are about 0° for place ①, 60° for places ② and ③, and 90° for place ④, while from A to B place ② rises, place ③ falls, place ④ falls, and place ① stays near 0°. Using the relation H = 90° − |φ − δ|, a 90° altitude means place ④ lies on the subsolar latitude at month A; a 60° altitude means places ② and ③ are 30° north and south of that subsolar latitude; and a 0° altitude means place ① is 90° away on the far southern side. Because the period is April to August and A is the earlier month, the sun’s declination shifts northward overall, so the place whose altitude increases (②) is north of the subsolar point and the place whose altitude decreases (③) is south of it. Therefore the latitudes increase from south to north as ①, ③, ④, ②. Final answer: ①③④②.

The map shows Diaoyu Island as a small, steep island at about 25°44′N, 123°28′E, surrounded by the sea and marked by closely spaced contour lines that indicate rugged, sloping terrain with a central upland of several hundred metres; this setting exposes vegetation to strong winds, salt spray, thin rocky soils, and rapid drainage. Under these stressful coastal-island conditions, plants typically develop morphological adaptations such as low, dwarfed or prostrate growth to resist wind, small and thick leathery leaves with a thick cuticle to reduce water loss and salt damage, and well-developed root systems to anchor in shallow soil. Final answer: The plants on Diaoyu Island are generally short and stunted, with small, thick, leathery leaves and strong root systems, showing wind-resistant and drought-tolerant morphology.

Place A (labeled 甲) lies on the eastern coast of South America in low latitudes near 20°S, facing the Atlantic Ocean and on the windward side of the Brazilian Highlands. Its climate is a humid tropical rainforest climate produced by the combined effects of its low-latitude position, the onshore southeast trade winds, orographic lifting on the coastal mountain slopes, and the warming and moistening Brazil Warm Current. Final answer: low-latitude location, onshore southeast trade winds, windward slope of the coastal mountains, and the Brazil Warm Current.

The map shows four villages connected by dashed-line roads across a contoured landscape. The village labeled 乙 sits at the intersection of two roads, giving it greater accessibility than the others, which lie on only one road or at road ends; the contour lines around 乙 are also the most widely spaced, indicating the flattest, most buildable site, and it lies near the river valley that runs through the region. Because commercial and trade centers tend to develop where transport routes meet, flat land is available, and a water supply is close, 乙 has the best location to serve the largest surrounding area. Final answer: 乙村 (Village 乙).

The graph shows two dates (M and N) when the noon sun is directly overhead (90°), so the place lies between the two tropics; on day H the sun is due south, so H is the December solstice and the place is in the Southern Hemisphere tropics. The endpoints E and F, with a noon solar altitude of 48°, represent the June solstice; using the relation H = 90° – (φ + 23.5°) for a Southern Hemisphere latitude gives φ ≈ 18.5°S, placing the location within the Southern Hemisphere trade-wind belt. Final answer: southeast trade wind.

The schematic shows annual noon solar altitude with two peaks at M and N and a minimum at H; the problem states that on H the noon Sun is due south and that M and N are the midpoints of EH and HF. Because the noon Sun is due south at H, H represents the December solstice, so E and F represent the June solstice, and the midpoints M and N therefore represent the September and March equinoxes, respectively. For Beijing in the Northern Hemisphere, days are longer than nights from the spring equinox to the autumn equinox, and day length decreases after the summer solstice; combining these two conditions gives the interval from the summer solstice to the autumn equinox. On the diagram this interval runs from E to M. Final answer: E～M.

In the four maps the shaded precipitation band remains near 140°E, 35°–40°N, while the surrounding pressure field changes. Map ④ shows only a trough between a northwest high and a southeast high, with no closed low-pressure center, so it represents the initial trough/stationary-front stage. Map ① shows a closed low (L) in the southwest and a northeastward trough extending toward the rain band, indicating cyclogenesis. Map ② shows the low center shifted to the northeast with tightly packed isobars, marking the mature, deepened cyclone stage. Map ③ shows a strong high-pressure center dominating the central region, meaning the cyclone has moved away or filled and cold high pressure is building. Therefore the developmental sequence is ④, ①, ②, ③. Final answer: ④①②③

The graph shows solar altitude plotted against Beijing time for Jia and Yi on the Northern Hemisphere summer solstice. Jia’s solar-altitude curve reaches its maximum before 9:00 Beijing time, whereas Beijing’s own local solar noon occurs at about 12:00 Beijing time; because a place that experiences noon earlier in Beijing time lies to the east of Beijing, Jia is east of Beijing. On the summer solstice the sun is directly overhead at about 23.5°N, so Beijing’s noon solar altitude is about 90° − (40° − 23.5°) ≈ 73.5°; Jia’s peak solar altitude in the figure is lower than this, indicating a higher latitude and therefore a position north of Beijing. Thus Jia is located to the northeast of Beijing. Final answer: northeast of Beijing.

The figure shows that from 1998 to 2000 China’s cotton purchase guide price fell from 617.5 yuan/ton to 390.0 yuan/ton (a 37% drop), sown area fell from 4.459 million hectares to 4.041 million hectares (a 9% drop), and unit-area yield rose from 1,009 kg/ha to 1,093 kg/ha. The sharp decline in the government purchase price reduced farmers’ incentive to plant cotton, so less productive, low-yield cotton land was taken out of production; with the remaining area concentrated on more productive land, the average yield per unit area increased. Final answer: The main reason was that the large drop in the cotton purchase guide price caused sown area to decrease, as low-yield land was withdrawn from cotton production, raising the average yield per unit area.

The map covers roughly 45°N–50°N and 122°E–126°E, lies beneath a cold high-pressure system shown by isobars of 1025–1030 hPa, and includes a 200-day seasonal frozen-soil line, all indicating a cold region with widespread frozen ground; in such a setting, fluvial erosion is strongly modified by freeze–thaw processes, and because opposite valley sides receive different amounts of solar radiation the more sun-exposed bank thaws more, weakens, and is eroded more readily while the shaded bank stays frozen and more resistant, so the river tends to carve an asymmetric valley with one gentle bank and one steep bank. Final answer: an asymmetric river valley

The table gives planting-area changes (thousand hectares) for five major producing provinces: Hubei, Jiangsu, Hebei, Shandong, and Xinjiang. In 1980–1990, planting area rose in Hebei (+362.2), Shandong (+672.3), and Xinjiang (+254.0) while falling in Hubei and Jiangsu; in 1991–2010, Hubei (-145.5), Jiangsu (-310.3), Hebei (-644.2), and Shandong (-1051.1) all declined, and only Xinjiang increased (+560.7). Since the spatial distribution center of gravity is the area-weighted average location of production, the large losses in the eastern provinces and the continued gain in far-western Xinjiang pulled the center of gravity toward Xinjiang. Final answer: The spatial distribution center of gravity shifted toward the northwest (westward), with production concentrating increasingly in Xinjiang rather than the eastern provinces.

The graph shows annual urbanization-rate increases for China’s four major regions; during 1990–2000 the line for Ding stays at the bottom, around 0.5 percentage points per year, while the other regions rise more quickly. Ding corresponds to Northeast China, whose old industrial base was heavily affected by the 1990s state-owned enterprise reform, leading to economic slowdown and a markedly slower urbanization rate. Final answer: the state-owned enterprise reform in Northeast China (restructuring of the old industrial base).

The three circles all show the environment surrounding human society, with material/energy flowing from the environment into society and waste flowing out; the vertical arrows show the changing nature of the relationship. In diagram ③ the environment influences society and society develops the environment, representing the early stage when humans were largely subject to nature. In diagram ① both vertical arrows are labeled “development/exploitation,” representing the industrial stage when humans tried to conquer and exploit nature. In diagram ② both vertical arrows are labeled “influence,” representing the modern stage when people recognize mutual influence and seek harmony between humans and the environment. Therefore the historical evolution is ③ → ① → ②. Final answer: ③→①→②.

The figure shows two raw-material origins M1 and M2, the market N, and five possible factory sites 甲, 乙, 丙, 丁, and 戊; the concentric curves centered on each center are equal-freight lines, and the number on each line gives the freight cost for moving the corresponding raw material or finished product to that location. Final answer: 丙

In the bar chart, the group labeled 甲 shows a wheat planting area of 3100万hm², a yield of 3178 kg/hm², and a total production of 9600万吨; using the relationship total production (万吨) area (万hm²) × yield (kg/hm²) / 1000, 3100 × 3178 / 1000 ≈ 9852万吨, which is close to the chart’s 9600万吨. The bar chart gives sown area, yield, and total output for the five coded countries 甲–戊. 甲 has the greatest sown area (3100) and total output (9600), so it represents China; 戊 has the smallest sown area (50) and the highest yield, so it represents Denmark. The figure depicts the area around Yan'an at approximately 37°N and 110°E, situated on the Loess Plateau with surrounding elevations near 1000 m, rivers, and a section of the Great Wall. This region is characterized by thick, loose loess deposits and a monsoon climate with intense, concentrated summer rainfall, which produces severe water erosion and gully development. Because the ancient Great Wall in this area was largely built from rammed earth or local materials, it is easily undermined and breached by rainwash and soil erosion. Final answer: severe water erosion (or soil erosion caused by concentrated heavy rainfall).

The image shows the Orinoco River Basin located in northern South America near 10°N latitude, within the tropical zone, with the Orinoco River flowing eastward toward the Atlantic. The pie chart shows that China’s desertified land is heavily concentrated in the northwestern and northern arid/semi-arid regions: Xinjiang accounts for 40%, Inner Mongolia 24%, Tibet 16%, Qinghai 8%, and Gansu 7%, with the remaining provinces each contributing 1%. Because these areas receive little precipitation and have dry climates, the spatial pattern indicates that aridity is the controlling natural condition. Therefore, the decisive factor in the development of desertification is the lack of water/precipitation, or drought. Final answer: aridity (drought/lack of precipitation).

The cross sections show the river changing from a steep, narrow, coniferous-forested valley at A, through a broadleaf-forested valley at B, to a broad lowland valley with paddy fields at C, so the river flows from A toward C. In these sections the right-hand bank, when facing downstream, is the steep, eroded side with older strata exposed, whereas the left-hand bank is gentler and carries newer deposits or cultivated land. Because the Coriolis effect in the Northern Hemisphere deflects flowing water toward the right bank, producing erosion on the right bank and deposition on the left bank, this river must be in the Northern Hemisphere. Final answer: Northern Hemisphere.

In Figure B, the R value is defined as the ratio of manufacturing population density to service-industry employment population density, and the peak of the R value shifted outward from roughly 20–30 km in 1996 to about 30–40 km in 2001, indicating that the location where manufacturing employment is most concentrated relative to service employment has moved farther from the city center. This outward shift of the R-value maximum reflects the suburbanization of manufacturing industry in Beijing, as factories and manufacturing employment relocated from the central city toward the urban fringe and suburbs, while service employment remained more concentrated in the city center. Final answer: the suburbanization (outward relocation) of manufacturing industry in Beijing.

The profile along 106.8°E runs from Baoji in the north to Zunyi in the south; terrain region ④ is the broad southern basin (Sichuan Basin), where the annual precipitation curve exceeds 1000 mm and the text notes that nighttime rain makes up 60–70 % of the total. From an atmospheric-radiation viewpoint, the dominant nocturnal feature is strong atmospheric back radiation (counter-radiation): the basin’s abundant moisture and cloud cover strongly absorb outgoing long-wave radiation from the surface and re-emit it downward, so the ground cools slowly and the lower atmosphere remains relatively warm and unstable, favoring nocturnal rainfall. Final answer: strong atmospheric back radiation (clouds produce strong counter-radiation at night).

The map shows solid contour lines falling from a >2000 m highland eastward to 200 m lowland, with dashed phreatic-water-level lines indicating the groundwater table. The figure shows that vegetable-planting specialized villages (squares on the right-hand map) are densely distributed across the eastern plain of Henan, where the terrain is low and flat and population density—and thus labor supply—is high; in contrast, apple and flower villages (left map) occur mainly in western and northern hilly areas, and tea villages (stars) are confined to the southern marginal hills. Vegetable production is highly labor-intensive because it requires frequent planting, tending, harvesting, and marketing, so it tends to develop in areas with abundant labor; therefore, the type of specialized village most favored by abundant labor resources is the vegetable-planting specialized village. Final answer: vegetable planting specialized village.

The map shows solid topographic contour lines (m) and dashed phreatic-water-level lines (m). At M the river lies in the higher western valley between the 2000 m and 1200 m land-surface contours, so the river water surface there is above 1200 m; the dashed phreatic line passing through M is the 1200 m line, indicating the groundwater level at M is about 1200 m. In the figure, region ② is located near about 125°E and 45°N (northeastern China), while region ③ is near about 115°E and 20°N (southern China). The map shows M city in the Central Valley at about 40°N and an average elevation of 52 m, and its climate table gives January 7.9 °C, April 15.5 °C, July 25.2 °C, and October 18.3 °C, with summer precipitation nearly zero. The chart plots population birth rate on the vertical axis and population death rate on the horizontal axis, with diagonal lines representing natural population growth rate (natural growth rate = birth rate − death rate). The figure shows two schematic maps with a 40° latitude line; point M lies in the mid-latitude zone above the 40° line, and the problem states that M is affected by the prevailing westerlies and that its west side is ocean. The prevailing westerlies are surface winds that blow from the west toward the east, so at place M the near-surface wind comes from the west and blows toward the east. The map shows an Atlantic island near 45°S and 20.5°W, with rivers draining from the interior toward the coast and four labeled points: 甲 (Jia) in the northeast, 乙 (Yi) in the northwest/west, 丙 (Bing) in the east, and 丁 (Ding) in the southwest. On a contour topographic map, closely spaced contour lines indicate a steep slope, and river pattern reflects gradient: short, straight rivers descend steep terrain, while long, winding rivers descend gentle terrain. The rivers on the western side of the island are shorter and more direct, indicating a steeper western slope, whereas the eastern rivers are longer and more sinuous, indicating a gentler eastern slope. Since 乙 lies on the steeper western side, the contour lines would be densest there. Final answer: Yi (乙).

The graph shows that the temperature curve (气温) reaches its maximum at about 12 h and then falls, while the air‑pressure curve (气压) reaches a minimum at about 12 h and then rises sharply in the afternoon. In a typical day, the highest air temperature usually occurs in the early afternoon because the ground continues to gain heat after noon; however, the passage of a cold front can reverse this trend. The pressure minimum around noon followed by a rapid pressure increase indicates that a cold front/cold air mass arrived at the station near midday. After the front passed, colder air replaced the warmer air, so temperatures dropped after 12 h instead of continuing to rise. Therefore, the highest temperature appeared around noon rather than in the afternoon. Final answer: A cold front/cold air mass arrived around noon, causing air pressure to rise and temperature to fall in the afternoon, so the day’s highest temperature occurred at about 12 h.

The graph plots the July–August latitude of the summer rain belt (or subtropical high ridge) from 1955 to 1990; in 1989 the curve reaches about 24°N, which is the lowest point in the series and well below the long-term average near 26°N. A southward shift of the rain belt places the main rainfall south of the Yangtze River Basin, which lies near 30°N, so the basin receives less July–August rain. Final answer: below normal.

The bar chart displays monthly sunshine hours for four cities, with the legend identifying the third bar in each monthly group (dark gray/patterned) as Shanghai. The figure is a land-use plan showing commercial, residential, industrial and green areas, with a river running through the city and four possible wind-rose diagrams; the two contour lines differ by 10 m, so the river flows from the higher upstream side toward the lower downstream side. Point R lies on the upstream section of the river, above the main built-up area, so any wastewater released at R would flow through the city’s residential and commercial districts. In rational urban planning, water-polluting factories must be placed downstream of the city’s water supply and residential areas, while clean or light industries may be placed upstream. Therefore, the least suitable factory to locate at R is a heavily water-polluting one such as a paper mill. Final answer: a paper mill.

The map shows Canada’s railways and major cities arranged in a narrow east–west belt along the country’s southern border, stretching from Vancouver through Winnipeg, Toronto, Ottawa, and Montreal to Halifax. This same belt is where Canada’s main industrial regions are concentrated, especially the St. Lawrence River and Great Lakes region, because this zone has the best climate, the largest cities, the main transport routes, and the closest access to the United States market. The map shows a county seat (large circle symbol) positioned immediately beside a river, with a railway and highway also running through or near it; the most direct spatial relationship is that the settlement is aligned with the river course. The map’s legend distinguishes Dongting Lake’s July–September water area from its June water area, and the June extent is shown reaching farther outward, indicating a larger lake surface during that month. The image depicts Xinjiang’s topography, with a major east-west mountain range running through the center and low-lying areas to its north and south. In Chinese regional geography, Xinjiang is described as having “three mountains surrounding two basins”: the Altai Mountains to the north, the Tianshan Mountains in the middle, and the Kunlun Mountains to the south, with the Junggar Basin north of the Tianshan and the Tarim Basin south of it. Since Northern Xinjiang corresponds mainly to the Junggar Basin and Southern Xinjiang mainly to the Tarim Basin, both areas mostly belong to basin terrain. Final answer: basin

The left map places Jia near 120° longitude between 30°N and 40°N, so Jia is in the Northern Hemisphere, while the right map places Yi near 150° longitude between 23°26′S and 30°S, so Yi is in the Southern Hemisphere.
