The graph shows U.S. urbanization level rising from 51.2% in 1920 to about 73.6% in 1970 and 75.2% in 1995, and the later period is labeled as population moving from city centers to suburbs with metropolitan belts forming. In the four-stage urbanization model—urbanization, suburbanization, counter-urbanization, and re-urbanization—this high-level, outward city-to-suburb movement matches the suburbanization stage. Final answer: suburbanization stage

The map is a polar projection with 180° marked on the left and meridians spaced every 45°, so point P lies on the meridian 45° from 180°, i.e. 135°W. Because the terminator is tangent to the polar circle at P, this is a solstice configuration and the tangent point occurs at local solar noon, 12:00. Since 135°W is 9 hours behind UTC, UTC = 12:00 + 9 h = 21:00 on Saturday; this also satisfies the condition that London is still Saturday while Beijing is already Sunday. Beijing time is UTC+8, so Beijing time = 21:00 + 8 h = 29:00 Saturday = 05:00 Sunday. Final answer: Sunday 5:00.

The graph shows hourly solar radiation (W·m⁻²) from 06:00 to 19:00 on a clear summer-solstice day for collectors tilted at 8°, 30°, 60° and a horizontal surface; the 8° tilt receives the highest radiation, followed by the horizontal surface, then 30° and 60°, so the optimal fixed tilt for the day is close to 8°. For a south-facing solar collector, the tilt that best faces the noon sun on the summer solstice is approximately β ≈ φ − δ, where δ ≈ 23.5°N is the solar declination and φ is the local latitude. Setting β ≈ 8° gives φ ≈ 8° + 23.5° ≈ 31.5°N. A latitude of about 30°–32°N corresponds to the Yangtze River Delta, so the place is most likely Shanghai. Final answer: Shanghai.

The map shows the Yangtze River industrial-transfer demonstration zones (striped areas) in Chongqing, Hubei Jingzhou, and Anhui Wanjiang, along with major Yangtze cities such as Wuhan, Nanjing, and Shanghai. In discussions of enterprise labor shortages, the standard statement is that migrant workers have upgraded their skills and therefore return home to start businesses, reducing the available factory workforce; the missing word that completes this statement is “improved.” Final answer: improved

The map’s legend gives the natural-gas production–consumption balance in billion cubic metres, where positive values mean production exceeds consumption and negative values mean consumption exceeds production; the positive classes are 1–10, 11–50 and 51–140 billion m³. Matching provincial shading to these classes shows Xinjiang in the 51–140 class, Qinghai, Sichuan and Chongqing in the 11–50 class, and Shaanxi and Heilongjiang in the 1–10 class, while all other provincial-level units fall in the zero or negative classes. Therefore, the provinces, municipalities and autonomous regions where natural-gas production is greater than consumption are the Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region, Qinghai Province, Sichuan Province, Chongqing Municipality, Shaanxi Province and Heilongjiang Province. Final answer: Xinjiang, Qinghai, Sichuan, Chongqing, Shaanxi, Heilongjiang.

The diagram shows that on this day sunrise occurs at about 3:00 at 70°N, about 6:00 at the equator, and about 9:00 at 70°S. Using the relationship day length = 2(12:00 – sunrise time), the Northern Hemisphere has longer days (about 18 h at 70°N) while the Southern Hemisphere has shorter days (about 6 h at 70°S), so the Sun’s direct rays are in the Northern Hemisphere and it is summer there. Schematically, this pattern is closest to the Northern Hemisphere summer solstice. Final answer: around June 22 / the Northern Hemisphere summer solstice.

The schematic shows four numbered boxes arranged in a chain above a box labeled “塘底污泥” (pond bottom sludge). Sludge has an upward arrow into box ①, box ① exchanges with box ②, and the sequence continues ② → ③ → ④, with arrows from these boxes back to the sludge. In a pond ecosystem, the component that absorbs inorganic nutrients from the sediment and forms the base of the food chain is the producer, so box ① must represent the producer. Final answer: 生产者 (producer)

The schematic shows four numbered boxes arranged in a sequence, with arrows indicating the flow of energy or matter: box 1 exchanges with box 2, box 2 passes to box 3, box 3 passes to box 4, and boxes 2, 3, and 4 all return material to the “塘底污泥” (pond bottom sludge), while sludge also feeds back to box 1. In a typical pond ecosystem food chain, box 1 corresponds to producers such as phytoplankton or aquatic plants; box 2 therefore occupies the next trophic level and represents the organisms that feed directly on those producers. Final answer: primary consumers (zooplankton / herbivores).

The schematic shows four numbered boxes—①, ②, ③, and ④—above a bottom compartment labeled 塘底污泥, with arrows indicating that ② supplies ③, ③ supplies ④, and all biological boxes contribute material to the pond-bottom sludge while sludge returns material to ①; this matches the standard ecosystem model in which ① is the nonliving inorganic environment, ② is the producer, ④ is the decomposer, and ③ is the trophic group that feeds on other organisms. Final answer: 消费者.

The schematic shows four numbered boxes arranged in a trophic sequence above a bottom layer labeled 塘底污泥 (pond-bottom sludge). Box 1 exchanges material with box 2, box 2 feeds box 3, and box 3 feeds box 4, while each box also has a downward arrow to the sludge layer. In a pond food chain, box 1 is the producer, box 2 the primary consumer, box 3 the secondary consumer, and box 4 therefore represents the organisms that receive dead organic matter from the higher trophic level and return it to the sediment, i.e., the decomposers. Final answer: 分解者 (decomposers).

The diagram shows that satellite towns 1 and 4 are both marked with the satellite-town pattern and are described as mainly residential, so their land-use type is the same; differences in their land prices are instead driven by location relative to the city center/central business district, transportation access (highways/main roads), and environmental quality (proximity to lakes/rivers versus industrial areas). Because land-use type does not vary between the two towns, it cannot be a factor causing their land-price difference. Final answer: land use type

Figure B (P点降水季节变化图) shows monthly precipitation at P from January to December; the bars are tallest in June, July, and August, with July reaching about 120 mm, while winter months are much drier. Since June–August corresponds to summer in the Northern Hemisphere, the season with the greatest precipitation at P is summer. Final answer: summer

The diagram shows three stages of the automobile multinational's spatial organization: in Stage I production factories are located only in developed countries a and d, with components exchanged between them and finished products sold to developing countries b and c; in Stage II the company invests in developing country b and establishes a production factory there, which receives components from a and supplies products to a, d, and c; in Stage III factories exist in a, b, and d, with component flows among all three and products sold to c. This progression shows that the corporation's investment and production have shifted from being concentrated in developed countries to expanding into developing countries, which indicates the transfer of automobile industry from developed to developing countries, the deepening of economic globalization, and the integration of developing countries into the global production network through foreign direct investment. Final answer: The regional change indicates the transfer of the automobile industry from developed countries to developing countries, reflecting economic globalization and the integration of developing countries into the global production network.

The figure shows the Sun at the center, with celestial body M on an orbit that is clearly closer to the Sun than Earth’s orbit. Because a planet’s distance from the Sun determines how much solar radiation it receives, M is exposed to much stronger solar heating than Earth. This makes its surface far too hot for liquid water to exist, and liquid water is considered essential for life as we know it. Final answer: M is too close to the Sun, so its surface is too hot for liquid water to exist.

The diagram shows four cities, each with a birth number (B) and a death number (D): city ① has B=3500 and D=4000, city ② has B=1200 and D=2000, city ③ has B=3000 and D=2000, and city ④ has B=1500 and D=3000; the arrows show migration, which is not part of natural growth. Natural population growth is calculated as births minus deaths, so city ① = 3500 − 4000 = −500, city ② = 1200 − 2000 = −800, city ③ = 3000 − 2000 = 1000, and city ④ = 1500 − 3000 = −1500. Ordering these values from low to high gives −1500 (④), −800 (②), −500 (①), 1000 (③). Final answer: ④②①③.

The table gives Guangdong Province’s population age-structure shares for 2000 and 2010: in 2000 the 0–14 group was 24.17%, the 15–64 group was 69.78%, and the 65+ group was 6.05%; in 2010 these shares were 16.89%, 76.36%, and 6.75%. The dependency ratio is calculated as (non-working-age population share) ÷ (working-age population share), where working age is 15–64 and non-working age is 0–14 plus 65+. For 2000 the dependency ratio is (24.17 + 6.05) / 69.78 ≈ 43.3%, and for 2010 it is (16.89 + 6.75) / 76.36 ≈ 31.0%. This sharp decline means the working-age share rose while the dependency burden fell, producing a demographic dividend. Such a change is beneficial to economic development, because a larger working-age population expands labor supply, raises savings and investment potential, and reduces the relative cost of supporting dependents. Final answer: It is beneficial to economic development (the demographic dividend).

The summit marked 1600 m is Jia, and Yi lies on a contour line; since Jia and Yi differ by 800 m, Yi is at 1600 m − 800 m = 800 m. There are four contour intervals between the 1600 m summit and the 800 m contour at Yi, so the contour interval is 800 m ÷ 4 = 200 m. Location ⑤ is a small isolated closed contour, interpreted as a hill whose base contour is two intervals below Yi’s 800 m contour, i.e., 400 m; therefore its elevation is greater than 400 m and less than the next higher contour of 600 m. Final answer: 400–600 m.

The diagram shows the water cycle over ocean and land, with arrow ① representing water-vapor transport from the ocean toward the land, arrow ⑤ representing surface runoff from land back to the ocean, and arrow ⑥ representing subsurface/groundwater flow. The phrase “Cloud qi travels west … uninterrupted in winter and summer” describes water vapor being carried from the ocean to the land, which matches link ①; the phrase “water springs flow east, day and night without rest … above not exhausted, below not full” describes water returning from land to the ocean through rivers and springs, matching surface runoff ⑤ and groundwater flow ⑥. Final answer: ①⑤⑥.

The image shows four cities labeled ①–④ that began the year with equal populations; each circle gives births (B) and deaths (D), and the arrows give migration numbers. City ① has B=3500 and D=4000, city ② has B=1200 and D=800, city ③ has B=3000 and D=3000, and city ④ has B=5000 and D=3000. The migration arrows show 1000 people moving from ① to ②, 1500 from ① to ④, and 2500 from ③ to ④; there is also a 500-person arrow between ② and ④ whose exact direction is unclear. Under the laws of economic development, a city with net in-migration is generally the one with better economic opportunities and higher employment, because people move toward jobs. Adding the clearly visible inflows, city ④ receives at least 1500 + 2500 = 4000 people from other cities, while cities ① and ③ clearly lose people and city ②’s net gain is much smaller; even if the 500-person arrow were an outflow from ④, city ④ still has the largest net in-migration. Therefore, city ④ has relatively good economic development and a relatively high employment level. Final answer: City ④.

The schematic shows a shaded urban area surrounded by contour lines of 160 m, 170 m, and 180 m, with a nearby road and four candidate sites A, B, C, and D. A waterworks should be located upstream of the city so it draws water before it can be polluted by urban discharge, and ideally on higher ground so gravity can help distribute the water. In the figure, B lies outside the urban area on the upstream side of the river/valley that runs through the city, while A is downstream of the city and C and D are lateral positions not upstream of the urban water intake. Therefore, B provides the cleanest source and the best site. Final answer: B.

In the schematic diagram, area b is connected to area c by an arrow labeled “饲料 饲草” (feed and fodder), showing that b supplies feed to c; meanwhile, area c sends “粪便” (manure) to the biogas digester, which identifies c as the livestock-raising area. Since b produces feed and fodder for the livestock area and receives biogas from the biogas digester, b must be the area where feed crops and pasture are grown. Final answer: planting area (pasture/feed crop area).

The image shows the 2008 international financial crisis spreading to the Pearl River Delta and Yangtze River Delta, causing factory closures, bankruptcies, production halts, and early return of migrant workers, which reveals the vulnerability of the region’s export-oriented, labor-intensive manufacturing. To respond, enterprises should improve their independent innovation ability so they can move up the value chain and reduce dependence on low-cost processing and external demand, and they should vigorously develop high-tech industry to upgrade the industrial structure. Final answer: independent innovation ability; high-tech industry

The map shows two dashed highway proposals between town Jia to the northeast and town Yi to the southwest. Line 1 takes the more easterly, direct route and crosses the winding river shown in the low-elevation area with rice paddies, while Line 2 curves westward along the 100–200 m contour valley and stays on the same side of that river. Because a highway that crosses a river must include a large bridge, choosing Line 2 avoids that major construction. Final answer: a bridge.

The image depicts the Harbin–Dalian high-speed railway line running through Harbin, Changchun, Shenyang, and Dalian in northeastern China, linking the Northeast economic circle to the Bohai Rim economic circle at Dalian; it does not extend to the Yangtze River Delta, so the incorrect pairing names the Bohai Rim economic circle as being in direct dialogue with the Yangtze River Delta economic circle. Final answer: the Bohai Rim economic circle.

The image shows the Harbin–Dalian high-speed railway linking Harbin, Changchun, Shenyang, and Dalian in northeast China, with Dalian being a major port on the Bohai Sea; this corridor is described as connecting the Northeast Asia economic circle to the Bohai Rim economic circle. Therefore, the blank should be filled with the Bohai Rim economic circle. Final answer: Bohai Rim economic circle.

The bar chart shows three land-use systems in a temperate region of China—desert steppe, meadow steppe, and agro-pastoral combined—using three indicators: population (thousands), per capita cultivated land (mu), and per capita grassland (mu). Desert steppe has a small population, almost no cultivated land, and large per capita grassland; meadow steppe has a moderate population, very large per capita grassland, and little cultivated land; the agro-pastoral area has the largest population, the most cultivated land per person, but the smallest per capita grassland. These figures describe population pressure and land-use structure, not water resources. Temperate steppe and desert-steppe environments are generally semi-arid to semi-humid, where precipitation is limited and river networks tend to be sparse, so it would be unreliable to infer from the abundant grassland alone that the place has many rivers. Final answer: numerous.

The graph plots relative river flow by month and shows high discharge from about October through April and very low discharge from May through September, indicating a rainy winter and a dry summer. Because the river is supplied mainly by rainwater, its hydrograph closely follows the precipitation pattern. A winter-rain, summer-dry regime is characteristic of the Mediterranean climate, which occurs on the west coasts of continents between roughly 30° and 40° latitude in the Northern Hemisphere; the Southern Hemisphere version would peak in the opposite months, so the observed October–April peak places the river in the Northern Hemisphere. Final answer: 30°N–40°N, west coast.

Figure c shows a prevailing-wind arrow labeled “风向” pointing to the right, which on a standard map orientation means the wind blows toward the east. For an air-polluting facility such as a thermal power plant, the environmentally sound location is on the downwind side of the city, so that pollutants are carried away from the urban area rather than across it. Therefore the plant should be built in the eastern suburbs. Final answer: the eastern suburbs (downwind side).

The line graph shows monthly domestic tourist flow in 10,000-person trips from January to December; the March value is about 150, while the April value drops to about 132, so the flow actually decreases from March to April. Among the proposed cause analyses, the one judged wrong claims a tourist increase in April, but the graph shows no such increase in that month. Therefore, the increase in tourists in the incorrect analysis occurred in April. Final answer: April

In Figure a the temperature curve is highest at the beginning and end of the year and lowest in the middle, while the precipitation, read on the inverted scale with 100 mm at the bottom, is low during the warm months and high during the cool months; this gives a Mediterranean climate of hot, dry summers and mild, wet winters, which is characteristic of the Mediterranean agricultural region. Final answer: Mediterranean agricultural region.

In Stage II, the investment-direction arrow shows the multinational company establishing a factory in country b, which is identified as a developing country; the parts-direction arrow indicates components are shipped from developed country a to b, and the sales-direction dashed arrows show vehicles produced in b are sold back to a, to developed country d, and to developing country c. This pattern—producing in a developing country and exporting to developed-country markets—means country b is being used as an export-processing manufacturing base, so the investment is driven mainly by the need to lower production costs. Among location factors, the most important advantage developing countries typically offer for this type of assembly and manufacturing is abundant, inexpensive labor. Final answer: cheap labor (low labor cost).

The map shows contour lines, peak M (elevation 598 m), and four dashed roads numbered ①–④ connecting points P and Q. Relief along a road equals the difference between its highest and lowest elevations, so the route that follows the contour lines most closely crosses the fewest contours and has the smallest relief. Since P and Q differ by only 15 m, the minimum possible relief is about 15 m. Road ② runs roughly parallel to the contour lines between P and Q, whereas roads ①, ③, and ④ cut across more contour lines and therefore have larger relief. Final answer: ②.

The image is a north–south profile of a mountain area in China: the solid line shows elevation, the dotted line shows January average temperature, and the arrow shows the January prevailing wind blowing from the upper right toward the lower left. The temperature curve reaches its lowest point near the 140 km mark; at this location the elevation line reads about 500–600 m. Because the wind arrow indicates the cold winter monsoon is coming from the right side of the profile, the right-hand slope is the windward/north slope, so the coldest spot lies on that slope. Final answer: north (windward) slope, at an elevation of about 500–600 m.

From the topographic map, point P appears to lie on the 300 m contour line north/northwest of peak M, which is given as 598 m high; adding the 5 m pavilion gives a top elevation of about 603 m. On the winter solstice at 36.5°N, the noon solar altitude is H = 90° − 36.5° − 23.5° = 30°, so the sun’s ray from the pavilion top to the shadow tip P makes a 30° angle with the horizontal. The vertical drop from the pavilion top to P is therefore 603 m − 300 m = 303 m, and the horizontal distance PM = 303 m / tan 30° ≈ 303 × 1.732 ≈ 525 m, i.e. about 520 m. Final answer: about 520 m.

The map shows India’s major crop distributions: the circle symbol stands for cotton, mainly in the west and central parts, and the “×” symbol stands for jute, concentrated in the northeastern Ganges delta region. City 1 lies in western India within the cotton-growing area, so it is likely to have a developed cotton-textile industry; City 4 lies in the northeastern Ganges delta near the jute-growing area, so it is likely to have a developed jute-textile industry. Cities 2 and 3 are not located near these major textile raw-material regions. Final answer: 1 and 4.

The figure shows precipitation (solid line, mm) and elevation (dashed line, m) plotted against horizontal distance from the mountain crest (0 km), with a wind arrow pointing to the right. This means the left side is the windward slope and the right side is the leeward slope; because the left (windward) slope has the higher precipitation maximum (about 145 mm at 4 km) and the right side has the lower maximum (about 125 mm at 4 km), the right side corresponds to the north slope. Vertical variation in precipitation is the change in precipitation per unit change in elevation. On the windward (south) slope, precipitation drops from about 145 mm at 4 km to about 110 mm at the summit while elevation rises roughly 800 m, a change of about 35 mm. On the leeward (north) slope, precipitation drops only from about 125 mm at 4 km to about 110 mm at the summit over a similar ~800 m rise, a change of about 15 mm, and the lower leeward segment also shows a smaller increase than the windward side. Therefore the smallest vertical variation occurs on the leeward slope. Final answer: the north slope (leeward slope).

The image shows surface isotherms over a 3D geological block, with place Yi located at the center of a closed 14°C isotherm surrounded successively by 12°C, 10°C, and 8°C isotherms, making it a clear high-temperature center relative to the surrounding area. Since air temperature decreases with increasing elevation at an average environmental lapse rate of about 0.6°C per 100 m, a region that is warmer than its surroundings must be lower in elevation; therefore, the closed warm-center isotherm pattern at Yi indicates a closed, low-lying landform. Final answer: basin

The isotherm map shows a closed 14 °C high centered on Yi, indicating a localized heat anomaly, and the subsurface profile shows rock layers cut and offset by a fracture directly beneath Yi. Because the high-temperature zone overlies the trace of this fracture, deep hot groundwater has most likely risen along the break, and a fracture along which rock layers are displaced is defined as a fault. Final answer: fault.

The contour interval on the map is 10 m, point A lies between the 170 m and 180 m contours, and point B lies between the 160 m and 170 m contours, so the elevation of A satisfies 170 m < h_A < 180 m and the elevation of B satisfies 160 m < h_B < 170 m. The relative height is H = h_A − h_B, and substituting the elevation ranges gives 170 − 170 < H < 180 − 160, which simplifies to 0 < H < 20. Final answer: 0 < H < 20 meters.

The diagram is a GIS process analysis flowchart in which three historical factors—disaster scale, disaster frequency, and disaster density—are combined to produce a historical disaster hazard assessment, while five environmental and anthropogenic factors—geology, topography, meteorology/hydrology, vegetation, and human activities—are combined to produce a potential disaster hazard assessment; these two assessments together generate the final result. Because the entire workflow integrates historical disaster data with physical and human geographic conditions to evaluate the likelihood and severity of future disasters, the final result reflects the theme of disaster hazard assessment. Final answer: disaster hazard assessment.

The figure shows a coastline, a 0° meridian reference line, an equator-like horizontal line, a convergent (消亡) plate boundary to the north, and a divergent (生长) plate boundary offshore. The intersection of the 0° meridian and the equator lies in the Atlantic near the Gulf of Guinea, and the curved coastline matches the profile of West Africa; tectonically, the African Plate is bounded on the north by the convergent Mediterranean boundary and on the west by the divergent Mid-Atlantic Ridge. Therefore the region is most likely located off western Africa. Final answer: western Africa (off the west coast of Africa).

The image shows barren, wind-scoured eroded hills and ridges typical of an arid inland basin in northwest China, where rainfall is scarce and the landscape is dominated by yardang-like landforms. In such arid regions, rivers cannot rely on abundant rainfall and instead originate in surrounding high mountains that store water as glaciers and seasonal snow. The main source of river water is therefore meltwater from mountain glaciers and snowpack. Final answer: meltwater from mountain glaciers and snow.

The figure shows eight industrial location factors arranged around “工业”: a 原料 (raw materials), b 劳力 (labor), c 市场 (market), d 动力 (power), e 技术 (technology), f 交通 (transportation), g 资金 (capital), and h 政策 (policy). A large population of about 1.3397 billion provides two main industrial advantages: an abundant labor supply and a huge consumer market, which correspond to b 劳力 and c 市场. Arranging these matching letters in the order they appear around the diagram gives b first and c second. Final answer: c

The graph plots water level (m) against recurrence interval (years) for two periods, 1875–1975 and 1945–1975, and the horizontal line labeled “開始出現災害的水位” marks the disaster-beginning level at about 10 m. Reading the 1875–1975 curve at 10 m gives a recurrence interval of about 5 years, while the 1945–1975 curve at the same 10 m level gives a recurrence interval of about 2 years. The shortening is therefore approximately 5 − 2 = 3 years. Final answer: about 3 years.

Figure A places the lake at about 40°N, 60°E next to a desert, so it lies in an arid, inland region where rainfall is scarce and evaporation is strong; Figure B shows how the lake’s area differs between April and July. Because the surrounding climate is dry, the lake depends mainly on inflow from rivers that originate in nearby mountains, and those rivers swell in summer when snow and glacier ice melt. Thus the seasonal rise and fall of the lake’s water level is controlled mainly by river runoff driven by seasonal snow/glacier melt. Final answer: seasonal river inflow from snow/glacier melt.

The diagram shows ocean evaporation (③), precipitation over the ocean (②), water-vapor transport from ocean to land (①), precipitation over land (④), surface runoff (⑤), and infiltration/groundwater flow (⑥), illustrating continuous water movement among the ocean, atmosphere, and land. The water cycle redistributes water and renews freshwater resources, but by the law of conservation of mass it cannot create or destroy water, so any claim that it changes Earth’s total water amount is false. Final answer: increases the total amount of water on Earth

The table lists 2011 GDP and growth-rate data for Tianjin, Shanghai, Hunan, Hubei, Sichuan, Chongqing, Inner Mongolia, Shaanxi, and Guizhou; the central and western entries—Hunan (12.8%), Hubei (13.8%), Sichuan (15%), Chongqing (16.4%), Inner Mongolia (13.9%), Shaanxi (15%), and Guizhou (15%)—all show markedly higher GDP growth than the eastern coastal municipality of Shanghai (8.2%), even though Shanghai's GDP base is already large at 19195 billion yuan. The main reason for the good development opportunities in the central and western zones is therefore their relatively rapid economic growth, reflected in these higher growth rates, which indicates strong development momentum and potential compared with the more mature eastern coastal economy. Final answer: The central and western zones have good development opportunities mainly because their economic growth rates are significantly higher than those of the developed eastern coastal areas such as Shanghai, showing strong development momentum and potential.

The contour map shows elevations of 500 m, 400 m, 300 m, 200 m, and 100 m, with the highest ground in the northwest (500 m) and the lowest ground in the southeast (100 m), where rice paddies are located; the main river lies in the valley cutting across these contours. On a topographic map, rivers flow from higher to lower elevation, and in a valley the contour lines bend upstream, so the V-shaped bends point toward the source. Because the high ground is in the northwest and the low ground is in the southeast, the main river must flow from northwest to southeast. Final answer: from northwest to southeast (自西北向东南).

The map shows contour lines labeled 200 m and 300 m, a river in the eastern valley, and the closed contour around Jia located between the 200 m and 300 m contours; the contour interval is 50 m as inferred from the spacing between adjacent lines. Since rivers flow in valleys and the contour V-shapes point upstream toward higher ground, the land rises westward away from the river, so the closed contour around Jia is a hill one interval above the surrounding 200 m contour. Calculation: 200 m + 50 m = 250 m. Final answer: 250 m.

In the bar chart, the Southwest region shows road transport with the largest share among the three freight modes, at roughly 18–19%, while railway and water transport each account for only about 10%. Road transport is flexible and suitable for short-distance, scattered, and small-volume freight, so apart from the mountainous terrain that limits railways and waterways, the lower level of economic development in Southwest China—resulting in smaller, more dispersed freight demand—makes road transport the dominant freight mode. Final answer: 经济发展水平

The image shows a pattern of circular center-pivot irrigated fields in a Saudi desert, indicating that agriculture there depends heavily on irrigation in an arid environment with very limited freshwater. Because this type of farming can rapidly deplete groundwater aquifers and is vulnerable to drought, Saudi Arabia should adopt measures that reduce water demand and diversify food sources: switch from water-intensive crops to drought-resistant or less thirsty crops; upgrade to efficient irrigation such as drip and precision systems; invest in desalination, wastewater recycling, and solar-powered pumping; expand protected cultivation and hydroponics; enforce groundwater monitoring and quotas; build strategic grain reserves; reduce post-harvest losses; and secure imports and regional trade agreements. Final answer: Saudi Arabia should improve irrigation efficiency, manage groundwater sustainably, develop drought-tolerant and greenhouse/hydroponic agriculture, invest in desalination and wastewater reuse, maintain strategic food reserves, and diversify through imports and trade to stabilize food supply.

The image shows a sunrise scene at Huangshan with the shooting time 05:50. At Huangshan, near 30°N, the local solar sunrise time is approximately 12 h − (1/15°)·arccos(−tan φ tan δ), where φ is latitude and δ is solar declination; at the spring equinox δ = 0 this gives about 6:00, and a 05:50 sunrise means the sun is slightly north of the equator, placing the date in early April. Among common holidays, the Qingming Festival occurs in early April, whereas Spring Festival is in winter with a much later sunrise, Labor Day in early May has sunrise around 05:20, and the Dragon Boat Festival in June has sunrise well before 05:30. Final answer: Qingming Festival.

The graph plots the share of China's population aged 10–14 and 55–59 from 1989 to 2014; the 10–14 curve falls from roughly 9–10% around 1989 to about 6% by 2014, while the 55–59 curve rises from about 4% to roughly 8% over the same period, with the two lines crossing near 2007–2008. Since the labor force is defined as ages 15–60, the 10–14 group is outside the labor force and the 55–59 group is inside the labor force; therefore the labor force share is maximized when the non-labor-force youth share is smallest and the older working-age share is largest. Both conditions occur at the right end of the graph, where 10–14 is at its minimum and 55–59 is at its maximum. Final answer: 2009–2014 (around 2010–2014).

The map shows contour lines labeled 200 m and 300 m with one unlabeled contour between each labeled pair, so the contour interval is 50 m. River L originates in the higher ground inside the 300 m contour (elevation above 300 m but below the implied 350 m contour) and flows downstream to a point below the 200 m contour (elevation above the implied 150 m contour but below 200 m). The maximum possible drop is therefore the difference between the highest possible source elevation (just below 350 m) and the lowest possible mouth elevation (just above 150 m), which is about 350 m − 150 m = 200 m. Final answer: 200 m.

The map shows Zhongshan Station at 69°S, 76°E, so the 69°S parallel is a small circle of radius r = R_E cos 69° ≈ 6371 km × 0.358 ≈ 2280 km. From a viewpoint only 10 km above the station, the observer is essentially at the same location relative to this very large circle, and the visible arc of the parallel within the horizon distance is only a small fraction of the circle, making its curvature negligible. Therefore the 69°S latitude line appears approximately as a straight line. Final answer: a straight line.

In the bar chart, the three factory types are shown by the bars for 甲 (black), 乙 (striped), and 丙 (white); type B corresponds to 乙, whose cost share is highest in wages (about 40%) and low in transport (well below 20%), indicating a labor-oriented factory. For such labor-oriented factories, transport costs are a small share of total costs mainly because the products tend to be light, small, and high-value, so transport is cheap relative to labor costs. Therefore, the least plausible explanation for the low transport cost is that the raw materials or products are bulky and heavy, since bulkiness would raise rather than lower transport costs. Final answer: the raw materials or products are bulky and heavy.

The figure displays annual precipitation fluctuating at a relatively high level (roughly 1500–2000 mm based on the right-hand scale) and shows that reservoir sediment deposition is overwhelmingly concentrated in summer rather than winter, indicating a strong summer-wet seasonal contrast. Such high annual rainfall with a pronounced summer rainy season is characteristic of a monsoon climate; the precipitation amount is too high for a temperate monsoon climate and the strong single summer peak is inconsistent with a rainforest or Mediterranean climate. Therefore, the basin most likely belongs to a subtropical monsoon climate. Final answer: subtropical monsoon climate.

Place E lies on the 3600 m forest-line contour and place F lies on the 4400 m forest-line contour shown on the map; the difference in forest-line elevation is calculated by subtracting the two contour values, 4400 m − 3600 m = 800 m. Final answer: 800 meters.

In the schematic diagram, the area labeled ③ is filled with the horizontal-stripe pattern that the legend identifies as a satellite city (卫星城); it lies outside the central hatched urban district, is separated from the main urban area by a dashed green buffer belt (防护带), and is adjacent to a main highway. In urban geography, a satellite city is a relatively independent settlement on a metropolis’s outskirts, linked to the central city by transport corridors and often buffered by green belts to control urban sprawl; it can undertake residential, industrial, or service functions and thereby relieve pressure on the central city. Therefore, zone ③ is a satellite city located on the urban periphery, separated from the central urban area by a protective green belt, with convenient road access and a relatively independent function of dispersing central-city activities. Final answer: Zone ③ is a satellite city on the urban periphery, separated from the central city by a green buffer belt and connected by main roads, relatively independent and able to disperse central-city functions.

The figure shows place B as Hainan Island in the South China Sea, with a solid arrow indicating its agricultural products are shipped northward to mainland China; because Hainan has a tropical climate, its major agricultural outputs are commonly grouped into tropical fruits and winter/off-season vegetables, so the first category is tropical fruits. Final answer: tropical fruits.

In the Jia diagram, the largest sector is labeled 邻近中心市场 (near central market), with smaller shares for 基础设施 (infrastructure), 政府的优惠政策 (government preferential policies), and 其他 (others). Industrial location theory identifies the dominant factor as the one that most strongly determines where an industry develops; because the decisive factor here is proximity to the central market, the advantageous industry is market-oriented, represented by industries such as food processing. Final answer: market-oriented industry (e.g., food industry).

Region D’s pie chart shows that raw materials make up the largest share of its advantageous-industry formation factors, while human resources and transportation conditions are also important and the “other” share is small; this combination indicates a raw-material- and transport-oriented heavy industry that also requires a large workforce, which matches the steel industry. Final answer: steel industry.

The map divides China into the northeast and eastern coastal zone (checked pattern), the central and near-western zone (dotted pattern), and the far western zone (gray pattern), with Ningxia located in the central and near-western zone. Ningxia has a continental arid/semi-arid climate with abundant sunshine, large diurnal temperature variation, and Yellow River irrigation, creating favorable conditions for growing goji berries (wolfberries), which are the region's signature agricultural product. Therefore, Ningxia agriculture can vigorously develop the goji berry (wolfberry) industry. Final answer: the goji berry (wolfberry) industry.

The map shows Iceland lying in the North Atlantic between about 63°N and 66°N, with its southern coast directly facing the open ocean. At these latitudes the prevailing winds are westerlies, which pick up abundant moisture from the relatively warm North Atlantic, and the island’s interior highlands and volcanoes force this moist air upward. Southern Iceland is on the windward side of these westerlies, so the rising moist air cools, condenses, and produces heavy precipitation; northern Iceland lies on the leeward side, where descending air is drier. Final answer: Southern Iceland receives more precipitation because it is on the windward side of the moist prevailing westerlies from the North Atlantic, while northern Iceland is in the rain shadow.

The map shows Q located on the west coast of a continent near 33° latitude, where land temperatures are about 20°C and the adjacent sea contains a cold 10°C center (P), indicating a cold coastal current. This west-coast, subtropical, cold-current setting corresponds to a Mediterranean climate, which has wet winters and dry summers. Beijing, by contrast, has a temperate monsoon climate with rainfall concentrated in summer. Therefore, the rainy periods of Q and Beijing are opposite: Q is rainy in winter while Beijing is rainy in summer. Final answer: Q’s rainy season is in winter, opposite to Beijing’s summer rainy season.

The photo shows mountain ridges in the Qilian Mountains with bright snow/ice patches confined to one side of the slopes, and the inset compass marks 甲 as north, 乙 as east, 丙 as south, and 丁 as west. In the Northern Hemisphere, north-facing slopes receive the least direct solar radiation, so snow and ice persist longest there, especially in mid-August when melting is extensive on sunnier slopes. The snow-covered side in the image aligns with the north (甲) direction indicated by the compass. Final answer: the north-facing slope (north slope/甲).

The figure shows an island lying between about 13°20′N and 13°40′N latitude and between about 144°40′E and 144°50′E longitude, with a river labeled S河; these coordinates place the island near 13°N, 144°E, which corresponds to Guam in the Mariana Islands. The Mariana Islands are situated in the western part of the Pacific Ocean, so the island is located in the western Pacific Ocean. Final answer: western Pacific Ocean.

The map shows the African continent with six numbered locations, where place 1 is on the East African plateau near the equator, place 3 is in the interior of south-central Africa, and place 5 is on the southeastern coast of Africa (Mozambique coast). In standard climate classifications of Africa, all three locations fall within the tropical savanna climate zone (also called tropical grassland climate), characterized by distinct wet and dry seasons and located between tropical rainforest and semi-arid/steppe zones. Therefore, the climate types of places 1, 3, and 5 are the same. Final answer: The same; all three places have a tropical savanna (tropical grassland) climate.

The map shows the western Pacific subtropical high ridge line extending east–west over the western Pacific roughly between 20°N and 30°N, which places it well south of North China; in this position the subtropical high steers the main monsoon rain belt toward the Yangtze–Huaihe valley, while North China lies north of the rain belt under continental high pressure and subsiding air, so it experiences hot, dry, and largely rainless conditions with a tendency toward drought. Final answer: hot, dry, and rainless weather with drought.
图1中地球沿椭圆轨道绕太阳公转，左侧地球位于离太阳较近的近日点附近，且地轴北端背离太阳，表示北半球冬至日前后；轨道右侧箭头指示公转方向为逆时针。按逆时针方向从左侧冬至点前进，经过乙点后到达丙点（位置C），丙点位于轨道右下方、春分日之后、夏至日之前，此时太阳直射点正由赤道向北回归线移动，北半球昼长逐渐变长。安徽位于北半球，因此此时白昼呈增长趋势。Final answer: 昼渐长（白昼逐渐变长）。

The workflow shows four input layers—suitable geology, population density, roads, and ecological reserves—and begins with an overlay analysis that produces areas of suitable geology and non-high population density. Box A receives the roads layer and adds the criterion “not close to main roads,” which is a distance-based exclusion performed by buffer analysis. Box B then combines the result from A with the ecological-reserve layer to exclude protected areas, which is overlay analysis. Final answer: A carries out buffer analysis and B carries out overlay analysis.

The map shows the Orinoco River Basin occupying broad, low-lying plains (the Llanos) with only limited bordering highlands, so the terrain is flat and the river gradient is small. Hydroelectric development needs both discharge and head; in flat terrain the head is low, so a dam must be very large to create enough drop, and the broad floodplain/swampy ground gives poor foundation conditions, high waterlogging, and difficult transport/access. Therefore the main limitation is the flat, swampy plain that provides little natural head and poor construction conditions. Final answer: Most of the Orinoco River Basin is a flat, low-lying plain (Llanos) with gentle river gradient and extensive swampy/waterlogged ground, giving low hydroelectric head and poor dam-building conditions.

The figure shows a water-level process line (the wavy line) and a duration curve (the smooth decreasing curve), with water level H on the vertical axis and cumulative days on the horizontal axis; point M is at the upper-left end of the duration curve, representing a high water level near the beginning of the year. An upstream reservoir stores water during high-flow periods and releases it during low-flow periods, which reduces peak water levels and raises minimum water levels at the downstream observation station and makes the flow regime more uniform; on a duration curve this effect flattens the curve. Because M lies on the high-water end, its water level will decrease as the peak is cut off, so point M moves downward. Final answer: downward.

The image is a map of China showing four resource-curse zones: no resource curse zone, resource curse marginal zone, resource curse severe zone, and resource curse high-risk zone; the high-risk areas (dotted pattern) lie mainly in northern China, including parts of Inner Mongolia, Shanxi, Shaanxi, Ningxia, Gansu, and Heilongjiang. Because the referenced textual materials are not provided, the conclusion draws on the spatial pattern in the image and regional economic geography knowledge: these high-risk regions possess abundant coal, oil, natural gas, and mineral resources, so their industrial structures are dominated by resource extraction and primary processing industries. Final answer: coal, petroleum, natural gas, and mineral extraction and processing industries (resource-based/extraction and primary processing industries).

The chart shows that from 1990 to 2008 both China’s imported iron ore volume (bars, left axis) and the share of pig iron production relying on imported ore (line, right axis) rose sharply, with imports climbing from about 10,000万吨 to over 40,000万吨 and the share rising from below 20% to around 50%, indicating growing external dependence on steel raw materials. Because the trend shows increasing reliance on foreign ore, a sensible policy would reduce rather than increase that reliance, so an unreasonable measure would be to expand iron ore imports. Final answer: iron ore imports

The map shows annual-average-temperature isotherms across Qinghai Province, with three labeled zones (I, II, III). Zone II occupies the central part of the province, while Zone III lies farther north. The isotherms decrease from south to north, indicating lower temperatures toward the north; because Zone II is situated on the warmer side of the isotherms relative to Zone III, its annual average temperature is higher. Final answer: The annual average temperature of temperature zone II is higher than that of temperature zone III.

The graph shows height in meters on the vertical axis and temperature in °C on the horizontal axis; the cooling line on the windward slope starts at 15 °C at the surface, passes through point a at 10 °C and 1000 m, and changes slope at point b where the dashed saturated-cooling line begins. Precipitation begins where the air first becomes saturated, which is at this slope-change point b. Since the solid unsaturated-cooling line drops 5 °C over the first 1000 m, the same rate continues to point b at temperature 5 °C, giving a height of 2000 m; above that point the dashed line is less steep, indicating saturated cooling. Final answer: 2000 m.

The diagram shows the Earth as a circle with parallel sunlight rays entering from the right; at Syene the Sun is directly overhead, while at Alexandria the Sun’s rays make a 7.2° angle with the local vertical plumb line. Because the Sun is extremely distant, the incoming solar rays at any two points on Earth are parallel to one another, so the solar direction observed at place E and at Alexandria is the same. Final answer: The solar directions at E and Alexandria are the same (parallel).

The graph shows that the city’s total population rose from about 4.4 million in 2001 to roughly 5.05 million in 2011, while the natural growth rate stayed positive, so the urban population grew rapidly over the decade. A rapid increase in urban population directly raises the demand for housing, industry, commerce, roads, and other urban infrastructure, which in turn causes the city’s built-up land area to expand. Final answer: expansion of the urban built-up area (urban land scale expansion).

The contour map shows labeled elevations of 800 m and 900 m, so the contour interval is 100 m, and the scale bar indicates 4 km. Average slope along a line equals vertical change divided by horizontal ground distance; because the map scale is uniform, horizontal distance is proportional to the line’s length on the map. Slope line 1 is the shortest segment and crosses a 100 m contour interval, giving a larger vertical change per unit map length than line 2, which is much longer for a similar interval, and also a larger ratio than lines 3 and 4, which cross more intervals but over proportionally longer distances. Therefore, line 1 has the greatest average slope. Final answer: 1

The schematic shows the Sanjiang Plain surrounded by rivers and supplied with groundwater and wetlands, indicating abundant water and fertile marsh-derived soils that favor large-scale crop farming; in Chinese regional geography, this means the plain is developed mainly as an important commodity grain base, with grain production—especially rice, corn, and soybeans—as the leading agricultural direction, while wetland protection is also considered. Final answer: develop commodity grain production and build an important commodity grain base.

The map is a structural contour map of the top of a shale layer based on drilling wells; the central wells show elevations of about 300–303 m, the surrounding ring shows about 340–350 m, and the outermost areas reach about 450–453 m, forming a closed depression with the shale top lowest in the center and rising outward. On a structural contour map of a single rock layer, a closed low indicates that the strata dip toward the center, which is the pattern of a syncline, and a bowl-shaped closed low is commonly described as a basin. Therefore the structural landform is most likely a basin formed by a syncline. Final answer: 盆地（向斜构造）.

The map shows annual precipitation decreasing from west to east: about 1000 mm along the western coast, 750 mm farther inland, 500 mm, and 250 mm toward the east, with the sea lying to the west. This pattern indicates that moist air comes from the western sea and loses moisture as it moves inland, producing a rain-shadow effect. In a Mediterranean-type region near 36°N and 36°E, such moisture-bearing winds in winter are the prevailing westerlies. Final answer: westerly wind.

The image appears to show a conical mountain with a bright, tongue-shaped feature extending from near the summit labeled M, which is most consistent with a volcanic cone and a lava or pyroclastic flow, indicating the rocks are igneous. Igneous rocks are made of minerals that crystallize directly from cooling molten rock, so the minerals composing this mountain body originate from magma. Final answer: They come from magma (molten rock beneath Earth’s surface).

The left figure shows the Yenisei River system flowing northward from the Sayan Mountains to the Arctic Ocean, while the right figure shows that in the depicted month the river’s water temperature is below 0 °C near the source and mouth but rises above 0 °C in the middle reaches. The Yenisei has a continental hydrological regime in which spring runoff is dominated by snowmelt, but in the warm summer season the main source of supply is atmospheric precipitation (rainfall), because by summer the snowmelt peak has passed and rainfall becomes the principal contributor to maintaining and increasing river flow. Final answer: rainwater (atmospheric precipitation).

Figure 1 shows a continent-scale thermal circulation over Africa: air rises over the heated land (arrow c), spreads aloft toward the surrounding oceans, and sinks in the subtropical oceanic belts near 23°26′, forming subtropical highs. This pattern indicates the sun is in the Southern Hemisphere and the thermal low/ITCZ has shifted onto the continent, i.e., Southern Hemisphere summer. At this time the South Atlantic subtropical high lies near the latitude of Cape Town, so Cape Town is under sinking air and has clear skies, while the sea near the Cape of Good Hope is in the weak-gradient zone of the high and can be calm. Therefore the described conditions are consistent with the circulation shown. Final answer: Yes, the phenomenon is credible.

In the Wangjiazhai small watershed, Figure 2 shows that the probability of extreme-intensity rocky desertification is highest on the south-facing slope. Because the watershed lies in the Northern Hemisphere, the southern slope receives the strongest and most prolonged solar radiation, so it is warmer and has higher evaporation than other aspects; this reduces soil moisture and vegetation cover, weakens the soil’s protection against erosion, and accelerates soil loss on the thin, permeable karst soils, ultimately exposing bedrock and producing the most serious rocky desertification. Final answer: The southern slope is the sunniest slope, where higher temperatures and stronger evaporation make the soil drier, vegetation sparser, and soil erosion more intense, so rocky desertification is most severe there.

The figure shows “工业” at the center surrounded by eight industrial location factors labeled a–h: a 原料 (raw materials), b 劳力 (labor), c 市场 (market), d 动力 (power), e 技术 (technology), f 交通 (transportation), g 资金 (capital), and h 政策 (policy). A large population of about 1.3397 billion provides two main industrial advantages: an abundant labor supply and a large domestic consumer market, which correspond to b and c respectively. Arranged in answer order, the first letter is b. Final answer: b

The left figure shows a coastline with land on the left and ocean on the right, where sea-surface isotherms of 25°C offshore and 21°C nearshore indicate colder water adjacent to the coast, characteristic of a cold current or coastal upwelling; the right figure marks 甲 off western North America, 乙 off eastern Australia, 丙 off eastern Asia, and 丁 off western South America. Cold currents along eastern ocean boundaries include the California Current at 甲 and the Peru (Humboldt) Current at 丁, but the pronounced coastal upwelling and the west-coast continental margin shown in the left figure best match the Peru Current region. Final answer: 丁

The map includes a north arrow pointing upward, a 1040 m peak, and a river cutting through a valley in the southeastern part of the area. On a contour map, a river flows from higher elevation to lower elevation, and valley contour lines bend upstream, forming a V-shape whose point indicates the upstream direction. The contour V along the river points toward the northeast, where the 1040 m peak and higher ground are located, while the land slopes downward toward the southwest, so the river must flow from northeast to southwest. Final answer: from northeast to southwest.

The graph plots salt content (g/L) of Qinghai Lake against time over the past 12,000 years, and the lowest point occurs at roughly 3,000–4,000 years ago, when the salt content drops close to 0 g/L. In a closed-basin lake, salt content is controlled by the balance between freshwater input (mainly precipitation and runoff) and water loss through evaporation: lower salt content means more dilution, higher lake level, and a positive water budget. Therefore, the period with the lowest salt content likely corresponded to a relatively humid climate with greater precipitation, reduced evaporation, and higher lake water level compared with other stages. Final answer: The climate was probably humid/wetter, with more precipitation and less evaporation, causing a higher lake level.

The figure is a triangular coordinate graph with three axes: a (labor) on the left side, b (raw materials) along the bottom, and c (technology) on the right side. In this type of plot, the percentage for each factor increases toward the vertex opposite its axis, so the bottom-left vertex represents 100% labor (a). Among the four plotted points, 甲 is located in the lower-left region closest to the a = 100% vertex, meaning it has the highest labor share; 乙 lies near the technology vertex, while 丙 and 丁 lie near the raw-materials/technology top. Because an industry with the greatest dependence on labor is most vulnerable when labor becomes scarce, the labor-intensive type is most likely to face a labor shortage. Final answer: Jia (甲).

On the map, the Xiangjiang River flows through the Zhuzhou area, and both M and N lie along the river; M is located on a river bend just south of Zhuzhou and near the railway, while N is farther upstream on a relatively straight reach. In river geomorphology, flow around a bend is thrown toward the outer (concave) bank by centrifugal force, causing erosion and deeper water there, whereas the inner (convex) bank receives deposition and becomes shallower. M sits on the outer, eroded bank of the bend, so it has deeper water suitable for berthing, while N is on a depositional or straight section with less favorable depth. M is also closer to the urban area and transport links, giving it better hinterland and flatter land for port facilities. Therefore the most suitable place is M. Final answer: M

The figure shows that in 2010 the province’s natural population growth rate was 0.23 %, which is clearly below the national natural growth rate of about 0.5 %. Since natural growth rate = birth rate − death rate, a natural growth rate far lower than the national average implies that, for a comparable birth rate, the province’s death rate must be relatively high. Final answer: the death rate is at a relatively high level (higher than the national average).

The figure shows sugarcane planting area (left, 10,000 mu) and sugar output (right, 10,000 tons) for Guangxi, Yunnan and Guangdong from 1994/95 to 2010/11; the bar of intermediate height, representing Yunnan, rises over the period and in 2010/11 exceeds the smallest/declining bar, representing Guangdong, indicating Yunnan has expanded its sugarcane base while Guangdong’s has shrunk. Because Yunnan is less economically developed than Guangdong, its land rent and labor costs are lower, giving it a cost advantage for the land- and labor-intensive sugar industry. Final answer: lower land rent and cheaper labor (abundant, low-cost land and labor).

The schematic shows a river valley in North China, with a steep, sharp peak labeled Jia rising beside the river and lower terrain nearby, indicating a landscape that has been uplifted and then dissected by running water. Such a peak forms when tectonic forces raise a block of crust above the surrounding land and the river then cuts downward, eroding the adjacent valleys and steepening the slopes; the river at the foot of Jia is the clear erosive agent. Because the drawing does not indicate rock type, the exact lithology is uncertain, but the visible relief and river point to uplift followed by strong fluvial erosion as the main geological reason. Final answer: Jia peak was formed by tectonic uplift of the crust followed by river erosion that carved the surrounding valley and left the steep peak.

The figure shows a circle representing Earth, with the vertical y-axis as Earth’s axis and the straight line L as the terminator (morning-evening line) making an angle θ with the axis. A noon shadow in Jakarta (6°S) pointing north means the Sun is south of Jakarta, so the Sun’s declination is in the southern hemisphere and the day hemisphere lies on the side of L toward the south. By definition, the morning half of the terminator is the sunrise line, where the Sun is on the horizon and local solar time is 6:00, while the opposite half is the sunset line at 18:00. Therefore, regardless of the exact value of θ, sunrise occurs at 6:00 local solar time. Final answer: 6:00.

The figure is a topographic map near 30°N, showing contour lines, a river with a waterfall, peaks, and settlements; tea cultivation requires a warm, humid subtropical climate, acidic soil, and a gently sloping, well-drained hillside, while steep ridges, cold peaks, and waterlogged valley bottoms are unsuitable. The place that best meets these conditions is therefore the area where the contour lines are widely spaced on a moderate lower slope, indicating a gentle gradient and good drainage. Final answer: the gentle, well-drained hillside on the lower mountain slope (the point/area with widely spaced contours at moderate elevation).

In the figure, arc a is the Arctic Circle, arc b is the terminator, and the crescent-shaped area between a and b is in the night hemisphere; as this night crescent shrinks, the terminator is moving northward toward the Arctic Circle, which means the Sun’s declination is increasing from its negative winter value toward 0°. For Guangzhou in the Northern Hemisphere, sunrise azimuth A satisfies cos A = sin δ / cos φ, so while δ < 0 the Sun rises south of east. Therefore, as the night band continues to shrink, the Sun in Guangzhou rises from the southeast. Final answer: from the southeast.

The diagram plots dissolved oxygen (DO) and biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) along river sections M through Q, with the vertical axis representing concentration. DO starts high at section M, decreases downstream as BOD increases, reaches its minimum value at section O, and then rises again toward Q; conversely, BOD rises from M, peaks near O, and then declines. Fish survival depends on adequate dissolved oxygen, and low DO causes hypoxia or death; the section with the lowest DO is the most dangerous. Since the DO curve reaches its minimum at section O, this is where oxygen depletion is most severe. Final answer: O

The map shows Ankara located on the inland Anatolian plateau and Beirut on the eastern Mediterranean coast, while the temperature and precipitation charts for both places show a clear winter precipitation maximum and a summer minimum, with hot summers and mild to cool winters. This seasonal pattern is the Mediterranean winter-rain feature, which results from the alternation of winter westerly winds and summer subtropical high pressure as the global pressure and wind belts shift seasonally. Because both the coastal station Beirut and the inland station Ankara exhibit the same winter-rain occurrence, the feature is controlled by atmospheric circulation rather than by how far a place is from the sea. Final answer: distance from the sea (sea-land position)

The map titled “Zoning Map of Natural Disasters in China” shows four main natural disaster zones, with the largest zones (I and II) covering eastern and northern China, corresponding to major flood and drought prone regions. In China’s monsoon climate, uneven spatial and temporal distribution of precipitation makes both drought and flood the most widespread and impactful natural disasters. Since the question asks for “another” disaster with the greatest impact, it refers to the counterpart of whichever major disaster was previously mentioned; in the standard Chinese geography pairing of the two most serious disasters, the other one is drought. Final answer: drought

The forecast map for 29 July 2013 shades the high-temperature regions (35 °C, 37 °C, 40 °C) mainly over the middle-lower Yangtze region, South China, and part of Xinjiang, while Changchun in the northeast is unshaded, indicating no forecast high temperature. The incorrect statement attributes Changchun’s lack of high temperature to the influence of cold air (a cold air mass/front/rainy cool weather). This is not supported by the map, which shows no cold-air system over Changchun; the absence of heat simply reflects that Changchun lies outside the day’s high-temperature zone. Final answer: cold air (cold air mass / cold front / rainy cool weather).

The map shows a watershed bounded by a dash-dot line, with dashed isochrones numbered 1 (nearest the outlet on the right) through 7 (farthest from the outlet). Adjacent isochrones represent equal increments of travel time to the outlet, so the distance between two adjacent isochrones is inversely related to flow velocity and thus to slope: a smaller spacing means slower flow and flatter terrain. Visually, the gap between the isochrone labeled 5 and the one labeled 6 is the smallest of the adjacent pairs, indicating the lowest average slope. Final answer: between 5 and 6.

The figure shows two schematic location maps, each with a horizontal line marked 40°; place N lies just north of the 40° line and has ocean on its west side. Prevailing westerlies blow from west to east in the mid-latitudes, and on a west coast this onshore flow produces a marine west-coast climate that is under westerly influence year-round, typically between about 40° and 60° latitude. Since N is at about 40° on a western oceanic margin and is affected by westerlies throughout the year, it matches the marine west-coast climate zone; among common representative cities, London is the classic example. Final answer: London.

In the map, place 4 lies on the dashed front line extending southwestward from the deep low-pressure center (isobars 1000–1015 hPa) over the northwest Pacific, which marks the cold front of a Northern Hemisphere extratropical cyclone; at a cold front, advancing cold air wedges under warm moist air, forcing rapid uplift that produces cloud and precipitation, while the closely spaced isobars indicate a strong pressure gradient and thus strong winds, and the October date means temperatures fall, so place 4 is experiencing rainy, windy, and cooler weather. Final answer: 阴雨、大风、降温.

The diagram shows a circular agricultural system in which corn is grown, the corn stalks are used to feed cattle, the cow dung is fermented to produce biogas, and the biogas residue is returned to the corn fields as fertilizer. This model therefore requires both extensive corn cultivation and a developed cattle-raising industry. Jilin Province lies in China’s Northeast Plain, which is the country’s main “golden corn belt” and has abundant corn stalks and a strong livestock base, so the model is most suitable for promotion there. Final answer: 吉林省.

The map shows part of western Europe bounded by the 0° and 10°E meridians and the 50°N parallel, with a dashed line representing the local January 0°C isotherm; point Jia lies on that dashed line, and at that location the isotherm runs roughly parallel to the meridians, following the north-south orientation of the major river valley visible on the map. Therefore the approximate trend of the January 0°C isotherm at Jia is north-south. Final answer: north-south.

The map is marked with longitude lines at 128°, 128.5°, and 129°E and latitude lines at 43°, 43.5°, and 44°N. The point where the tributary joins the main stream is located near the 128.5°E meridian, while place Jia lies close to the 129°E meridian on the southeastern part of the map. The longitude difference is therefore approximately 129° − 128.5° = 0.5°. Final answer: about 0.5°.

The diagram shows a mountain with the thick line representing the snow line, and the letter “S” is placed at the lower right, indicating the right-hand slope faces south. The snow line is lower on this south-facing slope than on the left-hand slope. Because the snow line is lower on the cooler, poleward-facing slope, a south-facing slope with the lower snow line means the mountain’s poleward side is to the south, which occurs in the Southern Hemisphere. Final answer: Southern Hemisphere.

The image shows a cold front, labeled L1, moving southeast toward point N, which is currently located in the warm sector ahead of the front, and the cold-wave orange alert indicates that strong cold air is pushing south so the front will affect N during the next two days. As the cold front approaches and passes N, warm moist air is forced upward, producing cloud cover and precipitation that reduce the daily temperature range by weakening daytime heating and nighttime cooling. After the front has passed, N will come under the control of a cold high-pressure system with cold, dry, and clearing conditions, which increases radiative cooling at night and solar warming during the day, thereby enlarging the daily temperature range. The figure is a parallelogram with a base of 12 yd and a dashed right triangle on its left side; the triangle has a horizontal leg of 4 yd, a right angle at the bottom left, and a 35° angle at the top between the vertical dashed leg and the slanted side of the parallelogram, which serves as the hypotenuse. The arrows show that \(BF \parallel CE\) and \(FD \parallel AC\), with \(B\) on \(AC\) and \(F\) on \(AE\), so \(\triangle ABF \sim \triangle ACE\) by AA similarity. The image shows triangle JKM with side JK = 8.5 ft, side KM = 5 ft, and altitude KL = 4 ft drawn from K perpendicular to base JM at point L. In the figure, \(MNPQ\) is a parallelogram with diagonal \(MP\); point \(R\) lies on \(MN\) with \(MR=\frac14MN\), and the matching tick marks on \(QT\) and \(TP\) show \(T\) is the midpoint of \(QP\); \(S\) is where \(RT\) meets \(MP\). Place \(M\) at the origin, let \(\vec{MN}=\mathbf{a}\) and \(\vec{MQ}=\mathbf{b}\). Then \(P=M+\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}\), \(R=M+\frac14\mathbf{a}\), and \(T=M+\mathbf{b}+\frac12\mathbf{a}\). A point on \(MP\) has the form \(M+t(\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b})\), and a point on \(RT\) has the form \(M+\frac14\mathbf{a}+\lambda\left(\mathbf{b}+\frac14\mathbf{a}\right)\). Equating the two descriptions of \(S\) gives \(t=\lambda\) from the \(\mathbf{b}\)-coefficient and \(t=\frac14+\frac14\lambda\) from the \(\mathbf{a}\)-coefficient, so \(t=\frac14+\frac14t\), hence \(t=\frac13\). In the image, quadrilateral ABCD is similar to quadrilateral EFGH, with the shown sides AB = x+1, CD = x-1, EF = 8, and HG = 5; the corresponding angle marks and vertex order indicate that AB corresponds to EF and CD corresponds to GH. Subtracting 5x and adding 8 gives 13 = 3x, hence x = 13/3. Therefore AB = x+1 = 13/3 + 3/3 = 16/3. Final answer: 16/3.

The diagram shows circle \(K\) with center \(K\), chord \(MN\), and a line through \(K\) and point \(J\) on the circle meeting chord \(MN\) at \(P\); since \(LP\) is drawn perpendicular to \(MN\) and \(L\) lies on that same line through \(K\), the diameter \(JL\) is perpendicular to \(MN\), so \(P\) is the midpoint of \(MN\) and \(PN=\frac{16}{2}=8\). The image shows a straight 1×1×n bar of n ordinary dice glued face-to-face, so the two faces glued on each interior die are opposite faces. On an ordinary die opposite faces sum to 7, and only faces with equal numbers are glued. Let the n−1 interface values be x_1,…,x_{n-1}. Because the glued faces on each interior die are opposite, the interface values must alternate, giving x_1+x_{n-1}=7 when n is odd and x_1=x_{n-1}=a when n is even. The sum of points on all non-glued faces equals the total 21n minus twice the sum of the interface values, which simplifies to 14n+14-(x_1+x_{n-1}). If n is odd this is 14n+7, and 14n+7=2012 gives n=143.214…, not an integer. If n is even this is 14n+14-2a with 1≤a≤6, so 2012=14n+14-2a, i.e. a=7(n+1)-1006; requiring 1≤a≤6 forces 7(n+1)=1008, hence n=143, which is odd, contradicting the assumption that n is even. Therefore no integer number of dice can give a total of 2012. Final answer: No such number of dice exists.

The image shows a clock face viewed from above with the minute hand pointing in the north-east direction, roughly between the 1 and 2 o’clock marks. A clock’s minute hand moves only clockwise at 360° per 60 minutes, which is 6° per minute. North-east is 45° clockwise from north, and north-west is 315° clockwise from north, so the clockwise angular distance from north-east to north-west is 315° − 45° = 270°. Therefore the time required is 270° ÷ 6°/min = 45 minutes. Final answer: 45 minutes.

The image shows the cryptarithm CAN + GUR = UUU, where each different letter stands for a different decimal digit. The folded strip is 3 cm wide and lies inside a 27 cm by 9 cm rectangle. The square has side length \(2\), so its area is \(4\). The two semicircles have diameters \(AB\) and \(AD\), so each has radius \(1\) and area \(\frac{\pi}{2}\). They intersect at \(A\) and at the center \(O\) of the square. The shaded region consists of the lens-shaped intersection of the two semicircles near \(A\) plus the corner region near \(C\) outside both semicircles. The lens is made of two \(90^\circ\) circular segments: each segment has area \(\frac{\pi}{4}-\frac12\), so the lens area is \(2\left(\frac{\pi}{4}-\frac12\right)=\frac{\pi}{2}-1\). The union of the two semicircles has area \(\frac{\pi}{2}+\frac{\pi}{2}-\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-1\right)=\frac{\pi}{2}+1\). Hence the shaded area is \((\text{square area}-\text{union area})+\text{lens area} = \left(4-\left(\frac{\pi}{2}+1\right)\right)+\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-1\right)=2\). Final answer: 2.

The image shows a regular hexagon with center \(O\) and three alternating vertices marked; these three vertices are folded so that they meet at \(O\). For any regular hexagon, folding a vertex to the center produces a crease that is the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining that vertex to the center, and that bisector is the short diagonal connecting the two vertices adjacent to the folded vertex. Since the marked vertices are every other vertex, their adjacent unmarked vertices are also every other vertex, so the three creases are the three sides of the equilateral triangle formed by the unmarked vertices. The three corner triangles fold inside this triangle, so the boundary of the folded paper coincides with that equilateral triangle. Final answer: an equilateral triangle.

The picture shows three three-digit summands—one with all digits square, one with two squares and a circle, and one with a square followed by two triangles—adding to 2003; since two three-digit numbers can sum to at most 999+999=1998, the row □△△ must be a third summand. Letting the square be s, the circle be c, and the triangle be t, the addition gives 111s + (110s + c) + (100s + 11t) = 2003, so 321s + c + 11t = 2003. Because 321·6 = 1926 and 321·7 = 2247 > 2003, s must be 6; then c + 11t = 77. With c ≤ 9, t must be 7 and c = 0, so s + c = 6 + 0 = 6. Final answer: 6

The top-view drawing shows a circular park containing a cylinder at the upper left, a cone at the right, and a hemisphere at the lower left; the curved arrow shows Betty starts at the marked point by the cylinder and walks clockwise around the park. From the left-side starting viewpoint the hemisphere is on the left and the cylinder is in front of the cone, matching picture 1.
